The G-buffer boxes: instances whose records differ, those condensing, those touched by a live front (the circle the front swept, plus its width and push, intersected with its scope box), pictures and 3D elements the lens may touch (only their intersection with the lens's reach), 3D elements under a burst and 3D elements whose mesh fingerprint changed (a 3D element's instance is compared by its meshes' fingerprint, not their number on the page, so one that comes or goes draws again only where it is or was, never the frame whole, and the others, renumbered, not at all: tests/dirty_parts.rs ); each instance's rect grown by the SDF range and the push; and where a picture given since the last frame ( Renderer::set_picture : one made as it comes into view) is drawn, with the cells that read it, so a picture that arrives is not a frame drawn whole ( tests/dirty_parts.rs : the next frame is the frame of a renderer that had it from the start, byte for byte, drawn in its box). The final box: the G-buffer box grown by the material's read range ( dirty::reach : each material by its own parameters, plus picture mark cells), plus the areas fronts act on, the lens (3.5 radii around both old and new pointer), bursts, the wipe line's rect and changed instances of the annotation layer. Instances are matched in order, not by place: the common start and end of the two lists, and between them runs of 4 equal instances found again further on, so a drawing whose strokes change in number leaves what is drawn after it matched; each run that did not match, in either list, is a box for each of its instances (gathered by merge : content scrolled into view at the bottom and a cell that changed what it draws at the top are not one box across the window between them), and a run changed in place (as many instances in both) a box for each instance, before and after, so marks that move all over the window (drifting motes, a turning body's glyphs) are each where they are; one whose clip alone changed (a clipping box, such as a cached element, whose edge crossed the viewport's) is the strips between the two clips' edges, grown by the pad. Each box ends at its instance's clip, grown by the pad (what is scrolled out of a viewport costs nothing). They are matched only between the same cuts of the list (the modal layer, each plate), and when the cuts differ, in place. A pixel outside every box is covered by the same instances in the same order, so it is the same. Several boxes : over 64, boxes are first gathered by where their centres fall on an 8 × 8 grid over them all; then merged where they overlap, then two at a time (the pair whose union adds least) down to dirty::MAX_SHADE_BOXES (32) for the final frame, grown from what changed as it is, and from those down to dirty::MAX_BOXES (8) for the G-buffer, which draws every instance again in each box (the final boxes are one scissored triangle each). Each stage is drawn once per box (boxes may overlap: a pixel drawn twice is drawn the same), the G-buffer's boxes in one render pass for each image, each box scissored, cleared and drawn in turn (a tile-based GPU loads and stores the whole image for every pass it opens), unless the frame needs passes of its own (a morph's tiles, an opacity group, a plate that adds this frame's ink), which open a pair of passes per box ( Cost::passes counts them). dirty::parts gives them; dirty::region and the readout their union. Acceptance: tests/dirty_parts.rs (a drawing that gains strokes redraws only its own cell, two cells far apart are two boxes under a quarter of the window, seven frames of cells changing under three materials, drawn in their boxes, are byte for byte the frames drawn whole, and 16 motes drifting over a window-wide drawing are shaded under 30 % of the window in plain, byte for byte as drawn whole). Scrolling moves the last frame : when one scroll container's offset moves by whole device pixels (or, with its trace showing, stays) and the ground is not in transition, the renderer copies the G-buffer and the kept frame inside the viewport by the offset ( dirty::Move , Renderer::carry : copies into a second set of images, then the views swap) and the boxes are taken against the last frame moved: the band scrolled into view, the strips along the viewport's edges that the material reads across (its reach, beyond the band), the scroll bar and what changed. Instances carried with the content are compared at their moved place; what was clipped at the viewport's edge keeps that edge. What is not the content's but lies over the viewport is drawn again where it is and where the copy took it, but for a plain shape whose edges (radius and border with them) and clip are all past the viewport by the pad, or past the window: a page's ground drawn as a shape behind its scroll area ( fill(Paint::GROUND) , the components pages) is one colour over the whole viewport, so it moves as the ground does (it was shaded again over the whole viewport, about 85 % of the window each frame of a slow scroll of /components/; tests/scroll_move.rs ). The field map is stirred by an element's motion within the content it scrolls with, so scrolling past it is not a change. Renderer::cost counts what a frame shades (material and G-buffer pixels), the pixels moved and the bytes uploaded. With the trace showing ( §1.8.3 , past Scroll::calm_speed ) the frame is moved too, when the trace points the same way in both frames and no material in use is glitchr (its rows slip on their own clock) or one from source. The trace changes from frame to frame only near the ink it trails: after the move, a pass over the viewport ( fs_trace , Cost::trace ) shades again every pixel the trace can reach in this frame or the last ( Move::trace , the stronger of the two: from where the material reads, any ink within as far round the trace's samples as they spread, along its longest reach, found by the nearness at probes as far apart as it reads: 12 px of nearness less that reach, every 4 px at the nearest) and keeps the moved pixel elsewhere; the boxes are drawn after it, and the marks over the viewport with them. The strips along the viewport's edges grow by the trace's length (what it read there has moved out of sight, or in). Dottr and charr hold the rows to their lattice while the trace shows ( latch ): the frame shows the content at its offset rounded to the pitch, so it moves by how far that rounding stepped ( Move::frame , maybe 0) while the G-buffer moves with the content. In the frame the hold comes on or goes off in (the trace passing the strength that holds the rows), one frame shows the content held and the other at its offset, and the frame moves by the difference. The frame moves as the viewport's ground does (held to its lattice, or with the content when it holds no rows): the page's material, or the override of an opaque shape that lies under the whole viewport in both frames (the components pages draw in plain over the dotted look, so their ground holds no rows; their plain content was shaded again over the whole viewport every frame as another lattice); what lies in the viewport in another material (another lattice, or none: a row in charr or plain on a dottr page) is shaded again where it is and where the frame took it, as far as its nearness reaches ( scroll_move 's third value; the components pages, with plain chrome round specimens in their own materials, moved only one frame in two before). This needs the scroll area alone in its viewport (a scroll area inside it that does not scroll itself, such as a strip of chips in a card, is content it carries, shaded again where it was and where it is; it had drawn every such frame whole), a step of whole device px and no held offset half way between two rows, and the boxes grow by the largest pitch. With a reduced pass for what is loose the frame is drawn whole. With one for the stages alone ( §1.35 ) the frame moves and the trace is shaded at full resolution as without it; the reduced grid is fixed to the content ( §1.35 ), so a stage the frame carried stands, and while the trace shows every stage in the viewport is shaded again where it is (its box among the shade boxes, in the reduced pass and the filter up) (a list with stages at 0.75 under plain, dottr and charr, scrolled fast down and up, is byte for byte the frame drawn whole). Acceptance: tests/scroll_move.rs (a slow scroll down and back up under four materials at two scales is byte for byte the frame drawn whole at every step, with the material shading under half of a small window; a fast scroll down, up and settling under six materials at two scales is byte for byte the frame drawn whole, moved with its trace in at least 12 of 40 frames; under glitchr it is drawn whole). The whole screen: the look changed (theme, material, parameters…), the window changed, a commit is showing, particles are flying, the low-resolution pass is being drawn, or a material that reads the material clock ( dottr , glitchr ) is in use and the clock moved. The material clock now follows only the field (fronts, commits, condensing, morphs, flows, recomposition, flings and overscroll, something loose under a time-varying material); hover bursts, sliding corner marks and annotations drawing in no longer advance it, since otherwise one hover would set dottr's ground drifting across the whole window and force a full redraw. Why a frame cost what it did : the renderer leaves in Perf::path how the last frame was drawn ( perf::FramePath ), and the full overlay shows it as one line ( FramePath::line ): move yes , or move no with the first reason the frame did not move the last one or was drawn whole ( global broken down as commit, morph, loose under a reduced pass, a stage rescaled, an opacity group, plates ageing or emptied, own colours; the look, the size, the materials or the dottr ground clock changing; soft scrolling; the trace with a reduced pass; a refusal of scroll_move , dirty::Parts::refused : the viewport changed, a jump past it, the trace turned, glitchr or a material from source, the latch switching, not alone, half a row); spec yes with the material, or no with why (an override, a material from source, still counting, off); the share of the frame shaded at full resolution (the shade boxes), with the three reasons whose boxes cover the most of it ( FramePath::shade_why , each a share of the window summed before the boxes merge, so they may overlap: what changed, the band a move scrolled in, the scroll areas, the lens, the field map, the marks, a lattice other than the frame's, a picture given, a plate's view, a stage moved or rescaled); the soft, stage and reduced scales; and, when the view was laid out since the frame before, how many times and where the first was asked for ( layout 2 (src/ui.rs:2081) : the Ui::relayout call, or the call that left it for the frame when input is coalesced; FramePath::layouts , layout_from ). A scroll lays nothing out. tests/scroll_move.rs checks it against what the renderer counted. Hashing : the runtime's own maps and fingerprints (node keys, instance and glyph ids, signatures) use fasthash::FastHasher , a folded-multiply word hash (as foldhash and ahash mix), not the standard library's SipHash, which cost about 0.4 ms a frame in wasm on the M1 when the components page laid out; none of those keys is chosen by an attacker. A paint that follows no new view (a scroll step) allocates little: the lists a text element's glyphs go through are kept between paints ( TextScratch ), the layout cache is looked up by the text's hash with the text kept in the entry ( Text::layout ), the field map is compared with the window's grid before one is built ( FieldMap::fit ), and a recording text that is the same text only takes its new place and glyphs ( Ui::recompose_jobs , one index of the scene for all of them). On the /components/ index a scroll step went from about 2,240 allocations (1.06 MB) to 1,480 (0.49 MB). What pointer movement costs : moving the pointer neither lays out nor shapes text. Parallax uses El::shift(dx, dy) (the whole subtree moves after layout, outside taffy's styles); the lens is counted in the boxes only where it can reach: beyond dirty::LENS_REACH (2.2) radii from the pointer its bell is below 0.01, picture pitch and dot ground dots don't change, and only on pictures, 3D elements and under dottr (other materials' grounds don't read the lens); picture marks' read range is added only when a picture changed; the annotation layer is compared as a set (those that appeared and disappeared), so one more character in a label doesn't make everything after it count as changed. Ui::dirty_inputs gives, without a GPU, the inputs the renderer would compare. Acceptance: tests/pointer_moves.rs : on every website page, of 200 pointer moves, those where what is hovered (a control, a 3D instance, the element the annotation looks at) didn't change do no layout and no shaping (only annotation labels that write coordinates following the pointer may shape), and a move starting from rest redraws a box that is not the whole screen and at most 60% of the window (the lens on a dot ground, a picture or 3D alone covers a third); the annotation crosshair and rulers follow the pointer across the whole scope and don't fit in one box, so such pages aren't measured for area. Acceptance : check item 15: on the button page, hover, press (with a front and the count recomposing) and move away, 48 frames per material; the picture page and the 3D page (the lens on a picture and a mesh) in several materials; the floating box dragged, thrown and settling into a corner, 90 frames per material, with plain and dottr again at 2× scale; every frame drawn by boxes is byte-identical to the full frame, with a control: most frames' boxes are less than half the window. The dirty section of bench ( §9 ).

Language is data. Every string a person reads comes from a message catalog: one plain text file per language ( assets/i18n/zh-Hans.txt , assets/i18n/en.txt , assets/i18n/ar.txt ), one key = text per line; {name} is a named argument (numbers written the language's way, with digit grouping), {{ is a brace; a line starting with two spaces continues the previous entry (a newline); key.one , key.other … are plural forms, chosen by the argument n (or the first number) with CLDR's cardinal rules ( intl_pluralrules ); Chinese needs only other , English one and other , Arabic all six ( Locale::categories asks the rules which). Fluent is not used: fluent-bundle brings intl-memoizer , fluent-syntax and a type system, and this needs only key → text, arguments and plurals, so the parser is 60 lines of our own. Catalogs are compiled in with include_str! , so the web version has them too. Interface ( src/i18n.rs ): Locale ( ZhHans , En , and Other(Tag) for any other BCP 47 tag, with Locale::AR shipped; tag , from_tag , name , direction , fallback , plural , number , date ); locale.tr(key) , locale.tr_args(key, args) , t!(locale, "key", n = 3, name = "…") ; try_tr returns a Result , a missing key being I18nError::MissingKey , which names the key, the chain of languages searched (zh-Hans → en) and which line to add to which two files; tr shows ⟨key⟩ when nothing is found and records it ( i18n::misses() , which tests use to list what is missing). The fallback chain: keys missing in any language but English use English. A language that is not built in may give its own name ( locale.name ) and date pattern ( locale.date , else ISO 8601). from_tag accepts any well-formed tag, matching a shipped or installed catalog by tag or by language ( ar-EG → ar ). An application installs its own catalogs with i18n::install , looked up before the framework's. Language lives in the state. An application keeps its Locale in its state, and changing language is an ordinary message (the website's Msg::Locale ); Ui::on_locale(fn(&S) -> Locale) lets the runtime set it as the current language ( i18n::current ) before every view , and components get their own strings (the dialog's "Close", a picture's name without a caption, the accessible names of a number control's side buttons, the 3D view, the ten-thousand-row list's "n rows") with i18n::tr . After a language change the whole page is laid out again; the text layout cache is keyed by the string itself, so nothing stale is used; keyed text recomposes as usual (the pixels of the changed characters fly into the new text, §1.16 ); text without a key is replaced and condenses from loose. The website's top bar has a Language menu (beside theme and material), and the marking at the top right of Body (English only, LANGUAGE EN / ZH ) changes it on press; tools use AMENUI_LOCALE=en and render --locale en . Direction. El::rtl(true) runs a subtree right to left (inherited): taffy's Style::direction , so a row's first child is at the right, start alignment is the right and padding and margins mirror. Bidirectional text in a paragraph is laid out by parley with the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. Not covered : text alignment does not follow rtl (a paragraph's start is decided by parley from the text's own direction); caret movement and selection in a text field have not been specifically verified in RTL text; scroll bars, annotation leaders and the website's side rail are not mirrored; Locale::direction is right to left for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and the other right-to-left languages (or an Arabic, Hebrew, Thaana, Syriac, N'Ko, Adlam or Hanifi script subtag). tests/i18n.rs checks that Arabic and Hebrew paragraphs get a glyph for every character (with a fallback face) and that the caret before the first character is right of the one after the last. Acceptance : unit tests in i18n.rs (parsing, continuation lines, errors for duplicate keys and bad lines, arguments, digit grouping, plurals, dates, the fallback chain and the missing-key error); tests/i18n.rs : every key exists in every language (plural keys have every form the language needs; Body's body.* keys only in the English catalog); the Body landing scene in both languages (text and body states) has no Han character in its tree and no missing keys (that page is English only); a right-to-left row has its first child at the right and starts from the right.

Data ( src/post.rs , serde, in a preset's post , and therefore in look:v3: recipes; old presets without the field have everything off): PostSpec { bloom, chroma, scanlines, grain, vignette, curvature, dither, palette } , each a number with a default, all off by default: Bloom { strength 0, threshold 0.7, radius 8 } , Chroma { offset 0 } (logical px; red and blue each offset that much outward from the center), Scanlines { strength 0, period 3 } , Grain { amount 0, size 1 } (fixed grain that doesn't crawl over time: a still page is an unchanging picture), Vignette { strength 0, radius 0.55 } (a fraction of the half diagonal), Curvature { amount 0 } (a point at distance d from the center shows what is at d × (1 + amount × d²) , black outside the frame), Dithr { kind, levels 4, strength 1 } and Palette { kind, colors } . Look::post is its fixed-size form (palettes of at most 16 colours). The order is fixed : bloom → chromatic offset → scanlines → grain → vignette → curvature, then quantization: dither and palette. Curvature is the last thing done to the image, so the shader computes its mapping first and every earlier step reads at the mapped position; dithering uses the screen's own pixels. Quantization happens in sRGB (with an sRGB swap chain the colour is converted there and back). Grain in a region ( El::grain() ): once any element on the page is marked, the grain is drawn only inside the box round everything marked elements draw this frame (each instance within its clip, in device px), so a picture that flows carries it where it is on each frame; the grain itself is the same (its hash, amount and cell), so a window shows the page's grain pixel for pixel. With nothing marked it covers the whole frame. The runtime sets the region in the look it draws with ( Post::region ). tests/grain.rs . Bloom in a region ( El::bloom() ): the same for the bloom. Once any element is marked, the bloom glows only inside the box round what marked elements draw this frame, and only from what is drawn inside it (a tap outside the box adds nothing), so a bright control beside a glowing picture stays its own colour and lights nothing. With nothing marked it covers the whole frame, as before, and the pass is the same pixel for pixel. The region is set each frame from where the marked elements are ( Post::bloom_region ); the finishing pass runs on the kept frame whenever it is shown, so a scroll's or a stage's moved frame takes it like any other. tests/bloom.rs . Dithering ( DithrKind ): bayer2 , bayer4 , bayer8 (recursive Bayer matrices); blue_noise : not a real blue-noise mask (that would need a texture or void-and-cluster at start-up) but the R2 low-discrepancy sequence fract(0.7549 x + 0.5698 y) , as even and textureless; atkinson_like : real error diffusion runs pixel after pixel and doesn't fit one fragment pass, so this is an ordered stand-in: 4×4 Bayer thresholds squeezed into 1/8–7/8, so that, as with Atkinson (which passes on only 3/4 of the error), the darkest and brightest quarters are solid and the pattern sits in the midtones. Without a palette each channel is quantized to levels steps (the threshold minus 0.5, times strength , added in); with a palette it dithers by about one palette step first and then takes the nearest colour (squared distance weighted 0.30, 0.59, 0.11). Palettes ( PaletteKind , data, colours defined by this project): one_bit (near black and paper), moss4 (four moss greens), amber (four steps of amber), cyan_magenta (ink, cyan, magenta, white), cga4 (black, green, red, yellow), originals8 (eight named colours: ink, paper, brick, ochre, moss, slate, plum, sky) and user ( colors , at most 16). Implementation : the renderer already copies the kept frame whole to the target each frame ( §1.19 ). With effects on, that step becomes fs_post (the same full-screen triangle reading the kept frame), so there is no extra pass; with everything off it is the original copy and costs nothing. The kept frame, the dirty boxes and the old picture a commit takes are all from before finishing, so partial redraw and transitions are unaffected; bloom (two rings of twelve samples) and curvature are full-screen, but this pass was a full-screen copy anyway. The legibility rules are unchanged: finishing loosens nothing, and still text stays whole (dither and palette change the colours at glyph edges). Black and white only ( PostSpec::binary ): the palette becomes one_bit and dithering is off; without dithering the shader takes the nearest palette colour, which is a threshold at mid luminance, so no new dither kind is needed. Line widths are rounded to device pixels at the same time ( scribblr and trail lines, at least 1 px). Invert ( PostSpec::invert ): the output is 1 − colour , in sRGB, after everything (after quantization), so the ink on the page, the annotation layer and pictures in transition all invert together; with binary there are still only two colours. Both are switches, off by default. Where they are used : Neo-Dotmatrix uses the amber palette with 4×4 dithering (strength 0.8) and a little bloom; Glitch uses chromatic offset 1.5, scanlines 0.22, grain, vignette and curvature 0.03; Lo-Fi Print uses grain and vignette; the Loose Thread style page has black-and-white-only and invert switches ( §4.4 ). Text to read kept clear ( PostSpec::clear_text , off by default; only Glitch turns it on): on the ink of text to read and 2 device px round it, the chroma offset is 0 and the scanlines are at most 0.08 (the preset's 0.22 elsewhere), so the strokes the eye reads are not split into fringes or darkened. Pictures, shapes, the ground and text not to read ( legible(false) ) keep the whole pass; curvature, vignette and grain apply to text as to the rest. The pass learns where the text is from a mask drawn before it (R8, the size of the frame): each glyph of text to read ( Scene::legible , filled where the frame's holds are) is drawn into it by its signed distance, full within 2 px of the ink and falling linearly to nothing at 4 px, so the fringe starts softly at the edge and does not cut off. A channel is not offset where the pixel or the point it would be read from is under the mask, so the text has no fringe and leaves none beside it. Glitch's large headings lose their fringe too: they are text to read. Without clear_text , or with neither chroma nor scanlines on, nothing is drawn into the mask and the frame is as before. The audit reads a bent frame (curvature) where the bend drew each pixel back to where layout put it ( audit::unbend , nearest), so text near the corners is measured against its own ink boxes and not the ground the bend moved in under them; the softening of the bend stays in what is measured. With no curvature the frame is measured as drawn, byte for byte. What the bend carries off the frame is not read back in: text to read whose ink the bend draws past the window's edge is Clipped ( audit::bent_off ; P0 for a glyph wholly off the frame, P1 for ink past the edge by more than half a pixel), unless layout has clipped it already. Acceptance : unit tests in post.rs (Bayer thresholds are a permutation, 2×2 is the classic 0 2 / 3 1, Atkinson-style thresholds lie in 1/8–7/8, palettes, JSON round trips, all off by default); preset.rs (recipes round-trip post.dithr.levels ; old presets without the field read as all off); check item 17 (formerly item 19): at strength 0 byte-identical to off; each effect turned on alone changes the picture, and the same frame drawn twice is byte-identical; after two-level dithering every channel is only 0 or 255; for every fixed palette and one user palette under four dithers, every pixel is a palette colour (±1/255; control: most pixels are not when off); with finishing on, partial and full redraw are byte-identical. Samples samples <dir> looks .

src/motes.rs (no GPU). Both are data on elements; the runtime moves them and draws them as shape instances (small squares in ink, Response::Ignore , above the page and below the annotation layer): Shedding ( El::shed(Shed { rate, life_ms, gravity, drift, size }) , by default rate 0 , 900 ms, 240 px/s², 30 px/s, 2.5 px): when the element's rect center moves d px between two tick s, rate × d / 100 marks are released from its edges (between the old and new positions; fractions accumulate), each with its own sideways drift, falling by gravity and fading out within life_ms . Nothing is released while the element is still, and with no marks there is no cost ( Ui::motes_moving is false, no frames wanted). With Shed.clear above 0 (default 0, off) marks avoid text: none are released within clear of any line of text ( line_boxes ), and a mark falling toward a line fades by distance within clear and is gone a pixel before touching it; in tests/motes.rs the dragged sign uses clear 10 (measuring every mark's distance to every line, frame by frame). Flow fields ( El::flow_field(FlowField { scale, speed, density, size, alpha }) , by default 140 px, 0 px/s, 6 per ten thousand square px, 2 px, 0.4): the element's box holds density × area / 10000 marks (positioned by hash, so the same frames give the same bytes), moving at speed along the direction of a fixed continuous noise field (value noise turned into an angle, two turns), entering from the opposite edge when they leave the box. At speed 0 they don't move and want no frames; the page sets it, so "no frames at rest" holds whenever the page stops it. Acceptance: unit tests in motes.rs (the field is continuous, nothing moves at speed 0, counts); tests/motes.rs (a page with its own text and a draggable sign): a still sign sheds nothing, dragging 185 px sheds at least 4, they fall, all are gone at the end of their life, no frames are wanted afterwards, and none comes closer than clear to a line of text; a flow field with speed has moving marks, and at speed 0 motes_moving is false with 0 frames in two seconds.

El::skeleton() (inherited by the subtree): the subtree is laid out as usual, and when drawn each line of text is a bar as wide as that line measures ( Text::line_boxes ) and SKELETON_BAR (0.56) of the line height tall, with round ends; pictures and 3D elements are blocks; fills and borders fade; it takes no input, and doesn't fade as a whole the way disabled does. Bars and blocks have identities of their own, so when the content arrives the text condenses by the framework's rules and the bars disappear; the layout is the same tree with the same text, so not one box moves by a pixel. The rules are numbers ( widgets::Loading { skeleton_after_ms 300, swap_stagger_ms 40 } ): what doesn't depend on the data is drawn at once; a skeleton appears only when the data is later than skeleton_after_ms (a quick answer never flashes a skeleton; before that the rows are hidden_until_morphed , holding their place and drawing nothing); once the data arrives, row i becomes content at arrival + i × swap_stagger_ms . Loading::show(i, now) says what a row is, next_change gives the next moment of change, and the application's on_wake wants frames only at those moments. The website's skeleton page compares four approaches: a spinner (eight dots lighting in turn, a step every 100 ms), a skeleton, a progress bar (moving to 95% over the expected time) and an optimistic update (rows are there at once, the newly added one faint until confirmed). Acceptance: unit tests in skeleton.rs ; tests/loading.rs : before 300 ms the rows have no instances while the button is drawn; during the skeleton each heading has as many bars as lines, each bar as wide as its line (±1); when the data arrives row 0 is text and row 4 still skeleton; every row's box is equal in skeleton and content; no frames wanted afterwards. Samples craft <dir> loading . The warm-up and the application's own preparation. The first frame is a readable page you can use: what takes long to make comes in over the next frames. Renderer::begin(device, queue, format, w, h) -> Warmup makes at once only what plain needs to draw (the main shader, the ink, nearness, material, annotation and copy pipelines). Warmup::step(budget_ms, text) (or Renderer::warm_step on the renderer it hands over) makes the rest in a fixed order, at least one piece a call and more while the budget lasts: the mark atlas one set at a time ( marks::Atlas::begin , AtlasBuild::step , finish ), the finishing pass, then the reduced-resolution upsample, a scroll move's trace pass ( fs_trace : compiled on the first fast scroll instead, it stalled that frame for seconds), the morph tiles' and the mesh pass's pipelines. Each material pipeline is drawn with once as it is made, into one pixel of a scratch target ( Renderer::prime ): a driver that finishes a pipeline on its first draw does it then, not on the frame that first needs it (on the CPU rasteriser the first frame of the site's dark scheme, the first with its bloom, took 0.9 s against 0.4 s for each later one); Progress { done, total, stage } says how far it is ( Stage::Plain , Pipelines , Ready ). Until the atlas and the finishing pass are made, frames are drawn in the plain look ( render::plain : material plain, no finishing pass, no material overrides). Rule 3 of §0 says a page at rest is plain, so this is the same page arriving early, not a lesser one; on the frame the look is ready, the page arrives at rest and then comes apart a little and condenses ( Ui::condense_all ): over ui::RAMP (120 ms) each element loosens from 0 to its cap, then condenses from there with the preset's own timing. Text to read and controls ( legible ) do not move: their cap here is 0, so they are born condensed, and under every material their ink in the frames after arrival is the same as at rest; only headings, decoration and pictures come apart and condense. The frame the material arrives in is the page at rest, so it differs from the plain frame before it only where the material has a look of its own at rest ( tests/warmup.rs : under 2 % of the pixels for dottr , whose ground has dots; for seven materials, dark and light, over 99 % of the pixels in each legible element's ink box, grown by 2 px, are the same at 0, 60, 120 and 300 ms after arrival as in the plain frame, or as at rest where the material has a look of its own at rest), and no element's looseness changes by more than 0.2 from one frame to the next at 60 Hz. Renderer::new is the same thing done in one go, for offline rendering and tests, with the same bytes; Offscreen::try_warming is an offscreen target that warms up. The hosts call Renderer::warm_frame(ui, WARM_MS) once a frame drawn, and Renderer::warm_idle in idle time ( §1.9 ): it makes pieces until 6 ms are spent, and stops early rather than start a piece whose kind has before taken more than 1.5 × the budget left (a kind not yet timed counts as too long, so after the first piece of a frame it waits for the next). It tells the runtime how far it is ( Ui::warm ; Ui::on_warm(fn(&mut S, Option<Progress>) -> bool) hands it to the state, None once ready); the last step reports done = total with Stage::Ready . An application prepares its own one-off work the same way ( src/warmup.rs ): Ui::prepare(key, job) takes a job that does one small piece on the state per call and returns how much is done (0..1). The runtime calls each job at least once a frame while it runs, then again while the frame's spare time lasts ( Ui::set_prepare_budget , 6 ms by default); a page with jobs running wants frames. Ui::ready(key) reads a job's progress (1 when finished or never asked for) and Ui::readiness() the least ready of the jobs and the renderer. The element being prepared is drawn as its own skeleton ( El::skeleton() ), measured to the size it will have, so it arrives without moving. The rules of how loading looks: never a spinner or a progress bar as the main thing on the page; the first frame is the plain page, readable and usable; progress is shown only as a readout of the annotation layer, READY 0.62 beside LEVEL ( §4.3 ), and only while something is not ready. Acceptance of the warm-up: tests/warmup.rs (before any step the frame equals the plain look's frame byte for byte; after the last step and the condensing it equals a frame of Renderer::new ; at most 32 steps, none over a fixed 3 s on lavapipe; a prepared job runs a piece a frame, its progress only goes forward, and the page rests afterwards).

widgets::card_stack ( Stack { count 5, angle0 42, falloff 0.7, delay_ms 28, spring (k 260, c 24), look, card, paints, outline, outlines } ). By default every card is raised ( paints [RAISED] ), outlined 1 px ( outline ), the top card in the ink and the ones under it in the hairline grey ( outlines [INK, HAIRLINE] : card n takes entry n, the last one repeating; empty, the ink); categories are not told apart by the accents. Flat, the top card's rectangle is the scene's Mesh3d.snap : its edges are on whole device pixels however large the box is drawn (a page that zooms it to fit a narrow window too), so at rest each side's outline is one whole pixel at its grey, not two at half strength. Hovering or pressing a card (a 3D element's Pick ) turns the n-th card beneath it (n from 0) to angle0 × falloff^n degrees, starting after delay_ms × n ms, each with its own spring with velocity hand-off ( §1.8.4 ), about its own bottom-left corner; the cards above stay. A press keeps it fanned, Esc closes it, and the arrow keys change card. The cards are one scene3d (a cube each), so their look follows the material ( StackLook::of ): under plain they are flat cards seen face on (an orthographic camera); under smudgr and the like they have thickness, seen from above at an angle, outlined, in two tones, with visible edges; under dottr , charr and halftonr they are flat cards handed to the mark material; at rest they are drawn as in plain , and they loosen to 1 only while the cards fan and settle (toward 1 within LOOSEN_S = 120 ms while any card's spring moves, back to 0 within TIGHTEN_S = 240 ms after the last one stops, then no frames; a fan held open and still is at 0). The formula caption under the page prints this moment's angle(n) and delay(n) . Acceptance: unit tests in card_stack.rs (the formula, the order of delays, holding, Esc, the look by material); tests/stack.rs (the pointer picks the top card, at 40 ms cards 1 and 2 have started and card 3 hasn't, after stopping each card equals the formula, no frames at rest, closing on leave); tests/card_stack.rs (marked cards' pixels are plain's at rest and from 240 ms after the springs stop; from 120 ms after the fan starts a quarter of their inside differs, under halftonr 15%, whose dots at full ink meet, with some in every window of 3 × 3 cells; at rest in a 520 × 340 box the top card's outline is one pixel at the ink within 2/255 on every side, with no pixel part way to it beside it, at 1x and 2x, dark and light). Samples craft <dir> stack : one row per look.

widgets::dot_chart ( DotChart { knots (7, 0..1), cols 56, rows 16, pitch 9, range (0.42, 0.68), max 120, unit } ). The curve is a Catmull-Rom spline through the control points, sampled once per column as v(c). Dot r of column c (counting up from the axis) covers the band [r, r+1)/rows, and how much of it lies under the curve is its coverage k = clamp(v·rows − r, 0, 1) : diameter pitch × (0.25 + 0.65k) , tone 0.25 + 0.75k , so a column's coverages add up to exactly v·rows and the field of dots is the area under the curve; above the curve are the smallest, faintest dots. The picked range is ink: its dots' tones go up to the ink, with an ink line under the axis; outside it a dot's tone is scaled to go no further than dim ( tone × Paint::DIM.tone ). The accent is only under the hand: the dot under the pointer, and a control point and its tick while it is dragged. While the pointer moves over the chart ( El::on_move ), that column shows a vertical line and its value (in the mono face, which is the pixel face); each control point on the axis is a draggable round handle ( Role::Slider ), dragged up and down to change its value, with the curve and dots recomputed; once focused, Left and Right move the line and Up and Down change the nearest control point. The formula caption prints the expressions for k, diameter and tone and the range's area. Acceptance: unit tests in dot_chart.rs (sums of coverage, the spline passes through its control points, dragging); tests/chart.rs (dot size by coverage, ±0.5 because layout rounds; the line and value when sweeping; dragging a control point raises the curve and enlarges that dot; the line disappears on leave). Samples craft <dir> chart .

The experiments of fields, the Lab and the decode transition were first broken down into primitives from first principles, to see what the foundation lacked: Experiment Comes down to What was missing Lit text (Lumen) Each glyph's tone by its distance to the light No access to each laid-out glyph Contours Scalar field → grid sampling → marching squares → polylines → strokes No fields, and nothing could draw a slanted line (2D instances couldn't turn) Silk Many points advected by a vector field (curl of noise + flow stirred by the pointer) motes::FlowField was special-purpose code with field and drawing welded together Grown Reaction–diffusion masked by an element's true coverage The state couldn't get an element's true outline Mercury Metaball scalar field → contours + dots by value As for contours Text on a path / sphere (Flow, Loupe) Each glyph's translation, rotation, scale and opacity Instances had no transforms of their own Orbits, spring, card stack Points and strokes; springs Only element boxes could be drawn So the foundation changed in five places, with no special cases in the effect pages: Per-instance transforms ( Instance::xf , the eighth vec4): a 2×2 linear transform about the instance's rect center, stored as "minus the identity", so zero means no transform and no existing constructor changed. The vertex shader turns the four corners by it, and exact_i maps pixels back into local box coordinates, so atlas coverage and distance and shapes' analytic distance are computed on the turned outline and materials work as usual. Instance::bounds gives the bounding box after turning, used by partial redraw. Sampling follows the transform too: morph::cover_at first maps the point back into the box through xf ( morph::to_box , like the shader's exact_i ), and cells and ink_bounds use the turned bounding box, so a posed or turned glyph loosens into particles from where it is drawn, and on_outline masks and decode blocks are there as well ( a_posed_glyph_loosens_from_where_it_is_drawn in tests/transform.rs ). Glyph poses ( El::pose(|GlyphAt| Pose) ): asked once per laid-out glyph when the scene is built (index, count, center, content box, the range of all glyph centers, and the pen as laid out: pen , the x of its origin before the glyph's image is put on a quarter pixel, base , its baseline as drawn, and advance , kerning in it; a pose that moves a glyph by target − pen puts its pen at target ), giving a translation, an angle, two scales, multipliers for tone and opacity, and a minimum accent; glyphs with opacity 0 aren't drawn. No layout or shaping: pointer movement only rebuilds the scene. Posed text is culled by where its glyphs go, not by its box: a box outside its clip still draws the glyphs posed into it, and the glyphs posed outside the clip are not made. Drawings ( el::canvas(Drawing) , src/draw.rs ): an element whose content is marks in its own coordinate space ( Mark::Dot , Mark::Line ), scaled to the element's width with the height in proportion. Each mark is a shape instance: a dot is a rounded square and a stroke a turned bar with round ends, so they have true outlines, every material can draw them and fronts can loosen them. Marks change every frame, so they don't condense (their birth time is long past). Pointer handlers on a canvas ( on_move , on_drag , and El::on_point , which combines move, press-drag and leave in one handler, fingers included) report coordinates in the canvas's space. A stroke with a ramp ( Drawing::ramp(a, b, w, paint, mid, far) , Mark::Line 's far and mid ): its colour and opacity go from paint at a to far at b , through mid (a paint and where it is, 0–1 of the way) if given, still one instance (the far and middle paints packed into its uv.zw , their hues and the middle's place into extra.x , all negative; a line without a ramp is the instance it was). The instance's opacity is its strongest stop's and each stop's is a share of it (the start's in extra.y ), so whatever scales an element's opacity later (a fade, a flow's wait, a see-through group) scales every stop: a ramp waiting at opacity 0 draws nothing. The ramp's parameter is the pixel's projection on a→b, clamp(dot(p − a, b − a) / |b − a|², 0, 1) , so each round end is its end's colour, flat. Over a picture (where ink is written as its own colour) the stops' colours are mixed in OKLab, each piece linear with no smoothing at the middle stop, and the opacity, linear along the length, is applied after the mix. Off a picture ink is a theme mix with one accent hue a pixel, so there the paint's numbers (tone, accent, opacity) go in a line and it keeps paint 's hue all the way: a ramp within one hue, or to transparent, comes out as drawn there; one from one hue to another is reported ( ViewProblem::RampHue , a P1 in the audit). 540 ramps are one draw. A drawing's own colours ( Drawing::palette([...]) , sRGB 0–1): a mark's Paint::hue(3 + k) is the drawing's colour k in place of a theme accent, its tone and accent mixing towards it as towards one, so a piece's marks are the same wherever they are drawn (its page, a window onto it, a band) whatever the theme there. The runtime gathers the drawings' colours each frame into one table of at most 32 ( draw::OWN_COLOURS ; the same colour in two drawings counts once, in the order first drawn), renumbers each mark's hue into it (3 + its place) and hands it to the shader with the theme's ( Scene::own ; a colour that changes under the same hue redraws everything). Over a picture, where ink is written as its own colour, they are exact and a ramp between two is mixed in OKLab as between theme hues (a ramp packs its stops' hues in 6 bits each). Off a picture, where ink is one of the theme's three accents a pixel, a mark in one of them is drawn in hue 0 and reported ( ViewProblem::OwnColourOffPicture , a P1 in the audit; what is drawn of a mark, cut by its clip, is what must be on a picture), as a ramp across hues is there; so is a hue past the drawing's palette or the table, and outside a drawing a hue of 3 or more is hue 0. tests/own_colours.rs (W-04's ray in its own three colours over its sky, by hand in OKLab within 2 / 255 under a dark and a light theme and the same pixels under both; off a picture hue 0 and a P1; two drawings sharing a colour count it once). Blades ( Mark::Blade , Drawing::blade ): a rooted stroke that the field map ( §1.29 ) bends, for a field of grass. root , len , width (at the root, 1.5 by default; the tip is half of it, 0.5 px at least), its own lean (0), max_lean (57°), stiff (0.5), paint , lean_paint and an optional head glyph. Its lean is lean + max_lean · clamp(flow.x / drift, −1, 1) with the flow read at the root, so vertical flow never lays it down: its own lean and the flow's add, all of it within ± max_lean (and ±85°); its colour is mix(paint, lean_paint, m) and its head's mix(head.paint, lean_paint, m) , where m ( Blade::mix ) is |lean| / max_lean by default ( lean_from 0, lean_full 0), and with lean_full above lean_from 0 up to lean_from , 1 from lean_full and a smoothstep between (a field that greens only once it really leans: 8° and 20° on the website). The lean is the angle of the tip's tangent from upright. Along the blade, a share s of its length from the root, the tangent is lean · (0.35 + 0.65 · g(s)) ( Blade::tangent ): the root leans 0.35 of the tip. With stiff 0, g(s) = s , one even bend from root to tip; with stiff above 0, g is 0 over the lower 0.6 · stiff of the blade (that part is straight) and then a smoothstep to 1 at the tip. What falls over is the head, not the whole stalk laid flat: the chord's angle is about two thirds of the lean with stiff 0 (38° at 57°, 49° at 72°) and less when it is stiffer (33° and 41° at 0.5). The shape ( Blade::at , Blade::shape , the same in the shader) is walked by arc length in 16 steps, so the length is kept. It is drawn as 10 segments when it is longer than 48 logical px, 6 when longer than 24 and 2 otherwise, their ends spaced evenly in (s + 3 · g(s)) / 4 so the segments are shorter where it bends and no two neighbours are more than 12° apart: strokes with round ends cut along the bisector where two meet, tapering, the first and last pulled in by half their width so the blade runs exactly from root to tip. The head's ink box has its bottom middle on the tip and its up along the tip's tangent; the stem ends there. All of it is worked out in the vertex stage from the map at the root ( blade_seg , blade_head ): while only the map moves, nothing is laid out, painted or built on the CPU, and the instances stay as they are. A blade is never pushed by fronts or the flow (it leans instead) and redraws wherever the map changes under its reach. Inside a turned element ( El::turn ) a blade is not turned with it. Fields ( src/field.rs ): Scalar (any Fn(x, y) -> f32 ), Noise (value noise with time), Bump , Balls (metaballs) and Sum ; Grid (sampled at nodes, read back bilinearly, contours producing polylines with marching squares, saddles decided by the cell average so lines never cross); curl (divergence-free flow); Flow (a vector grid; stir adds velocity, fade returns it to rest); Swarm (points advected by a velocity field); GrayScott (masked reaction–diffusion: u = 1, v = 0 outside the mask, no flux across the outline). The hash and noise of motes were replaced by these, and the old copies deleted. Drawing::dots and Drawing::contours are two ways to draw a field. Two things an element tells the state : El::on_visible(|bool| ..) (entering or leaving view: its box intersects its clip; experiments out of view don't step) and El::on_outline(cols, rows, |Grid| ..) (the subtree's true outline, hidden instances included, as coverage on a grid by morph::cover_at ; sent only when the instances changed). Both are messages the runtime queues after layout or scene building and hands to update together ( Ui::flush ); the state never changes in the middle of drawing. Acceptance: unit tests in field.rs (a circle's contour is closed and on the radius, open at the edges, noise is continuous and deterministic, curl has no divergence, reaction–diffusion grows only inside the mask and deterministically, a stirred flow comes to rest); tests/lab.rs (each experiment runs deterministically in the headless runtime, Grown receives its outline and grows only inside it, lit text has light and dark). Depth and facing: text on a form. A pose also has a depth and a facing: Pose::z (logical px, positive toward the viewer) and Pose::facing (1 facing the viewer, 0 edge on, negative facing away). The defaults, 0 and 1, draw exactly as before. The glyphs of one text element are drawn far to near by z (a stable sort; there is no depth buffer). El::form(FormFx) keeps such text legible, with four numbers: name what range step default back opacity kept by glyphs facing away 0–1 0.05 0 edge glyphs facing less than this fade out; at 60 % of it they are not drawn 0–0.6 0.05 0.25 overlap a glyph whose ink is covered by nearer glyphs more than this is not drawn 0.1–1 0.05 0.35 fog tone of the farthest glyphs (the nearest keep theirs) 0–1 0.05 0.6 overlap is how dense a form may be, and it is measured on the true ink, not guessed from spacing: going from near to far, the turned bounding boxes find the candidates, then morph::cover_at on a 7 × 7 grid over the glyph's ink measures how much of it the nearer drawn glyphs cover; the samples come out of the frame budget ( budget::grant ), and past it the boxes alone decide. El::reveal_by(Reveal::Word | Line | Glyph) says how clips, poses and the window take text away. With Word (or Line ), a word (a line) is drawn whole or not at all: it takes the faintest of its glyphs' opacities, it is left out when any of its ink would be cut by its clip or the window, and on a form it is thinned as one (left out if any of its glyphs is covered past overlap ). Words are Unicode word boundaries with the punctuation after a word belonging to it ( Text::reveal_groups ). Glyph is the default and is what happened before. The amenui::form module wraps a block of text onto a shape seen by a mesh::Camera . Form { shape, spin, camera, cover } : the shape is Shape::Sphere(r) , Shape::Surface(f) (how far the surface is along each direction) or Shape::Mesh ; spin turns it (yaw and pitch, degrees); cover is how much of it the block covers (a fraction of the longitudes and of the latitudes). Form::pose_of(GlyphAt) (or form.pose() for El::pose ) gives each glyph its place, turn and scale on the surface, with z and facing filled in; across and down use the same angular step, so glyphs keep their proportions where the shape faces you. Form::hit(x, y, w, h) casts the pointer's ray and returns FormHit { point, normal, t, uv } , the place on the surface in the block's own terms (analytic for a sphere, Mesh::ray for a mesh, a march and bisection for a surface function), so what the pointer lights follows the form as it turns, and a pointer off the form finds nothing. Hits follow what is drawn. Ui::glyph_at(x, y) -> Option<GlyphHit { key, i, z, local }> answers with the nearest glyph drawn at that point, after poses, turns and thinning ( hit::glyph_under over the last paint's glyphs, Ui::glyphs ); El::on_point gets the same in Point::glyph and Point::z while hovering (during a drag they are None and 0). An element turned with El::turn(radians) is drawn turned about its centre, and so is its subtree; hits go through the same transform ( hit::Affine , hit::contains ), so a turned button is pressed where it is drawn, not in the empty corners of its box. A 3D hit says where it is: MeshHit has point (world), normal , t (along the ray) and uv (the place in the view); Pick is unchanged. A press goes to the nearest element under the pointer that takes a press or a drag: a button or link inside an element that drags (a scene hearing the pointer with on_point ) gets its own press, and the outer element's drag starts on its own area or on something inside it that takes no press. Fingers follow the same rule. The recipe form3d ( docs/recipes/form3d.md ) is a passage on a sphere with edge 0.5, words revealed whole, the words around the pointer's place on the surface lit, and a drag that turns it. Acceptance of depth and forms: tests/form.rs (a passage on a sphere turned a whole way round in twelve steps draws no glyph facing away, no two drawn glyphs cover more of each other's ink than overlap (+0.15 for the grid), depths never fall along the drawing order, the same turn gives the same instances, words come and go whole, a pose with the default depth and facing draws exactly as before, Form::hit finds the glyph drawn under the pointer); tests/pointer.rs (after a quarter turn of the sphere the glyph glyph_at gives at the same point is the one now drawn there; a square turned 30° presses at its drawn corner and not at its box's empty corner; a button inside a pointer scene takes its own press, and the scene still drags from its own area and from text inside it); unit tests in mesh.rs (a ray hits the unit sphere at length 1 with the normal along the point, within 1e-4) and form.rs .

Many small marks (morph cells, shed marks, flow field marks, swarms in experiments, the marks of a drawing) used to have limits of their own (4000, count_max …) and stuttered when there were many. Now they all draw from one frame budget ( src/budget.rs ): budget::grant(want) gives how many this frame may have ( want × scale , and no more than what remains of MAX_MARKS = 24000 this frame); budget::cap() is the most one drawing may draw (beyond it marks are dropped evenly by stride); the runtime starts a frame at each tick ( begin_frame ) and, after each frame, gives its time to feed : 8 consecutive frames over TARGET_MS (14 ms) lower the scale by a fifth (to no less than 0.05), and 60 consecutive frames under half raise it by a tenth (up to 1). Only what can be seen moves: flow field marks move only while their box is in view, and experiments only when on_visible says they are seen. There is one way to draw: they are all shape instances in the same instance buffer (morph cells have their own pass and scale their cell count). The readout (F2) shows how many this frame used, how many were asked for, the limit and the scale. Acceptance: unit tests in budget.rs ; tests/budget.rs (asking for a million marks keeps the instance count and the frame time bounded).

El::decode(Decode { tiers [32, 16, 8, 4], stagger_ms 90, duration_ms 720, seed 7, hold }) ( src/decode.rs is the part that needs no GPU): when an element appears it is covered by blocks that resolve from coarse to fine over a few tiers, finally revealing the real content; when the element leaves the view, the runtime plays the same thing backwards with its last frame's instances. It uses the loosening machinery : blocks are not a grid in a shader; the element's true outline is sampled the way morphs sample ( morph::outline_cells , how particle cells are cut) for coverage on the finest tier's grid, and inked cells are gathered into each tier's coarser cells, so every tier covers all of the ink and none of the box's empty space. Coverage follows the outline, not colour ( morph::cover_at ): a panel filled with the ground colour is an outline too, so a dialog's inside is covered even at the finest tier; only the cells a morph flies use morph::ink_at (visible ink, since ground-coloured cells would fly invisibly). Blocks are ordinary shape instances (true outlines, drawn by every material), and the content is the element's own instances, shown at the right moment. Timing : with T tiers, tier i's blocks each appear at a hashed moment in [i·S, i·S + W] ( S the stagger, W = (D − (T−1)·S) / 2 ); a block disappears when its last child appears; at C = (T−1)·S + W every tier has appeared, the content is drawn beneath the blocks, and the finest blocks each disappear within [C, C + W] . So at every moment in between each inked cell is under some block, and the content is not drawn before C ; at progress 0 and 1 there are no blocks at all (nothing half covered at rest). Colours are the current look's first two accents, chosen by hash. hold: Some(u) stops it at progress u (the documentation page's timeline). Played backwards, the content drawn before C is the instances from before it disappeared, with the element's own Decode spec and inside the clip it was last drawn in (a decoding element taken away alone, its page staying, decodes out within its scroll area or dialog, not over the page). The documentation page ( #decode ): a card held at the timeline's progress; the same plan pulled apart in depth by tier (one plane per tier seen at an angle, squashed to 0.42 height and sheared 0.55, each tier 74 px further down and right, the content as the bottom layer; each plane shows that tier's blocks lit at this moment, with a leader on the right to a label beside it: cell size, when it appears and how many are lit now); a draggable timeline (each tier's span, the content's span, the current position); every number a number control; and "Open dialog" opens a dialog that appears by decoding and plays backwards when closed. Acceptance: unit tests in decode.rs (no blocks at 0 and 1; from the first tier being fully present until the content appears, every finest cell is covered; mean cell size shrinks; deterministic); tests/decode.rs (a dialog opening shows only blocks first, the content appears after C , and there are no blocks at the end; closing plays backwards and leaves nothing at the end). A decode held at a step ( DecodeSpec::hold ) draws that step once and then the page rests: it asks for no more frames until something changes ( tests/frames.rs ).

Where something has moved, a short trail follows it: dragging, throwing and settling the floating box, the bottom sheet rising, the card stack fanning; the decoration it passes loosens a little and drifts a few pixels along the direction of motion, then returns; ground dots ( dottr ) lean that way and grow a little. A second or so after release, the page is identical pixel for pixel to how it was before and wants no more frames. This is part of rule 2 (one way to move: the field), not a new animation. One map ( src/fieldmap.rs , no GPU): one coarse grid over the whole window with spacing cell (16 logical px by default; 1280 × 800 is 82 × 52 nodes, one extra per side), node (i, j) at (i, j) × cell. Each node holds three numbers: energy e (0..1, which the instances that read it take as looseness) and flow u , v (length ≤ 1, times drift in px). Stepping : a fixed step of 1/60 s; tick accumulates elapsed time and steps whenever there is enough (ten small steps and one step of ten are equal node by node, so the render tool stays byte-deterministic). Each step: (1) all three numbers x ← mix(x, 3 × 3 average, bleed) ; at nodes with ink ( creep ), inked neighbours weigh more and empty ones less, and bleed grows, so energy creeps along text and shapes (the ink is the coverage of what reads the map, read again on a new scene only for instances that changed, never for blades or for what lies inside a box with lives of its own, where nothing creeps); (2) e ← max(0, e·exp(−dt/energy_life) − 0.15·dt) , and the flow's length decays the same way by flow_life ; meander turns the flow direction by a slow field (the product of two travelling waves, patches of about 160 px) by at most 40° per second, keeping its length; (3) nodes inside an El::calm box are cleared. The linear term guarantees reaching exactly 0 in bounded time: at most τ ln(1 + e0/(0.15 τ)) , 1.24 s by default; averaging never raises the maximum, so this holds with bleed too. What becomes invisible once quantized to a byte is dropped, so the map returns exactly to 0, moving() is false and no frames are wanted (rule 3). Only nodes that still hold something, and one ring around them, take part in the step. Breath ( breath , breath_s ): above 0, energy has a floor that rises and falls periodically (with phase by position), so the map always moves and always wants frames; 0 by default, only for presets that want it. With reduced motion there is no breath. Putting things in is one action, a stir: energy and flow added within radius R by (1 − (d/R)²)² , written only to nodes in the scope box and not in a calm box. Two sources: an element with El::stirr(Stirr { energy 1, radius None, scope Container(None) }) that moved (its rect center travelled d between two ticks, ignored under 0.5 px; a stir every half cell along that segment, in the direction of d , by min(|d|/24, 1) , the energy also multiplied by the look's stirr , the radius by default stirr_radius plus half the element's short side; the frame the window resizes and the frame the element first appears don't count); and Cmd::Stir { at, v, energy, radius, scope } , where at is a point, an element's center, or a stretch of a path ( StirAt::Path { points, from, to } , with v the amounts along and across the path and the flow following the path's tangent). Reading : the G-buffer stage's own_loose takes w = max(w, fmap_e(this point)) and then the existing k + clamp(w, 0, max(resp.x − k, 0)) , so responses and the legibility cap need nothing new: 0 for Ignore and Nudge , up to 0.15 for legible text, up to 1 for decoration. The vertex stage translates by the flow at the center, flow × drift × scale , only for instances that fronts push (so Response::Ignore keeps an element, a title in a field a gust crosses, exactly where it is; El::calm does too and clears the map over its box); the map is sampled between its nodes, so a scope's edge is soft over one cell on both sides. Pictures and 3D elements are not translated (they loosen in place, so the page ground never shows inside a picture's box as a trail passes, check 19.5). The shading stage: dottr's ground dots add fmap_e to their swell and the lattice leans along the flow by at most half a pitch; glitchr's row slips take fmap_e as looseness on the ground (not on ink). Other materials' grounds hold nothing at rest and add nothing. The CPU model Ui::looseness adds the same bilinear value (reading the quantized bytes) into the same rule. What doesn't read it : the subtree of the element leaving the trail, recomposition cells in flight, morph particles, shed marks and decode blocks (instance record look.z is 0). An element that trails and has a ground fill (the floating box, the sheet) is drawn on a layer above, like a dialog: where it has ink it replaces the SDF beneath, so loosened decoration it passes doesn't show through it as loose marks. Texture : RGBA8, r = round(e·255), g, b = 128 + round(127·u), 128 + round(127·v), with 0 restoring exactly to 0; uploaded only on frames where bytes changed (about 16 KB). When the whole map is 0 a uniform turns reading off, so a still frame is byte-identical to having no map. Drawing only what changed ( §1.19 ): the bounding box of nodes whose bytes changed, grown by one cell; the G-buffer box adds pushable instances that read the map and intersect it (grown by drift ), and the final box grows again by the material's read range. With reduced motion : energy is added, flow isn't, lifetimes are halved and there is no breath ( Ui::set_reduced_motion ). What the framework brings in and takes away (new instances condensing, the ghosts of what left) fades in or out over 150 ms instead of loosening and moving ( Ui::reduced_motion ). What leaves takes its field with it : an element that leaves with its page (a page change, a closed dialog) (its nearest keyed ancestor goes too) leaves nothing: where it stirred the map, drew a flow or a decode, or was a ripple's scope, the map is cleared over its box, and when none of the old keyed elements is left the whole map is ( Ui::forget_gone , FieldMap::clear_in ), so no field or colour of its stays on the next page. A press's front still running when the page changes belongs to the press: it goes on over the new page as a whole ring at half its strength, its old scope (which went with the old page) dropped. audit::off_palette counts pixels in no colour the theme makes (the ground mixed toward the ink or an accent), and tests/fieldmap.rs checks it is 0 on the page after. Gusts ( Cmd::Gust { gust, scope } , fieldmap::Gust ): a band width px wide (330) that travels along dir at speed px a second (240) from the line through from , across the scope ( Scope as for fronts, at most the window). At a share u of the band its flow along dir is strength · 0.5 (1 − cos 2πu) · MapFx::flow ( strength 1) and its energy energy (0.2) times the same; for wake_s (0.5 s) behind its trailing edge the flow goes the other way, strength · wake · sin²(πu) ( wake 0.105: 6° on a blade the band leans 57°). Across dir the band lags slant · n^curve px ( slant 0, curve 1; n is the distance across dir over the scope's extent that way, 0..1), so it can sweep a field in perspective (W-01: 500 and 0.53). A gust is never put into the map to decay: on each step it is worked out from the map's clock at every node and laid over what the map holds, the larger energy and, of each flow component, the larger in size with its sign ( FieldMap::encode ). So a trail under it keeps its own life, and the frame the band and its wake have left the scope ( Gust::gone ) the map's bytes are what they would have been without it and no frame is wanted. With reduced motion it puts no flow. Lives by area ( El::map_life(energy_life, flow_life) , 0.1–30 s): a life is the time after which what was put in inside the element's visible box is back at rest, byte for byte, however much and however wide it was (a node takes the first such box it is in). The map there is the look's slowed down, with nothing spread: no bleed and no creep, so a thin path neither soaks away nor closes early; each node goes down from what was last put in it along the look's curve from 1 ( (1 + a) e^(−t/τ) − a , a = 0.15 τ , the exponential less the linear floor) stretched so that it is under half a byte step exactly at the life, energy and flow each by their own; the meander turns the flow as many times slower. All the nodes of one stroke keep their shares of each other, so a path keeps its width and closes all at once, the part walked first first. Stirs narrower than a cell are put in a cell wide (the nodes are a cell apart; the GPU reads them bilinearly, so the edge is smooth, not in cells). With W-01's 6 s, a 40 px path's stalk leans over 3° 5.0 s after the pointer passed and is upright at 6.0 s. Pacing what moves by itself ( Ui::ambient_fps(n) , 60 by default, which is no pacing): a frame wanted only by what moves by itself (the map, gusts, breath, flows, ticks) waits until 1 / n s after the last drawn one, within half the gap between the last two ticks (at most 0.5 / n s), so at 30 on a 60 Hz display with timestamps a little off it is every second refresh; needs_frame is false until then and next_wake gives that time ( web/amenui.js sets its timer 20 ms early, so the wait ends on the refresh it is due on). Input is never paced, and neither is what it starts until 1 s after the last input; after that it is what moves by itself (a trail that takes 6 s to close does not run at 60 frames a second). Everything goes by the clock, not by frames, so a frame at a given moment is the same bytes at 30 and at 60. Numbers ( MapFx , in Look::map and a preset's interaction.map ; each a number control): cell 8–32 (16), stirr 0–1 (0.6), stirr_radius 8–160 (48), flow 0–2 (1), drift 0–24 (6), energy_life 0.05–3 (0.45 s), flow_life 0.05–3 (0.5 s), bleed 0–1 (0.2), meander 0–1 (0.35), creep 0–1 (0.3), breath 0–0.3 (0), breath_s 2–12 (6 s). Presets: Normcore stirr 0; Cyberminimalism 0.25 with radius 32; Tech-Manual 0.2; Gaze 0.3; Bauhaus 0.4; Lo-Fi Print and Linocut 0.5; Glitch 0.7 with energy_life 0.25; Dotmatrix 0.8 with energy_life 0.7. Components : the floating box, the bottom_sheet panel and the card_stack cards (an invisible small element at each card's far corner carries the trail, since 3D elements don't read the map themselves) carry .stirr(Stirr::default()) by default, with the preset setting the strength. The page #stirr (in the side rail's concepts group): an area with decoration, a picture and a passage of text, with a draggable floating box over it; below, a formula caption whose twelve numbers are number controls; a "Stir" button sends Cmd::Stir . The F2 readout gains a line: the number of non-zero nodes in the map and its mean energy ( level ). Acceptance: unit tests in fieldmap.rs (after a stir energy falls monotonically and reaches exactly 0 within the bound; ten steps equal one accumulated step of ten, node by node; nothing is written outside the scope or in calm boxes; flow length never exceeds 1; meander keeps length and creep moves energy along ink; with reduced motion there is no flow, and at 0 it is exactly 0); tests/fieldmap.rs (dragging the floating box 185 px at 60 Hz: decoration beside the path above 0.3, Nudge text 0, legible Loosen text within the cap, Ignore 0, far away 0, the box itself 0; after release and settling into a corner, the map is all 0 within 1.5 s and no frames are wanted; under Normcore the map is never written and two seconds draw 0 frames; a press without a drag doesn't stir; with reduced motion the flow stays 0; Cmd::Stir in its element and path forms; over the drag each new scene reads the ink of no more instances than the box has, and the ink is on the shapes and 0 on the bare page); tests/render.rs (the same arguments with a drag rendered three times are byte-identical); check item 19; bench … map (one step plus upload at 1280 × 800 within 0.2 ms); craft <dir> stirr (eight frames each in plain , dottr , smudgr and glitchr ). Blades and gusts: tests/blades.rs (an 80 px blade at 0, 19, 38, 57 and 72° and stiff 0, 0.5 and 1: the tip's tangent within 1° of the lean, its lowest 4 px within 2° of 0.35 of it, with stiff 1 the lower 48 px within 0.5 px of a straight line, neighbouring segments at most 12° apart, the length within 2 %; the GPU draws it on its shape, its head along the tip's tangent and in its own paint upright, the lean paint at 72° of 72°; with lean_from 8° and lean_full 20° stem and head in their paint at 5°, half way at 14°, in the lean paint at ±25°, and the default mix linear; a title with Response::Ignore under a crossing gust draws the same pixels as at rest while text beside it that reads the map moves; a gust of 0.79 over one blade with max_lean 72° peaks at 57° ± 0.5°, sways back once to 6° ± 0.5° within 0.5 s of the trailing edge and is upright from 1.25 s after the peak, after which the map is byte-identical to before and no frame is wanted; a pointer's walk with map_life(6, 6) , 40 px wide: its last stalk over 3° at 5.0 s and upright at 6.0 ± 0.1 s, the end walked first upright first, then the map byte-identical to before with no frame wanted, and a box with lives of its own away from it changing nothing; paths 20, 40 and 80 px wide on and between the nodes' rows close within 0.1 s of each other at 6 s and keep their width (where the stalks lean half their most) within a cell, fresh and at 5 s; a gust over a path with 6 s lives leaves the path's bytes and its closing time as they were alone; the same schedule three times gives the same map bytes and frame; frames at 30 and 60 a second are the same at the same moments, input is not paced and what it starts is a second later; 3,000 blades are one draw, and while a gust crosses them the runtime's time a frame is within 0.1 ms of the same page without them, with nothing laid out or shaped).

A still page is byte-identical to plain . When something not meant to be read (a heading, a shape, decoration) loosens, its fill fades and its ink becomes one continuous thin line. Up to looseness 0.3 the line lies exactly on the glyph outlines, with straight bridges between glyphs and between a glyph's rings, so the whole element is drawn in one stroke as clean outlined letters. Looser, vertices one by one slide onto the chord between the vertices kept on either side and are removed, the two sides of the stroke merging into one line and then into long chords across several glyphs, while the remaining vertices wander off and the line bends into one soft curve through them. The one to three places with the most energy knot into tangles of the same thin line looping through itself dozens of times, and two long tails, one coming in from the scope's edge to the line's start and one going out from its end to another edge. Coming back runs in reverse: knots and tails shorten, vertices return in the opposite order, the line settles back onto the outline and the glyphs fill in. Text to read and controls never become thread and always stay as they are, except a control's own fill held loose (below). Two parts. The shading stage's m_scribblr is just exact (a flat ground, equal to plain at k = 0 ). The thread is geometry: in finish , after decode ( Ui::paint_strands ), the runtime computes the thread for each loosened element and draws it as turned round-ended bars ( SHAPE instances, the same kind as Mark::Line ), after the page's instances, into the G-buffer stage as usual, with true outlines. The element's own instances fade by fill(k) = 1 − smoothstep(0.02, 0.25, k) (instance opacity changed on the CPU, the original kept; Ui::looseness uses the original), so the fill has faded before the line leaves the outline, and there is never an offset line over a half-transparent fill. How the thread is computed ( src/strand.rs , no GPU): (1) glyphs are sampled for coverage at the grain pitch ( morph::cover_at ), Grid::contours(0.5) traces the iso-line, simplified to half a pixel and cached by glyph, size and transform; shapes use their rounded box. (2) They are joined in order into one line: each ring walks back to its start, then a bridge goes to the nearest vertex of the next ring; one Ramer–Douglas–Peucker pass over the whole line records each vertex's distance from its chord ( Rest::chord ), no greater than its parent's ( Rest::keep ), so a larger tolerance keeps fewer vertices, always a subset of those kept at a smaller one. (3) The tolerance is tolerance(k) = 0.5 + smoothstep(0.3, 0.5, k) × 0.3 × line height (a text's line height, a shape's short side): a vertex whose value is below it slides onto its chord by smoothstep over half a looseness from the looseness at which the tolerance passes it (between 0.3 and 0.5), and once there produces no segment, so at looseness 1 every vertex with a value below 0.5 + 0.3 × line height is gone. While sliding, a vertex follows its chord's ends and only its distance from the chord shrinks in proportion, so nothing jumps. Remaining vertices move by smoothstep(0.3, 1, k) × (reach × (0.4 W + J) + pull × drift × (u, v)) : W is the curl of smooth noise (patches of about 60 px, differentiated analytically, length at most 1, so a whole word drifts together), and J is a hashed direction per half line height along the path (length 0.3–1), eased between cells and seconds, so vertices a chord apart go their own ways and those between them follow. (4) Knots: clamp(round(path length / 200), 1, 3) per element, at the vertices kept to the end where the map's energy is highest, at least 80 px apart ( strand::knot_plan ). They are a primary and its seconds: the most energetic is the largest ( knot_r ), each next one smaller by knot_fall (1, knot_fall , knot_fall^1.75 ); each centre sits off the line by 0.5–0.9 of the largest radius, above and below in turn, then moves clear of text to read (below). The largest has strand::knots = round(60·knot·(0.5 + 0.5·e)·smoothstep(0.2, 0.6, k)) control points (36 at the defaults, fully loose), the others 64–100 % of that; a knot of fewer than strand::MIN_KNOT (12) is not drawn, since so few points read as a star. The knot is strand::tangle : control points that each turn about the centre from the last, 55 % of the steps 1.9–2.8 radians (across the knot), 30 % 0.5–1.3 (round it, making loops), 15 % 2.9–3.4 (back the way it came, a narrow loop); most at r × (0.25–1) , escape of them set out so the curve gets to r × (1.5–2.2) and back (a narrow stroke out of the knot); the centre itself wanders within 0.25 r , and the whole is stretched along a hashed way (1.3 against 0.75), so it is lopsided. The line goes from its vertex through the curve ( strand::curve ) of those points and back, and goes on. Curves ( strand::curve(ctrl, max_turn) ): a uniform cubic B-spline with each end point tripled, so it starts and ends on them; sampled densely, then drawn as the fewest straight pieces that turn at most max_turn (15°) from one to the next, stay within a quarter pixel of the curve and are 1.5–48 px long (shorter only at the tip of a tight loop). A B-spline does not pass through its points, so where the points fold back the curve makes a narrow loop. (5) Two tails: the one at the end follows the flow there (or, when the flow's way reaches less than six tenths as far as the farthest way, the farthest way); the one at the start takes whichever of 16 directions reaches farthest without running the same way as the end tail, joined backwards to the line's start; a way that has a clear run to the scope's edge (past no text to read) wins over one that stops short, so a tail never cuts across the page behind a picture or the controls. Their length is at least max(tail, 0.6 × the scope's long side) , and when the way meets the edge, exactly enough to reach it; each is one long slow curve: tail_turns gentle bends (each 12–25°, smaller with more turns, at about even places, one way then the other, so a tail never strays more than 25° from its way) are the control points of a curve sampled at 24–32 even places, with a waver of the hand across it (0.6–1.5 % of its length, two or three times along it); a way that would pass within 24 px of text to read scores 0.3 of its reach, and a tail whose tip would land within 24 px of text to read is drawn back until it does not; the line goes round pictures 12 px clear (a picture is drawn over what lies under it); a Trace 's points keep 12 px off pictures and 24 px off text to read ( strand::clear_path ). The clearances move the control points and the knot centres, before the curve is made through them, rather than the sampled curve, so the curve stays one smooth line; tails are cut where they meet the line and go round picture corners; every point draws back in proportion to k . Once the line bends, where it turns into a tail tighter than a 10 px radius it turns on an arc of 12 px × smoothstep(0.3, 0.5, k) instead (from 4 px before the join, or farther back while the line there is tighter), then on a curve tangent to the tail three radii on; on the side the tail goes, or the long way round on the other when that side is outside the scope or in a box to keep clear of. A line end or a tail stub that would run straight for 20 px or more between two control points (a glyph's upright stroke, a tail drawn back) gets one more control point halfway, 15 % × smoothstep(0.3, 0.5, k) of its length to the side away from the next turn, so it bends to its end.
