Tails, and the long line once drawn, are at tail_tone (0.5) of the line's opacity, and knots are whole: bright knots on quiet lines, so the density reads. Leaving the scope box, the last segment is cut at the edge, and a tail stops before the box of text to read or a control (and before calm boxes). (6) Past k = 0.3 the line bends toward the curve through its vertices: the vertices left are simplified (to 2 px × smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, k) ), the polyline through them is blended with their curve by (1 − angular) × smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, k) , its corners rounded as far as the blend goes; below 0.3 the line is the outline. (7) No piece of thread enters text to read: a knot whose circle ( 2.2 r ) meets a calm box grown by 6 px moves away from it by up to 3 r , then shrinks, and is not drawn below 12 px; a pose vertex inside a calm box goes to its nearest edge; any piece still crossing a box grown by 5 px goes round it. The line's opacity is smoothstep(0, 0.12, k) , bridges, knots and tails smoothstep(0.1, 0.3, k) , and its width is weight throughout. The looseness the thread shows is strand::shown(k) : the same at the ends, but it hurries through 0.15–0.4 (crossed while k goes from 0.22 to 0.30), where a half-drawn letter and a few loose lines look neither like text nor like a thread, and a held pose (a step of the beat) is never worked out inside that band ( strand::held ): drawing back from 1 to 0 spends at most 8 frames there. At k = 0 there are no thread instances (rule 3 holds by construction). Text to read and controls ( legible ) don't become thread, their fill doesn't fade, and the map's flow doesn't push them (under scribblr their instances loosen in place in the G-buffer stage, look.w = 1). Rule 3 in its own words: the pointer passing over text leaves the text alone. Thread is only for headings ( legible(false) ), shapes and decoration, and for a control's own fill that the page holds loose ( El::loose above 0 on a control whose own instances are all shapes): as in every material ( §1.15 ) the fill comes apart, here into a thread round its outline that keeps out of its label's box, while within the island round the label it stays whole (the faded fill is restored there, core_at ); fronts passing a control still leave it alone. The thread starts from the outline as drawn : the G-buffer stage pushes instances that aren't for reading along the map's flow by flow × drift ( §1.29 ), and the thread's rest path adds the same offset, so as the fill fades the line lies exactly on it, not as an offset shadow beside it. The thread's bars don't read the map themselves ( look.z = 0); fronts push them as usual ( resp.y the same as the element's). The pose follows the material clock : the time for wandering, knots and tails is mclock , which advances only while the map or something else moves, so an element held loose at rest keeps its pose and wants no frames; seeds depend only on the element, not the beat, so poses change gradually rather than being redrawn every beat. With a beat ( §1.32 ) the pose is rounded to its step (the thread's vertices are equal one by one within a step), while opacity and fill stay continuous every frame. Elements of shapes only (a rule, a box, a ground) have no knots and no tails, and wander half as far: they come apart into one line that wavers gently. Knots and tails belong to text. Budget ( §1.27 ): an element asks for (rest vertices + 6 × knot points + 64) × 3 segments, at most 2400; when it gets fewer, curves first turn up to 30° a piece instead of 15°, then knots lose points (a sixth at a time), a knot left with fewer than 12 is dropped (never a straight star), then every n-th vertex is taken, and finally the end is cut short. The thread never breaks. What never becomes thread : canvases, morphs, recomposing text, decoding elements, and elements in a role hand-off or a flow (they loosen as plain ). Thread appears only when the global material is scribblr (not under a subtree override). Long paths El::trace(Trace { points, progress, weight, dash, gap, pull, stir, paint }) : a very long polyline (in the element's own coordinates) drawn by progress , bent by the flow by pull × drift ; with dash above 0 it is cut into segments by arc length from the start (with gap between), so segments already drawn don't move as it draws; with stir above 0 its head stirs the map where it passes each frame. It draws under every material. The #stirr page's "Draw a line" button draws a looping dashed line through the area. Numbers (row 9 of MAT_PARAMS ): weight 0.5–3 (1), grain 1–6 (2), reach 0–64 (40), knot 0–1 (0.6), knot_r 4–120 (48), tail 0–1200 (480), pull 0–2 (1), angular 0–1 (0.35); Look::beat ( §1.32 ; a preset's interaction.beat ) sets how long a pose is held. The thread's shape ( strand::ThreadShape , in StrandFx ): knot_fall 0.3–1 (0.55), escape 0–4 (2), tail_turns 1–6 (3), tail_tone 0.2–1 (0.5). strand::figure uses the same. A drawn tangle strand::figure(seed, r, above, below) : the same knots and tails generated once from a fixed seed (one knot of radius r , 36 control points, and one line passing through it top to bottom, above long above the knot and below long below), not reading the map, for use as page content ( El::trace , §4.4 ). While a dialog is open : the page's thread and drawn tangles are not drawn (they would land on the dialog's layer, above the card); elements inside the dialog behave as usual. Tails : every segment stops before the box of text to read (not only testing whether a point falls inside, so a step never jumps over a line of text), and never passes back through the inner half of the element's own box. Pictures over the thread : the thread (an element's and El::trace ) passes behind pictures, and no thread is drawn inside a picture's box ( strand::outside cuts each segment at the picture's box). In the G-buffer stage, thread ink over a picture would be read as the picture's own colour (turning red), so it can't be drawn on top. The page #material-scribblr . Acceptance: unit tests in strand.rs (no segments at k = 0 ; at k up to 0.3 every vertex is within half a pixel of the outline, even with the map moving; the ends join; the vertex ranking is nested, with a chord's ends ranked before the vertices that slide onto it; fully loose, segments are at most 15% of the vertex count with a median segment length of at least 24 px, and over 30 frames from 1 back to 0 no vertex moves more than reach / 6 per frame; curve over a hundred random sets of control points: under 3 % of turns over 20°, none over 60°, the ends on the first and last point, the same input the same output; a knot at r = 48 with 36 points, for ten seeds each: under 3 % of turns over 20°, at least 40 self-crossings, at least 6 small loops (two passes through a crossing less than 3 r of line apart), at least 35 % of its length within 0.5 r of its centroid and at least two strokes out past 1.4 r and back; 1–3 knots, the largest at least 1.6 times the radius of the next, the centres not all the same distance from the line, with a knot radius of at least 0.5 × knot_r at looseness 0.5; every piece of a tail turning at most 8° from the last and at most 25° from its way; two tails: the end tail's ends at least 300 px apart, stopping within 8 px of the scope's edge, the start tail at least half as long, neither entering the box of text to read, and the end tail at least 100 px long at looseness 0.33; nothing outside the scope box; within budget; the same input gives the same bytes; figure twice is the same, its height is above + below , under 3 % of its turns over 20°, and its knot crosses itself at least 40 times; a segment cut at several boxes keeps the parts outside them; dashes are dash long each, earlier segments don't change as more is drawn, and dash = 0 is solid); tests/strand.rs (no thread and no frames at rest; dragging the box past a large heading makes thread, one line, with tails running with the flow; text to read has no thread, its instances' opacity and position unchanged and not pushed by the flow; drawing a title back from 1 to 0 at 60 Hz, at most 8 frames show a looseness in 0.15–0.4; once stopped the thread is gone and no frames are wanted; at budget scale 0.25 it is still one line; recomposing text has no thread; with a beat of 83 ms steps the same step is identical and different steps differ, with 0 every frame differs; at the default angular fully loose, over nine in ten turns between the line's pieces are at most 25°, and at looseness 0.2 the line is within half a pixel of the one at angular 1; on the sample page ( amenui::sample ) at looseness 1, 0.7 and 0.4 no piece of any kind crosses the ink box of text to read (grown by 4 px), and the rule has no knot or tail; "回" is four rings (two boxes with inner and outer edges each) with three bridges; neither end of a morph has thread; "Loose thread" at 64 px fully loose without knots or tails: segments at most 15% of the rest vertex count, median segment length at least 24 px, at most a quarter of the thread's ink within 2 px of the rest outline, and the bounding box at least 0.6 × reach larger than the still text on each side; for the Loose Thread style page see §4.4 ); check item 20 (1. at looseness 0 byte-identical to plain on dark and light grounds, control: different at 1; 2. no page background in a fully loosened picture on a light ground; 3. at looseness 1, at 20 places well clear of other segments, the thread's ink integrated along the normal equals weight × scale within half a pixel, measured for 1 and 2 px widths at 1× and 1.5 px at 2×; 4. over 30 frames from 1 to 0, the farthest distance of the thread's ink (bridges and tails only while visible) from the rest outline never grows; 5. under scribblr , dragging the floating box with its trail for 90 frames, partial redraw equals full redraw); bench … strand (200 glyphs fully loose within 1 ms); craft <dir> scribblr (eight frames of a heading from 1 back to 0, each frame stirring the map by its looseness and filling the whole heading up to that frame's looseness before drawing, so the energy at the heading is at least 0.8 in frame 1; the last frame waits for the map to settle; dark and light grounds), and craft <dir> thread-ref (the style page with the heading held fully loose, one frame each on black and paper, to compare side by side with the reference).

One command says what is wrong with a page as drawn: render --page <name> --audit prints a list of findings, most serious first, and with --strict a P0 or P1 is an error. amenui::audit::audit(ui, px, ground, theme) takes a deterministic frame's pixels, the same frame drawn with every glyph hidden (the ground under the text, before the finishing pass), the runtime that drew them and the theme they were drawn in, and returns Vec<Finding> ( level , key , kind , measured , limit , fix ); drive::audit(spec, faces, o) renders a page and audits it, drive::audit_with for an application's own pages ( Driven::audit ). The view's structural problems ( Ui::problems() ) are on the same list as P1 Structure . Everything is measured; each fix is one sentence to act on, naming the element and the number. kind what is measured level Clipped text to read whose ink ( Instance boxes after poses and turns) is cut by a clip, the window or a reveal; or a word drawn in part. Not what a scroll view can bring into view: a cut is a clip only where no scroll view can bring that edge's side into view. A scroll view's own edges along the way it scrolls do not clip (across, they do); an edge outside a scroll view (the window's, or a clipping box's around it) is as far out as the scroll view can still move the text from it; a box inside it that does not scroll clips as ever a whole glyph or more, or a word in part: P0; less than a glyph: P1 Contrast per line of text, the strongest ink pixel against what is drawn under it (WCAG 2) text to read below 3:1 P0, below 4.5:1 P1; large text to read (a font size of 24 px or more, or 19 px bold: El::weight of half a pixel or more, or a face of weight 600 or more) below 3:1 P0 and nothing more; a lone mark (no letter or digit, such as › or −) below 3:1 P1; text not to read below 3:1 P3 Overlap the share of a glyph's ink covered by another drawn glyph, in one element or between two to read text to read over 10 %: P1; posed text over its overlap + 0.05: P2 Small the drawn height of text to read (size × scale × the pose's vertical scale) under 9 device px: P1 Eroded at looseness 0, the ink pixels (differing from the ground by at least 24 and by at least half the line's contrast) inside each text-to-read ink box, against the same page drawn in plain under 85 % of plain's: P1 Restless after the last input, the clock run on at 60 Hz: still asking for frame after frame 2 s later with nothing visible marked El::ongoing() (a timed wake now and then, such as a caret's blink, is not restless) P1 A preset's rules ( Preset::rules , preset::Rule ). A preset can hold its pages to more than the floors above, and only to more: five rules, each measured on the same frame, and audit::audit_under(ui, px, ground, theme, preset) adds them to the audit. render --preset <hash|file.json> draws the page in a preset and audits it by its rules ( drive::in_preset wraps an opener so, for render_with , audit_with and frames ). A page that draws a preset in part of the window marks that subtree El::audit_under(preset) : what is in it is held to that preset's rules (and the accent's share is of its box), the rest to the page's preset if it is audited under one, else to the floors alone; a nearer mark inside wins. audit::audit reads the marks from the runtime, so a page audited through any wrapper is held to them. Driven::audit and Driven::audit_under have no default: a wrapper forwards both, or does not build. rule what is measured finding contrast { of, min } as Contrast ; of: prose is running text (legible, no larger than the theme's body size, more than 40 characters in the element), of: read all text to read Contrast text_size { min } the drawn height of text to read, as Small , in logical px Small margin { min } the ink of text to read to each window edge, logical px; in a scroll view, the left, the right and (scrolled to the top) the top Margin measure { max } characters on each line of running text, wide ones (CJK, full-width) counting 2 Measure accent { max } the share of the frame within 24/255 of the theme's accent in every channel Accent A rule's finding is a P1. Where the floor and a rule find the same kind in the same element there is one finding, the rule's, at P0 when the floor found a P0. A preset read from JSON or a recipe with a contrast under 4.5 or a text size under 9 px is refused ( PresetError::Looser , naming the rule); one written before rules has none. The ten presets: running text 7:1 and all text to read 4.5:1; text size, margin and measure 11/16/80 (Algorithmic Gaze), 12/14/64 (Neo-Dotmatrix), 12/16/72 (Lo-Fi Print), 12/24/72 (Glitch), 12/16/68 (Metamorphosis Linocut and Bauhaus), 11/24/80 (Tech-Manual), 12/12/80 (Normcore), 11/16/80 (Cyberminimalism), 11/16/72 (Loose Thread); an accent share of 2 % for Tech-Manual and Normcore and 1 % for Cyberminimalism and Loose Thread. The default looks have none. A preset's contrast rules are not for large text: its floor is the 3:1 the base rule holds it to (no preset has a floor of its own for it). For them the recipes changed: the preset and form3d recipes' descriptions are TEXT (running text in DIM is 5–6.4:1 in five presets), the stack recipe's formula is 12 px, and the gesture recipe's floating label is padded 10 px (its ink was 22 px from the top). Posed text dimmed by depth on purpose is read by its nearer half; the smallest size of posed text is its 10th percentile among the glyphs drawn at half opacity or more. A clipped finding says which side is cut, how far the ink reaches past it (px) and what cuts it (the clipping element's key, or the window), and suggests reveal_by(Reveal::Word) when a reveal cuts a word. The eroded check guards materials with a look of their own at rest ( near , charr , and materials added from source); one whose rest is plain passes by construction. The annotation layer shows what the audit measures: gaze::INK draws the true ink's bounding box of an element (after transforms and poses) dashed, with a leader dashed 4 px on, 4 px off from a corner of that box to the nearest point of the drawn outline (of a shape's true outline too), never outside the box: of the corners 12 px clear of text to read, the one farthest from the outline, the line kept round text to read ( strand::clear_path ). A leader shorter than 16 px (two dashes) is not drawn, so a box that hugs its ink, as text's does, has none. Then an INK w×h label ( hit::ink_of , Ui::leaders ), from the same measure the clipping and overlap checks use. The annotation colour ( Gaze::colour ) is used as given where it stands 4.5:1 from the page's ground; on a ground where it does not (the light theme) it is the same hue darkened until it does ( Gaze::colour_on ), for the boxes, leaders, labels and guides alike. Tags and INK readouts never cover text to read or each other: each tries outside the ink box above at the left, then below, then to the right ( gaze::place_tag ), takes the first place that meets no text-to-read ink box and no other label, and when none is free only the box is drawn. What the audit found on the recipes, and what changed for it: Paint::DIM was 0.5 of the way from ground to ink, under 4.5:1 on the light theme (3.2:1); it is 0.66 (5.2:1 light, 6.9:1 dark). The light theme's accent was under 4.5:1 against its ground, both as text and under a solid button's label (3.4:1); it is darker, (0.64, 0.20, 0.035) at 5.6:1, and the selection tint is 12 % instead of 14 %. A selected list row's note is TEXT . The near material drew text as outline and 25 % fill, too faint at text sizes, and lost the outline entirely on a filled panel (the panel's nearness is max-blended over the glyph's); text keeps its own ink whole there, and text set in the ground's colour (a label on a solid button) takes the ink's colour, since near draws the panel open. The loading recipe's tick asked for a new view every frame forever; it asks only when a row changes. Acceptance: tests/audit.rs (five pages broken on purpose, each reporting its finding at its level: text past the window Clipped P0, grey on grey Contrast P0, two lines over each other Overlap P1, 6 px text Small P1, an element that never stops moving Restless P1, and not when it is marked ongoing ; text a material wears away at rest Eroded P1; a calm page has no findings; the seventeen recipes in every material, dark and light, have no P0 or P1); tests/preset_rules.rs (each rule on a page broken for it reports one P1 with its measure and limit, and nothing without the rule; the floor and a rule on the same text report once; a looser preset is refused and an older one reads with no rules; the seventeen recipes in each preset have no P0 or P1); tests/clear_text.rs (under Glitch, inside the ink boxes of text to read red and blue are those of the frame with no chroma offset within 1/255, at 1x and 2x, compared flat; text not to read keeps its fringe; a page with no text is byte-identical with it on or off; only Glitch has it); a unit test that a bent frame unbent has its marks back where they were laid out, and with no bend is the frame byte for byte; text a bend carries off the frame is Clipped ( tests/clear_text.rs ); render --page recipe-form --audit --strict exits 0. A component's examples are a page too: render --page component-<name> lays out examples/components/<name>.rs one example under another ( recipes::components::ui ). In Claude Code the repository's save hook ( .claude/settings.json , tools/audit-hook.sh ) renders, after an Edit or Write, the one page a view file belongs to (a recipe, a component's examples, or its widget in src/widgets/ ) with --audit --strict and hands the P0 and P1 findings and the view's problems back to the model; AGENTS.md is also its amenui skill ( tools/skill.sh , tests/skill.rs ). Ui::line_inks(key) reads each line of a text element as drawn: its text range, line box and ink box ( LineInk ), for tests and for an application that places things by the text's real ink.

Look::beat: beat::Beat { bpm, steps, swing } (a preset's interaction.beat ): bpm 40–300, 0 is off (the default); steps a beat 1–8 (4); swing 0–0.5 (0), how much later every second step starts, in steps. A bar is four beats. With a beat, what moves on its own falls on its steps: a front's radius, glitchr's held rows, scribblr's held pose, a transition's steps and a morph's flight are drawn at the start of the step the beat clock is in ( Ui::beat_grid ); line widths, opacity and condensing are not rounded (the shader's condensing reads the clock off the grid). Off, every clock is the runtime's own, byte for byte as before the beat. The beat clock runs with the runtime's ( Ui::beat_time ; Ui::beat() is BeatNow { bar, beat, step, phase } , each from 1, for the application's own state) and only the beat's commands move it against it: Cmd::Hold(n) stops it for n steps (the frame stays byte for byte, and frames are still wanted: the scene presented is the one the hold began with, whatever the application changes meanwhile, and after it the page is drawn from the state as it is then), Cmd::Retrigger plays the current step again from its start, Cmd::Rewind(beats) takes it back (never before 0) and with it what it carries (fronts, transitions, held rows); the application's state, the field map, condensing and the materials' own clocks (the ground's drift, scribblr's pose) are not taken back. With a beat, text to read is not pushed by fronts (a push a step at a time reads as the page shaking), only loosened up to legible_cap ; without one it is pushed as before. Cmd::Set { name, value } sets a number of the look over the application's ( Look::set : loose_scale , legible_cap , loose_max , press_ms , fx.* , beat.* , a material's number as <material>.<name> in MAT_PARAMS , clamped to its range); a switch ( post.invert , post.binary ) given 1 turns over and given 0 goes back to the look's own. Ui::command(cmd) sends any command from outside the application; a script schedules them ( §1.17 , kind: "cmd" , at: "bar.beat.step" ). There is no audio, no beat detection and no video: the beat comes from the script, and the result is a run of PNGs. Look::hold_ms is gone: a held pose of h ms is a beat of one step h long, at the fewest steps a beat that keep bpm in range ( Beat::of_hold ; 83 ms is 240.96 bpm in 3 steps). Recipes are look:v3: ; a look:v2: recipe is refused, with the beat its interaction.hold_ms becomes. Acceptance ( tests/beat.rs ): at 120 bpm and four steps a front's radius moves a whole step or not at all between frames; frames during Hold(2) are identical; the frame after Rewind(1) is the frame drawn a beat before; Set of post.invert once turns every pixel over (within 1/255), twice gives the frame back; an event at "3.2.1" and one at 4500 ms give the same frame; bpm 0 with any steps and swing, and the beat's commands, change nothing.

A plate keeps the ink drawn on it. El::plate(Plate { fade_s }) on an element: what its subtree draws is not wiped the next frame; new ink goes over the old, and a pixel drawn again is new again. It is a picture, not content: it is not in the accessibility mirror, its text cannot be selected, and a new window size empties it. Cmd::ClearPlate { key } empties it in one frame, hard (a cut for the beat); fade_s (0–60 s in steps of 0.5; 0 keeps the ink for good) is the soft way. The plate draws nothing of its own: no edge, no ground, no dimming. An empty plate is byte for byte the page without it, and costs the same: a plate that has held no ink since it was made or cleared is not laid on (no extra pass). What is on a plate is ink, not something to read or press. Text to read and controls go beside the plate or over it, as its siblings, not its children; one inside a plate's subtree is reported ( OnPlate in Ui::problems , P1 in the audit). A label meant to stay readable must not rely on ink that fades: with fade_s set, what a plate holds goes, so a label drawn onto it (or strokes that make a label) is gone too; it belongs over the plate, as a sibling. Cost, as regression lines on lavapipe at 1440 × 900 (a whole-window plate, the fifth set's measurement: keeping ink 12.3 → 15.0 ms, ageing 49 → 57.5 ms): a frame keeping ink at most 125 % of the same page without a plate, an ageing frame at most 120 %. On a real GPU a whole-window plate may add at most 0.6 ms a frame; that measurement is still to be made before a release, and if it is over, plates are for music videos and the lab only. It reaches as far as its clip box and ink is cut at the box's edge, with no fade there (that would draw the box). The ink on a plate is ink: the near image is max-blended, so strokes laid one over another keep a true outline, and every material draws it as usual. There is no material code for plates. At most 4 plates in a window, their images together at most twice the window's area; more are drawn as ordinary elements (keeping nothing) and Ui::problems reports PlateOver . A slot newly taken starts empty. The renderer keeps four images for each plate: ink, near, and when each pixel was drawn, in 1/120 s ticks as 24 bits, twice (where the ink was drawn, and where its nearness reached). A new stroke's spread keeps its own outline alive without making the old ink under it new, so the line between old and new ink is the new stroke's outline, to within a pixel. In the G-buffer stage the plate's instances of this frame are drawn into its ink and near images and its ages, and the kept images are laid on in their place (premultiplied over the ink, max over the near image). The plate clock stops while a Hold lasts and never runs back: Rewind does not take ink back. A transition's mask acts on the plate's ink as on anything else, and the plate of a page that went is emptied when the page goes. Ageing ( fade_s above 0): a pixel is as drawn until four fifths of fade_s have passed since it was last drawn ( a = 0.8), then its ink's coverage is multiplied by 1 − smoothstep(0.8, 1, a) , so it fades as plain's condensing fades in, with no pattern of its own, and is gone at fade_s . The material draws what is left as it draws any ink with that coverage. The near image is a distance, which a fade would move, so it stays whole until a is 1. While only ageing moves, the runtime asks for at most 30 frames a second; when the last stroke has gone the page is the clean page and asks for none. With less motion it is the same. A plate with fade_s 0 keeps its ink without asking for frames; it belongs in music videos, the lab and pages that say they are a drawing board, not on ordinary pages. Frames with plates redraw only what changed, as any page does ( §1.19 ); a frame in which ink is ageing redraws every plate whole. Text to read on a plate's ink holds what is under it by §1.15 's rule, as on any other ink. Acceptance: tests/plate.rs (a stroke stays when the view no longer has it; the cleared frame is as never drawn; an empty plate is as no plate in nine materials and both themes; with fade_s 4, a = 0.25 as just drawn, the ink unchanged before 0.5, never growing, empty at 1, at most 30 frames a second and none after; fade_s 2 empty 2 s after the last stroke with no frames after; ink on a plate loosening in dottr; clearing and inverting in one frame under 5 % of pixels changing; at a 0.9 in plain every pixel inside a stroke within 2/255 of the others and halfway between ink and paper to within 3 %, the ink never growing from 0.8 to 1 in steps of 0.02 and none just past 1; an old stroke at 0.9 with at most 55 % of the ink of a new one at 0.5, which is 99 % as just drawn; old ink 2 px from a new stroke's outline as old as the rest of it; a Hold(2) byte for byte; five plates keeping four; a new window size emptying them; the same timeline three times the same 300 frames; halfway through a crack the ink only in the pieces not yet turned and gone at the end; nothing on a plate in the accessibility mirror, and text to read in one reported; an empty plate not laid on, one with ink laid on once).

Each effect the framework draws can be turned off from the look, without the application building its view again: Look::off: style::Off , every field false (on) by default. An effect that is off goes straight to its end state: nothing is lost but the motion, every control still works, it asks for no frames and draws no pass of its own. A switch takes effect on the next frame; a morph, a flow, a recomposition or a decode in flight when its switch goes off ends where it was going, and fronts in flight stop. field off means close new things are there at once, without condensing ( Fx::enter ) fronts Cmd::Ripplr and a commit's front send nothing; Cmd::Commit shows the new look at once, with no transition flows Cmd::Flow does nothing: the page changes at once morphs Cmd::Morph , Ui::morph and Ui::morph_from_last do nothing: the new picture is there at once ripples a press sends no front: it changes the control and nothing round it loosen a press does not hold what is pressed loose or condense it again after, and no burst runs on press or hover recompose changed text is replaced at once ( §1.16 ) decode El::decode text is there at once ( §1.28 ) material_still the materials' clocks stand (their rest pose: no drift, no slips, no wandering thread) and the beat stops bloom no bloom pass ( post.bloom ) ground the field's dots, the ground's own marks (dottr's ground units, smudgr's paper grain), are not drawn: the ground is the theme's plain ground, the same under fronts, the pointer and the field map; a material copied with amenui add material reads the switch as ground_marks() Acceptance: tests/off.rs (for each switch, the frame after what would set the effect off is byte for byte the frame the effect settles on, and the page asks for no frames in the 2 s after; a flow switched off mid-flight ends at once; everything is on by default; with ground off the empty ground is the theme's ground under a front and the pointer, and no frames are asked for once the front is over).

El::stage() marks the live piece a page is about (a Lab cell's picture, a demo's canvas), so that controls beside it answer the hand even when the piece is slow to draw. A stage that draws within the frame is drawn every frame like anything else: the thumb, the value and the piece all show a change in the same frame. The runtime times each draw of a stage's subtree; when its draws average more than 0.6 of a frame (the frame being the time between ticks) over the last 8, the stage is slow , and it is no longer slow once its draws have stayed under 0.4 of a frame for 1 s. A slow stage holds the image it last drew on a frame that answers input (a pointer move, a press, a key, text, the wheel): its subtree is not painted, and the instances it drew last are drawn in its place, so the renderer has nothing new to draw there and the controls are drawn in the frame. It draws again on the first frame without new input, on the first frame after a release, and during a long stream of input at least every max(100 ms, 6 × its average draw) , at most 500 ms ( stage::HOLD_MIN_S , HOLD_DRAWS , HOLD_MAX_S ). A draw replaces the image whole, at once (a cut), and nothing marks a stage that holds. A stage whose box, clip or number of elements changed draws whatever the input. Holding costs nothing beyond the stage's own draws: a frame in which a held stage would still hold paints nothing for it, a step of it ( Ui::on_step , below) that comes while it would hold is not viewed but waits for its next draw, and when it may draw it is viewed and drawn alone, as a step is, the rest of the page copied ( Ui::needs_frame asks for that frame, next_wake gives the end of its hold). A stage that held is drawn whole when it may, never by its parts alone (below): its held image is behind all of it. When a stage's own device scale steps down under load (the governor, below), that acts first; a stage is held only when the lowest scale is still slow. Not for controls: what is inside a stage that holds does not change while it holds. A stage that changes by itself (a Lab cell that runs, a demo that moves) need not rebuild the page it is on. Ui::on_step(f) steps the stages' pieces on every tick, after on_tick , and returns the keys of the stages that changed; Ui::stage_view(f) gives one stage's subtree by its key, as the page's view would make it. When nothing else changed the view on that tick, only the stages that stepped are viewed again: each new subtree takes the place of the old one in the boxes the last layout gave it, if it is laid out the same (the same elements with the same keys, styles and text to measure); its places are worked out again (scroll, transforms, clips), and the paint draws only those subtrees, copying every other element's instances, glyphs and colours from the last paint. The frame is the one a whole view, layout and paint of the page would give, instance for instance. A step whose subtree is laid out otherwise (it grew, an element came or went, a text changed what is measured), a stage that holds a 3D scene, an animation or a transition in flight, or anything else that changed the view on that tick, and the whole page is viewed, laid out and painted again. Text recomposing glyph by glyph ( §1.16 ), in a stage or anywhere else on the page, does not: what is copied is copied as it was painted, not as the last frame's motion left it (a glyph hidden under its tiles, one sliding), and the tiles are drawn over it as they are on any frame. perf().counters.restages counts the frames drawn so (a frame that had to paint the page whole is not counted). What changes with a piece outside its stage (an experiment's formula, a label with the value) is marked El::steps : on_step returns its key with the stage's, stage_view gives its subtree, and it is put in place as a stage is, but drawn every frame like anything else (never held, never at a stage's scale). An element marked El::steps inside a stage is a part of it that changes alone (the Lab's Loupe: a lens moving over a page that stays): a step that names the stage views only its outermost parts, by their keys through stage_view , and puts them in place as a stage is, and the paint draws only them, the rest of the stage copied from the last paint as the rest of the page is. A part that is not viewed ( stage_view gives None for its key) or is laid out otherwise, and the stage is viewed whole as above. A slow stage a part of which was drawn alone draws on its next paint whatever the input, since its held image is no longer what it shows. So the page that names a stage's step need not know what in it moves. Text counts as laid out the same when its words changed but it measures as before at its widest, at its narrowest and at its width (figures of one width: the mono face, or a fixed box). An absolutely placed element whose offsets alone changed (each side a length before and after, the opposite side auto; a chip dragged about a stage) counts as laid out the same too: it is moved by the change on whole pixels, with its subtree, and the tree takes its new offsets for the next layout. Messages that are a subtree's own ( El::local_messages ): what the handlers in such a subtree send (a press, a drag, a key, the pointer over it and the pointer leaving it, the wheel) is taken to change only it and the elements marked El::steps . After such a message the subtree (by its key, through stage_view ) and those elements are put in place as a stage that stepped is, and drawn again; laid out otherwise, the page is viewed and laid out whole. A stage the hand drags its chips about (the Lab's Weld) is marked so: a drag frame then costs no view of the page and no layout. A glass that follows the pointer (the Lab's loupe) is marked so too: the pointer leaving it is restaged as its moves are, not a view and layout of the page (about 10 ms on the loupe's page at 2x). The hold reads the input of the frame that lays it out: with input coalesced ( Ui::coalesce , as the hosts run), a tick leaves the frame's input to the paint that Ui::settle makes, and that paint spends it. A stage's own scale. When the machine cannot draw a page in time, the stages are what give: their device scale steps down 2 → 1.5 → 1 → 0.75 (from the device's own; on a 1× display the only step is 0.75), while text, panels and the chrome stay at the device's. The governor ( perf::StageScale , fed by each drawn frame while stages are on the page) goes by the intervals between frames, since a GPU's time is not measured on the web: the display frame is the 10th percentile of the intervals of the last second that had no step, never under 4 ms. It steps down when the 95th percentile interval over 3 s is above 1.5 display frames or 20 ms (50 fps), whichever is less (intervals come in whole frames, so 1.5 is the first value that means frames were missed; the 20 ms catches a piece that misses from its first frame, which would otherwise measure a display frame of two). It steps up after 5 s with no missed frame and every frame's cost under 60 % of the display frame, and only when the 95th percentile cost over those 5 s, times the pixels the level up has more (the new scale over the old, squared: × 1.78 from 1.5 to 2 or from 0.75 to 1, × 2.25 from 1 to 1.5), is under 85 % of the display frame; never while a pointer is down. A step down within 5 s of a step up holds the lower level, and so does a second step up ( perf::STAGE_UPS , all levels together), until Ui::reset_stage_scale (a new route) or a new window size: a route's visit has at most two steps up. Every step is a cut. The look's quality below 1 pins the scale at that share of the device's (the nearest step), and the governor rests. perf().stage_scale and Perf::stage_label ( stage 1.5x , shown dim by a status line; nothing at the device's scale) say where it is; the readout's look line shows it too. The renderer draws a stage's ink and nearness at the device's scale as everything else, and shades its pixels in the reduced material pass at the stage's scale, filtered up into the frame; a pixel whose reduced neighbours are not all the stage's is shaded at the device's scale, so the stage's edge is sharp. The reduced grid is fixed to the content of the largest scroll area: its texels' centres are at (i + n0 + ½) / q device px less the area's offset modulo GRID_WRAP = 1536 px (a whole number of texels at every scale, 2/3, 3/8, 1/2 and 3/4 of the device's), on 1/256 px, and the filter up weighs its four texels itself ( textureLoad ) by where the pixel is among their centres; against the sampler's filter for the same reduced pass ( Renderer::checks , its weights in 8 bits on most GPUs) no channel differs by more than 1/255, at any offset of the grid, and at full quality there is no filter up ( tests/scroll_move.rs ). So a stage the scroll carried by whole device px is, pixel for pixel, the stage shaded where it is, and a moved frame keeps it. A stage is shaded again where the grid moved under it: every one when the grid moved otherwise than the frame (a scroll that did not move the last frame, another largest scroll area, a wrap), with the move those outside the moved scroll area (their content stayed, the grid did not) and, while the trace shows, those in it too (the content held to a lattice moves otherwise than the grid). On the website's Lab, slow scrolling at 0.375, the stages had been shaded again in every moved frame (39% of the window on average); now 2% in 12 frames of 40 (a stage outside the list), and the frame shades 7% instead of 44%. What is drawn after a stage within its box (the modal layer, menus, popovers, tooltips, the readout, a caption laid over it) is shaded at the device's scale: the renderer keeps up to 16 boxes over the stages for it, each what it touches merged. Up to 16 stages are shaded at their scale; more are at the device's. A stage held under input (above) is not shaded again, since it does not change. The scale steps first: a stage is held only when its scale is as low as it goes (or pinned, or no renderer measures it). Ui::slow_stage(ms) adds ms to every stage's draw, for checks (by the stage's pixels: at 1.5 on a 2× device, 0.5625 of it); Ui::stage_state(key) says whether a stage is slow and how many times it has drawn. Acceptance: tests/stage.rs (with 40 ms added to a stage's draw, a 2 s drag of a slider beside it at 60 Hz, with input coalesced or not, moves the knob and changes the value in every one of the 120 frames, every frame that does not draw the stage takes under 16.7 ms, the stage draws at most once per hold during the drag (the count is printed) and on the first frame after the release; a stage that draws in time draws every frame of a drag; a held stage asks for a frame and draws on the first frame without input); tests/stage_step.rs (a stage that steps alone for 150 frames is viewed alone with no layout, and every frame's instances, owners, held text and boxes are those of a page viewed, laid out and painted whole, with a count beside the stage marked El::steps viewed with it; a step that makes the stage taller lays the page out; a stage whose messages are its own, dragged for 30 frames, is restaged in each with at most one view and one layout in all, its chip where a whole layout puts it). tests/stage_scale.rs (a stage costing 24 ms at 2 and by its pixels below, on a 60 Hz display, settles at 1.5 within 4 s and changes at most 3 more times in 60 s; one whose level up would fit by its pixels but misses there comes down within 5 s and holds at 1.5; one at 59 % of the frame at 1 never steps up; one heavy for 5 s of every 20 steps up twice in 120 s and then stays down; no step up while a pointer is down; at 1.5 on a 2× device, every pixel outside the stage and under a tip drawn over it is the one at the device's scale, and the stage's are not; the governor stepping down twice and back up shades only the stages again, each frame the frame drawn whole at that scale, and the frame after shades nothing). A step of the stages' scale is not a whole frame: the stages are shaded again where they are (their boxes among the shade boxes, in the reduced pass and the filter up), the rest is kept. On the website's Lab index at 1440×900 2× with one cell running, a frame takes 2.9 ms median and 3.1 ms p95 on the CPU, from 6.9 ms.

A page of thousands of small glyphs (the Lab's Loupe: a source file at 2.75 px, about 20,000 glyphs) costs as many instances every frame it is drawn. El::cached() draws such a subtree once and keeps it. A cached element is a plate ( §1.33 , fade_s 0, with its limits and its rules: a picture, not content; it clips its children). When the page is painted, its subtree's instances are hashed. Equal to what the plate holds, and the plate not emptied this frame, they are dropped from the scene: the plate's span is empty and the plate lays on what it kept, so the frame costs no instances for it. Different, they replace what the plate holds where the frame draws ( PlateSpan::replace ), once: a frame drawn whole empties the plate and draws them onto it; a partial frame ( §1.19 ) empties and inks the plate only within its stage-1 boxes, before stage 1, so a cached_view of it reads it inked. A restage that copies the subtree from the last paint with nothing in it leaves it as it was. (With fade_s above 0 the plate is emptied and drawn onto.) To the dirty region a plate laid on from what it holds counts as the instances it holds (the renderer keeps them as they were last inked), so a frame that inks it again is compared with what it held, as any other instances are. A scroll that moves the last frame ( dirty::Move ) moves the plate's ink and near images the same way when what it holds, in this frame and the last, is the content's (clipped by the viewport): the plate then has only the band scrolled into view, the edges and the boxes of what changed in it inked. When part of it is the content's and part lies over the viewport (a plate across a scroll area's edge), the frame is drawn whole ("plate across a viewport"). A cached_view of a plate inked this frame is drawn again where it is ( tests/plate_scroll.rs : a cached sheet in a scroll area, scrolled down and up while a line in it changes, is the frame drawn whole byte for byte, and stage 1 draws under half the window). A paint in which nothing the subtree draws from changed passes it by: it is neither drawn nor hashed ( Counters::kept ), the plate's span is empty, and what it drew besides its instances (its identities' and texts' births, its texts' recomposition records and laid glyphs) is what it last drew. What it draws from is its nodes (key, box, clip, text and its type, fill, border, looseness, opacity, material) and what its ancestors give it (scale, a press held, the modal layer, the look's timing). Something it reads that its nodes cannot tell the same is never passed by and is compared as above: a morph or flow on the page, faces changing, and in it a drawing, a picture, a 3D view, a stage, posed, selected or composing text, a caret, a see-through group, something hidden, turned, at its own size, under a view scale, that stirs, sheds, traces or wipes, or that is pressed, focused, recomposing or decoding ( tests/cached.rs ). So it is drawn again whenever what it draws changes: it scrolls or moves (into the plate where the frame draws: a scroll inks its band), it loosens (a front passing, its birth), its words change, the window changes size (which empties every plate). A stage, a 3D view or a see-through group inside it is drawn with the rest, each time the rest is. Text in a pixel face asked for under its native size inside a cached element (Departure Mono at 2.75 px) is set and drawn at the size asked, as its outline's coverage at that size (a box filter of the native raster), not at its native size as anywhere else ( §1.6 ), so the small page is laid out as asked and does not overlap itself: its faces carry text::FINE . At its native size and above it is a pixel face as anywhere. A plate is the renderer's. A renderer that meets a cached element drawing nothing into a plate it has not inked (one made after the page was painted, offscreen) has it drawn again ( Ui::plates_lost ), and sends the whole glyph atlas on its first frame. Each paint's ink goes into a plate once ( Scene::paint ), so the scene drawn again (no paint between) lays on what the plate holds. el::cached_view(over, from, ink) shows the part from (logical px on the page: x, y, w, h) of what the cached element over drew, scaled to its own box. Each pixel of the plate's ink is read as its coverage (alpha), nearest, and drawn as a glyph's coverage in ink : at a whole zoom each source pixel is a square of whole pixels, and the material draws it as text. It is one instance ( Instance::cached_slot : its coordinates are packed below −1 with the slot; its batch, scene::CACHED_BATCH + slot, binds the plate's ink where a glyph's atlas would be). It draws nothing before the cached element has drawn once in this window, or inside the cached element itself. A cached element over the plates' limit (a fifth, or past twice the window's area) is drawn as a plain one and has no kept image, so a cached_view of it draws nothing. The state can know: Ui::on_kept(f) tells it a cached element's key and false when a paint finds it so, and true when it has a kept image again or goes while it had none ( Ui::kept_image(key) reads it). The paint that finds the change asks for the next frame; the state is told there (or straight after a paint run by a message or a relayout) and the page is viewed again, so what the view does instead (the Loupe's glass shows only its rim, ×1) is a cut on that frame, both ways. El::clip_round(radius) clips the subtree to the box inside the border with round corners (half the side: a circle). The radius rides in each instance's look[3] above its in-place flag (twice the radius in quarter device px); the ink stage discards past half a pixel outside and antialiases the edge. A square clip inside it that cuts it is square; a clip around it that cuts it keeps its own straight edge. Presses are still taken anywhere in the box. Acceptance: tests/cached.rs (a cached page drawn the first frame as without caching, then laid on with no instances of its own while something else changes and the same as uncached; a frame with nothing new identical; drawn again when its words change, with no old ink; after a new window size as uncached; a cached view at ×4 inside a round clip of radius 40: every source pixel a 4 × 4 square of one colour, with ink, and the box's corners outside the circle as the page without it; a page pushed over the limit, by area and by count, told it has no kept image and viewed again, then told it has one when back under or gone).

Button, number control, text field, switch, slider, tabs, choices ( choice and the segmented segmented ), list, card, dialog, image, divider, scroll area, and the rest listed in registry.json . Components are plain functions returning El<M> . Like shadcn, they are distributed as source: one file per component ( src/widgets/ ), and registry.json at the repository root lists each component's name, title, description, files and the other components it depends on (all depend on base , the shared sizes in src/widgets/mod.rs ; the slider depends on the number control's Spec , the dialog on the button). Users copy the source and change it. The tree a component returns can be resized further with El methods ( .height , .pad , .radius , .border , .disabled ). Buttons come in three variants: default (outlined), quiet (no border) and accent (accent fill with text in the page background colour); unavailable is .disabled(true) .

A theme is data: colours, type scale, spacing, line widths, corner radii. The current Theme : the background (possibly a top-to-bottom gradient from ground to ground2 ), ink, three accents ( Paint::hue(0/1/2) ), which face each of the display, body and mono roles uses, the type scale (heading, subheading, body, small) and thin and thick line widths. There are fifteen: dark, light, pixel, and each style's own (Loose Thread has a black and a paper set: THREAD , THREAD_PAPER ). style::THEME_IDS are their ASCII names, matching THEMES one to one. The root sets .fonts(theme.roles()) , and text elements use roles ( Font::Display / Body / Mono ) or a face directly. The greys ( Theme::greys ) are opaque colours of the theme's own between its ground and its ink: raised (surfaces off the ground: a stage, a preview box), hairline (card frames, rules, dividers, control outlines at rest), dim (labels, numbers, hints, descriptions) and text (prose, idle control labels). Paint::RAISED , HAIRLINE ( FAINT ), DIM and TEXT stand at fixed tones (20, 51, 168 and 219 of 255, so the ink image holds them exactly) and are drawn as those colours exactly; a tone between two is drawn straight between their colours ( Theme::grey , the shaders' grey ), so a grey is never the ink at an alpha. A theme without greys of its own takes Greys::mixed (the plain mixes of ground and ink at those tones), or Greys::mixed_dim(ground, ink, 4.5) , the same with dim taken toward the ink as little as it takes to stand 4.5:1 from the ground; a theme made from another with its own ground and ink sets them ( greys: Greys::mixed(ground, ink) ), or it keeps the other's. The extreme ( Paint::EXTREME , Theme::extreme ) is white on a dark scheme and black on a light one: past the ink, for what the pointer is over. In the ink image it is a fourth hue code (0.45; the code the glyph heights once took, which nothing wrote). The default theme ( DARK , LIGHT ) takes the AA.9 table: ground #1a1b1d / #f1f0eb , raised #232528 / #e6e5df , hairline #383b40 / #cbc9c1 , dim #989da4 / #5f6266 , text #d6d8d4 / #2b2c2e , ink #f2f2ee / #141517 , accent #f47a3c / #b23f0d , second #7db0f7 / #1a5cc7 , third (the warning colour) #f2c94c / #7d5c00 . Its controls rest in ink on the ground: a primary button ( Variant::Primary , one in each group of actions) is an ink plate with a ground label that turns to the extreme under the pointer; a switch that is on is an ink track with a ground knob (off: a hairline track, a dim knob); a slider's run and thumb are ink, the rest of the run hairline; a radio's dot, a checkbox's tick and outline, a pressed toggle and the current option of a choice are ink (a toggle, an option and the current page of a pagination as an ink plate with a ground label), as are a current tab's rule, a progress bar's fill and the label of a selected list row or menu option; a selected or keyed row's plate ( widgets::SELECTED ) is the raised grey, not a tint of the accent, and the hairline grey on a surface that is itself raised ( widgets::selected_on ); a hot menu row (command, context and nested menus) is that plate with an ink label, and a skip link an ink plate with a ground label. Menus, selects, context and nested menus and the sheets (sheet, bottom sheet) are raised: the raised grey in a hairline frame ( widgets::MENU_SURFACE ), so their selected and hot rows are the hairline grey; a popover stays on the ground. The hover and focus marks are ink. Outlines of interactive controls (a default button, an input, a number, a select or menu button, a checkbox, a radio, a choice, a toggle, a page of a pagination) are dim at rest and ink under the pointer or with focus ( El::border_hover ), and ink while a select or menu is open or a number is typed into; the hairline grey is for card frames, rules, dividers and the outer frame of a group (panels, dialogs, sheets, popovers, toasts, tooltips, menus). The accent is for what is held or dragged (a slider's thumb, a switch's knob while pressed), a number's caret, a dot chart's dot under the pointer and its control points while dragged, and the explicit Variant::Accent . Categories (an avatar's people, a chart's series) are told apart by ink, dim and text ( widgets::SHADES ), and by shape where three are not enough; second and warn are not category colours. The framework's examples follow the same rule: a main action is Variant::Primary , and the accent is only in a named Accent or colour specimen or on what is held or dragged. Paints that answer the pointer ( El::fill_hover , El::fill_held , El::border_hover ): an element's fill while the pointer is over it or the control it is part of (the nearest pressable element at or above it), and while that is pressed or dragged; its border while the pointer is over it or it, or the control it is part of, has focus. Each falls back to the paint at rest (held to the hover fill under the pointer). The page is painted again when what they answer changes; a cached subtree with one is drawn every time. A material is how the shading stage draws. Annotation is whether the third pass is on and what it draws. A style preset ( style::Style , plain data; style::styles() gives ten) is: a theme, a material, that material's parameters, annotation settings, a looseness scale (Normcore's is 0.3), the text lattice pitch, and the Markr for pictures on the style page. The top bar's Style menu sets all of them at once, after which the theme and material menus work as usual; switching is a commit that spreads from the press. Opening a style page applies it too (its side rail item is a commit). The table is the design intent; the actual presets are in styles() : Preset Theme Material Annotation How Neo-Dotmatrix Black, monochrome dottr off A global dot lattice; loosened, each dot's size is the ink beneath it Lo-Fi Print Paper, two inks smudgr off Halftone dots, misregistration, paper grain, ink bleed (thresholding the SDF) Glitch Black glitchr off Band slips, channel separation, block displacement, holding the last frame Metamorphosis Linocut Paper, monochrome carvr off Ink = a threshold of SDF + noise , edges like knife cuts; white cut along iso-lines; interpolating two states' SDFs is the morph Algorithmic / Digital Gaze Black, monospace any on: boxes, numbers, confidence-style labels, tracking lines The annotation layer Tech-Manual Grid paper, black + one signal colour plain + hatched fills on: leaders, numbers, dimension lines Another way of drawing the annotation layer Normcore System grey, default sizes plain off Only a theme Cyberminimalism Near black, hairlines, monospace plain off Only a theme Bauhaus Primary colours, geometric shapes plain off A theme plus geometric shape components Loose Thread White thread on pure black (or black on paper), one accent scribblr hover: EDGE , FRAME At rest: small type, a picture and a drawn tangle; headings that are touched come apart into thread ( §4.4 ) The plain material also goes through two-stage drawing; it just doesn't loosen. Waves, condensing and corner marks are still there.

preset::Preset (serde, to_json / from_json ): a name, the theme (by name) and its three faces, the material and its 8 numbers, annotation, the looseness scale, the lattice pitch, the pictures' Markr , an interaction character ( Interaction : press feedback duration, front speed / width / lifetime, the default responses of text and controls and of everything else, recomposition parameters) and a transition ( Transition { duration_ms, steps: [Step; 4] } ). Preset::apply(&Look) gives the look ( Look::press_ms , Look::roles and Look::transition are new); the runtime uses roles to decide how elements without a response respond and press_ms for the press burst. Preset::numbers() lists every number by its JSON path ( transition.steps.0.a ) and set_number(path, value) changes it: the website's number controls are generated from the data. A transition is a small program : up to four steps, each with a kind, a start and end within the transition time (0–1) and five numbers; the material's last step composites by it between the old picture (what was on screen at the moment of the commit) and the new: how much of the new shows here, where each side samples from, what colour is laid over, how far the old fades toward the ground, how far channels separate. Kinds: reveal (circle, line, row by row, shuffled cells, a torn line; row by row, the rows just swept show only lattice dots), slipping bands (each band shifts, channels separate, a few hard cuts, then lock), fade (with a little displacement), light bar (a photocopier: the new page behind the bar, toner noise settling with distance), colour blocks (a few rows of flat theme colour slide from left to right, revealing the new page), loosen (the whole page loosens by its material, computed on the CPU into rip.y ), layers (separating nearer the brighter, swapping, closing), detection boxes (the largest few elements are boxed in reading order, the box drawn along its edges, and the inside swapped for the new), carve (the old fades to the ground, knife cuts grow on both sides of the new outline, then ink floods in), outline first (outlines and boxes are drawn first in reading order, the content filled in after), torn reveal (torn along a noisy line, the old layer sliding away offset) and crack ( StepKind::Crack , id 11; numbers preset::CRACK : cell size 120 px, angle 70°, bias 0.6, waver 2 px, hard edge 1): the page breaks along the edges of a Voronoi tiling turned by the angle and squashed across it by the bias. The cracks run out from where the commit was pressed (the page's centre without one): a pixel's crack is drawn once the run (0 to the page's diagonal over the first 0.4 of the step) has passed it, and the cracks stay thin, from 0.6 px to 0.06 a (7 px) at 0.4, measured in page px whichever way they run. Their edges are straight but for a slow waver ( d px every a / 5 px). Then each piece leaves whole at its own time t = 0.28 + 0.6 × (0.6 × distance from the press ÷ the farthest corner's + 0.4 × the piece's hash) : between t and t + 0.15 its own crack widens (slowly, then fast: the fourth power) until it covers the piece, so at any moment most pieces are whole or gone. (Against the farthest corner rather than the diagonal, so the last pieces leave at the step's end wherever the press was.) Inside a commit's scope ( El::commit_scope ) the Crack is measured against the scope's box: pieces of clamp(short side ÷ 3.5, 16, a) px, the cracks' width ( 0.06 × that, at least 1 px) and waver (every fifth of it) with them, the run over the box's diagonal and the distance against the box's farthest corner from the press; and the step takes clamp(box diagonal ÷ page diagonal, 0.5, 1) of its time ( Split::span ). Without a scope the bytes are as before. The preset recipe's Crack button commits the tech-manual look through an 800 ms crack ( tests/transition.rs : the last frame is the new page drawn directly, a tenth of the way in under a tenth of it shows, what shows only grows, the same numbers give the same bytes; at 0.2 nothing of the new page shows farther than 0.6 diagonals from the press; at 0.3 under 12 % shows; at 0.6 at most a quarter of the pieces are between 15 % and 85 % gone). During a masked transition every pixel is one page's whole colour (ground, ink and edge together); no element blends its own colours between the two themes, and render --frames <the transition> --audit finds no P0 in any frame. The ten presets' transitions ( presets() , all ≤ 900 ms): Gaze detection boxes; Dotmatrix row-by-row lattice; Lo-Fi Print light bar; Glitch slipping bands with three hard cuts and then lock; Linocut carve; Tech-Manual outline first with boxes; Normcore none (0 ms); Cyberminimalism a 120 ms fade with 6 px displacement; Bauhaus colour blocks; Loose Thread 700 ms: loosen first (the whole page into thread, 0–0.55), then outline first (0.45–1). scribblr 's thread is computed on the CPU, so the loosen step is computed once more on the CPU ( Transition::loosen , the same function as the material pass), and text to read still goes only to legible_cap . Where they are used : switching to a style (the top bar menu, a style page's side rail item, a scene) and entering a style's page are commits ( §1.5 ) using the target style's transition (the look is already the new one after the commit). Interruptible : the commit's before is the picture on screen at that moment (the frame the renderer keeps, §1.19 ), so switching again mid-transition continues from how it looked then toward the new target; input stays available throughout. The frame where the transition ends (time ≥ 1) is the new picture directly, without the program. A look without a transition ( duration_ms 0) uses the original front spreading from the press. The page : #styles (style switching): from / to choices (choosing "from" applies it at once), Play (a commit), every number of the target style's interaction and transition (number controls generated from the data), and JSON export / import (a multi-line field that can be copied and pasted). Acceptance : unit tests in preset.rs (JSON round trip, number paths, ≤ 900 ms); check item 16: for every preset, the frame after the transition ends is byte-identical to the same page drawn directly with the target preset (the material clock aligned to the transition's side), and mid-transition and both ends differ (except Normcore); samples samples <dir> transitions (6 frames per transition, one row each).

Tracking : El::tracking(em) , −0.05–1.5, 0 by default, laid out by parley ( text::Setting { around, track } ), so measured widths, selection, recomposition and scribblr 's outlines follow it. Quiet type : Font::Whisper is a fixed face, not a theme role: Source Serif 4 at its 8 pt optical size and weight 400, Latin only (82 KB, OFL, assets/licenses/source-serif ; text::SERIF ). El::whisper() makes the text lowercase, in this face, with 0.6 em tracking; the size is set by the caller, 11–13 px. There is no Chinese serif: in demos small type is Latin only, and Han characters fall back to the fallback face. Edge notes ( gaze::EDGE ): a one-device-pixel hairline at the scope's right edge, exactly on the scope rect's rightmost column; ticks every 10 / 50 / 100 px (3 / 6 / 9 px, inward), and a 14 px mark at the pointer's height. To the line's left, a few lines of small type set vertically, read bottom to top (turned 90° counter-clockwise), in the serif at 12 px with 0.12 em tracking and 18 px between lines, starting a new column to the left when they don't fit and never leaving the scope. They all state current values: the scope's width × height, the pointer's coordinates in the scope ( x — y — when it isn't there), the material and theme ( THEME_IDS names), how loose the loosest instance is right now (by Ui::looseness 's rule) and the number of non-zero nodes in the field map. Turned text: each glyph instance turns about its own center ( xf = [−1, 1, −1, −1] ), the center moved to its place on the turned line; widths and heights are integers, so after turning glyphs still land on whole pixels and are not resampled. Acceptance: edge_notes_say_what_is_true_now in tests/gaze.rs : every line equals the runtime's current value (scope, pointer, material and theme, looseness("root") , fieldmap().nonzero() ), the hairline is at the scope's right edge, and every line is inside the scope without overlapping. check item 7.2 ( dottr and plain at 1×, plain at 2×): the hairline is every row of the scope's last column, not the column outside, one device pixel wide between ticks; every pixel of the type is a mix between ground and annotation colour (within 2/255 under plain ), each line has full-colour pixels, and over 30% of its ink is solid (coverage > 0.6). Item 7.3: at 1920 × 1080 and scale 1, over 30% of each edge note's ink is solid (currently at least 42%).

The field map ( §1.29 ) is how disturbed the page is right now, so it is read like an instrument; no audio is involved. ** OSC **: a line across the scope (stopping 40 px from the right edge when edge notes are on, so it doesn't cover them). One point per column of map nodes: x is that column's position, and the height is that column's energy in some row (the quantized byte, as the shader reads it) times osc_amp , upward from the baseline scope top + height × osc_y . The row is the pointer's row, or the row with the most energy when the pointer isn't in the scope ( FieldMap::strongest_row ). It is drawn as a one-device-pixel polyline without anti-aliasing: each device column gets one vertical run of whole pixels covering the heights where the line enters and leaves that column, so the colour is exactly the annotation colour, never mixed with the material beneath. ** LEVEL **: a 6 px vertical bar at the scope's left edge, rising from the bottom to scope height × min(1, mean energy / level_full) ( gaze::level_height , the mean energy being FieldMap::level ). Numbers (in Gaze , with number controls on the website's annotation page): osc_amp 4–120 px, default 40; osc_y 0–1, default 0.5; level_full 0.01–0.5, default 0.08. With the map at 0 the waveform is flat and the level bar 0 high, and no frames are wanted (no frames while the map is still; the readouts ask for none of their own). The exported tree's root gains field: { level, nonzero } . Acceptance: the_waveform_and_the_level_read_the_field_map in tests/gaze.rs : with the map at 0 every point is on the baseline, the level is 0 and two seconds draw 0 frames; after a stir at x, the highest point is within a cell of x and rises above the baseline by the energy there times osc_amp (within 1 px), reading the row with the most energy; the level bar equals the formula, and export_tree().field.level equals what was drawn; once the map settles both are flat again. check item 7.2: in every device column away from the baseline the annotation colour is one continuous run, exactly one device pixel where flat, with no annotation colour mixed into the pixels next to it; the level bar's height equals the readout (±1 px); control: after a stir the waveform is not flat.

The pieces above, combined into the tenth preset. Item Value Theme THREAD (pure black ground, white ink, one accent [1.0, 0.33, 0.20] , the other two accents being the ink), or THREAD_PAPER (paper white ground, near-black ink). The accent is the annotation colour and appears only where the pointer touches Material scribblr Type Headings and body as usual; small type with El::whisper() Annotation Hover, EDGE and FRAME Interaction Text loosens by default too ( roles gives text Loosen ); text to read doesn't become thread or move under scribblr ( §1.30 ) Field map stirr 1.0, meander 0.5, creep 0.15, energy_life 2.0, bleed 0.06, breath 0 (when the pointer sweeps a heading not meant for reading, its looseness passes 0.8, is still over 0.3 a second later, and returns to 0 within three seconds) Hold beat 240.96 bpm, 3 steps (an 83 ms step) Transition 700 ms: Loosen (0–0.55) then Outline (0.45–1) Finishing Off by default; the style page can turn on black and white only ( binary ) and invert ( invert ) The style page ( #style-loose-thread ) is a real piece, English only within its scope whatever the interface language ( Locale::En.tr , with thread.* only in the English catalog): a line of quiet type at the top, amenui — no. 10 ; the title loose thread in Font::Whisper at 30 px, lowercase, 0.3 em tracking; a picture with the caption fig. 1 ; a sentence of 14 px body text on the right; and a footer line of quiet type that is three controls (a two-option radio black · paper and two switches, 1-bit and invert ), the selected one in the accent, drawn without switches or borders but reachable by keyboard and in the accessibility mirror as a radio group, radios and switches. 72 px on the right are left for edge notes. The page has a drawn tangle as content: a knot of radius 70 at the picture's bottom right (one corner of the knot behind the picture) and a line passing through it from the top of the page to above the footer, 1 px in ink, never covering text to read ( El::trace , with points from strand::figure on a fixed seed); it draws in over 700 ms on entering the page, then rests and wants no frames; it draws under every material, so rule 3 is unaffected, and the map's flow pushes it a little and lets it return as the pointer passes ( pull 2.5). As the pointer moves over the composition, a 1 px point following the pointer stirs the map ( El::stirr , radius 72), so thread appears only where touched; the title is set as text not for reading ( legible(false) ) and comes apart into a single thread with knots and two tails; body text and controls stay. Narrow windows have no tangle. Samples craft <dir> loose-thread and craft <dir> thread-ref . Acceptance: the unit tests in preset.rs and check item 16 (every preset's end frame equals drawing it directly) include it automatically. the_loose_thread_page_loosens_its_title_all_the_way_and_text_to_read_holds in tests/strand.rs : at rest there is no thread and two seconds draw 0 frames, the tangle is at least 80% of the scope's height and enters no box of text to read; after the pointer sweeps the title its looseness is at least 0.8, with two tails (the end tail's ends at least 300 × k apart, the start tail at least half as long), every point of the thread inside the scope, and the tails entering no box of text to read; a second after the pointer leaves it is at least 0.3, and at three seconds 0, with no thread and no frames wanted; throughout, no thread belongs to an element for reading, and the glyphs to read keep their rest positions and opacity one by one. loose_thread_shows_no_chinese_in_either_language in tests/i18n.rs : under both interface languages the text and names in the scope are the same with no Han character, the title is lowercase in text::SERIF , and the three controls have their roles and are reachable by keyboard. corner_marks_never_lie_on_ink in tests/gaze.rs : with the pointer resting on the small type, the title, the picture, the body text and the two switches, no pixel of a corner mark falls in any glyph's box (corner marks are 6 px outside the element rect). check item 20.6: with binary the read-back frame has only two colours; text and thread are thresholded by coverage (coverage of at least half is ink, however bright its colour; a very faint fill is still ground), pictures get a two-level 4 × 4 ordered dither (by the square root along the ground-to-ink range, so dark pictures keep their midtones on a dark ground), and the annotation layer uses the same coverage rule; for every glyph of body text, small type and control labels and every edge note, the inked pixel counts with and without it (without, a pixel counts when at least halfway from the ground to its fullest colour) differ by at most a fifth, and ink takes 20% to 80% of the picture. Item 20.7: with invert every pixel is 255 − value of the original (within 1, currently 0), and turned off it is byte-identical to the original; together with binary there are still only two colours.

Written with the framework itself, it is an application and the web version's main page. It now lives in the website repository ↗ ( src/gallery/ ): Top bar: the name amenui on the left; on the right the theme, material and style menus ( menu : the button shows the current item, and pressing it lists them all in a layer below; El::anchor places the list under the button) and Reset. Menu items are commits ( §1.5 ), spreading from the item pressed. A 220 logical px side rail in eight groups: components, marks (one page per mark set), materials (one page each: a fixed sample of a heading, a paragraph, a picture, a row of controls, a card and a few shapes, with looseness that can be fixed by number, every material parameter, and a Ripple button that sends a front), annotation (mode, kinds, density and draw time acting on an example), styles (one page per preset), transforms, type, and scenes (the list and seven scenes, §6 ). Below 720 px wide, the side rail becomes a horizontally scrolling row of tabs under the top bar. One page per component, top to bottom: the title (display size) and the function to call; one sentence on what it does; a preview (the live component on the page background with generous space around it); variants (one cell per variant and state, wrapping, with a faint caption under each); parameters (the component's own numbers, changed with number controls); and the source (the component's file via include_str! , in the mono face with faint line numbers, in a scroll area, long lines wrapping under their own line number). Mark pages: a picture in this mark set with a compare line, every number of Markr editable, and a choice of picture. One page per style preset, each a small composition of its own rather than the same sample in other colours: Gaze is a stream of boxed, measured pictures (filterable); Dotmatrix a departure board ticking every second; Lo-Fi Print a zine page; Glitch a title card that slips as you pass and a row of controls; Linocut a carved headline, a sun and a picture printed in strokes; Tech-Manual an exploded view and a parts list, where the pointer on a row marks the matching part in the drawing and the other way round (the runtime tells the state about hover with Ui::on_hover , and about keyboard focus with Ui::on_focus ); Normcore a settings form; Cyberminimalism a command line and its filtered results; Bauhaus a geometric poster and a set of controls that change it. Every page has real interaction; a press sends a front, showing how the style loosens.

A line of small mono type under a live demo ( widgets::caption , El::caption_params(key, formula, params, msg) ) that prints the real parameters driving the demo: the line is formatted from the same fields the demo reads, never written by hand, and each parameter below it is a small number control ( number scaled to 0.8) that changes that field. The website's interaction pages (bottom sheet, floating box, nested menu, loading, card stack, dot chart) have one each, and every cell of the Lab works this way ( §5.3 ).

#lab : small experiments that each do one thing, each a file in the website's examples/lab/ , written only against the public interface ( experiment::Experiment : view, update, step, whether the next frame is wanted). The look is one theme ( style::LAB ): a near-black ground, grey-white hairlines and dots, and a single blue that appears only where the pointer touches or has an effect; all type is the mono pixel face. The page should read as a wall of living pieces, not a form with small pictures: each cell has [ name ] at the top left and a one-line hint at the top right; in the middle the stage ( experiment::STAGE , height : width = 3 : 4, clipped), which the piece fills, taking over 70% of the cell's height (drawings use 240 × 180 coordinates; text pieces are placed by the stage's width and height); below it one line of formula (mono, unwrapped, cut off when too long) whose numbers are the values driving it now; and at the bottom a small label on the left and [ params ] on the right, which opens the cell's number controls only when pressed (scaled to 0.72, Params::open , toggled by the message at index experiment::TOGGLE ), with no sliders. Cells are laid out in columns of at least 340 px, one column in narrow windows. Ten cells: lit text (a block of small mono type filling the stage, under a soft light), contours, silk (each mark a short line segment along the flow, long when fast and short when slow, so it looks like flowing silk), grown (f 0.029, k 0.057, maze stripes on 120 × 90, dots sized by concentration; every T seconds it changes shape by itself: a letter → a switch → a rounded square, the old pattern decoding away as the new one decodes in), mercury, text on a path (four lines along waves of their own phase), text on a sphere (the sphere fills the stage, the back showing through, dark and reversed), orbits, a spring and the card stack (lab-style cards: faces close to the ground with thin outlines, the one under the pointer in the accent); each experiment also has a page ( #lab-<name> , the website's docs/site/<lang>/lab-<name>.md : the formula and a table of parameters). Wherever the pointer touches, that one blue appears: lit text, bent contours, stirred silk, sown seeds, a held ball, a stretch of text pulled into a curve, the text under the pointer on the sphere, attracted points, the held spring, the card under the pointer. Living cells (an explicit exception to "every page comes to rest", §0 rule 3) : Lab cells step every frame while they can be seen ( El::on_visible ) and stop when scrolled out of view, so the Lab page never rests; their marks all come from the one frame budget ( §1.27 ) and shrink in proportion when there are too many; when frames exceed the budget ( budget::usage().scale < 1), only that proportion of the visible cells step each frame ( Lab::turn ), so the page's cost falls with it. When the viewer asks for reduced motion (the web's prefers-reduced-motion , set_reduced_motion ; Lab::reduced ) the original rule returns: cells step for experiment::IDLE_S (1.2 s) after arriving on the page or after the last input, then only those still finishing (springs, coasting, points following the pointer) continue, and then the whole page rests and wants no frames. Acceptance: the_labs_pieces_run_while_seen_and_stop_when_scrolled_out in tests/frames.rs (frames wanted while seen, none when scrolled out, at rest with reduced motion) and every_page_comes_to_rest (the Lab included, with reduced motion).

The gallery is organized as a documentation site after shadcn/ui (the website's src/gallery/docs.rs ).
