amenui is a self-drawn interface framework in Rust (wgpu; the same code runs natively and on the web). Everything on screen — glyphs, shapes, pictures — is an instance with a true outline that can loosen, morph and condense again; how it looks is a swappable material. You write a view (state → tree) and an update (state, message → state); the runtime does layout, input, animation and drawing.

view(&state) → El tree → layout (taffy + parley) → instances (glyph / shape / picture) → stage 1: ink + near images (true outlines) → stage 2: material → stage 3: annotation layer input → hit → message → update(&mut state) → view again input → field (fronts, lens) There is one way to make things move: events put things in the field (a front from a press, the lens), and commands ask the runtime ( Cmd::Morph , Cmd::Flow ). Widgets never animate themselves.

Every block below is compiled by cargo test (this file is a doc-test of amenui::agents ). A view and an update (Elm style; messages are plain values): use amenui::el::{El, Paint, col, text}; use amenui::widgets::button; #[derive(Clone)] enum Msg { Inc } struct S { n: u32 } fn view(s: &S) -> El<Msg> { col().pad( 24.0 , 24.0 ).gap( 12.0 ) .child(text(format!( "{}" , s.n), 32.0 , Paint::INK).key( "count" )) .child(button( "inc" , "Add one" , Msg::Inc)) } fn update(s: &mut S, m: Msg) { match m { Msg::Inc => s.n += 1 } } let _ = (view(&S { n: 0 }), update as fn(&mut S, Msg)); A runtime, headless (tests, tools); press by position, read the tree: # use amenui::el::{El, Paint, col, text}; use amenui::widgets::button; # #[derive(Clone)] enum Msg { Inc } struct S { n: u32 } # fn view(s: &S) -> El<Msg> { col().child(text(s.n.to_string(), 20.0 , Paint::INK).key( "count" )).child(button( "inc" , "+" , Msg::Inc)) } # fn update(s: &mut S, _: Msg) { s.n += 1 } let faces = amenui::text::embedded(); let mut ui = amenui::ui::Ui::new(S { n: 0 }, view, update, faces, 400 , 300 , 1.0 ); let (x, y) = ui.node( "inc" ).unwrap().rect.center(); ui.press(x, y); ui.release(x, y); assert_eq!(ui.export_tree().find( "count" ).unwrap().text.as_deref(), Some( "1" )); Layout: rows, columns, sizes, gaps, padding (logical px; nothing shrinks unless asked): use amenui::el::{El, Paint, row, col, space, text}; let bar: El<()> = row().fill_width().pad( 16.0 , 8.0 ).gap( 12.0 ) .child(text( "Title" , 18.0 , Paint::INK).grow( 1.0 )) .child(space( 80.0 , 30.0 ).radius( 4.0 ).fill(Paint::ACCENT)); let page: El<()> = col().fill_width().fill_height().child(bar).child(col().grow( 1.0 ).scroll()); let _ = page; Keys: give every element you will look up, animate, or that holds state a stable key: use amenui::el::{El, Paint, col, text}; let rows: El<()> = ( 0 .. 3 ).fold(col(), |c, i| c.child(text(format!( "Row {i}" ), 14.0 , Paint::TEXT).key(format!( "row/{i}" )))); let _ = rows; Numbers are number controls, never sliders as the main way (Draft while typing, Set on commit): use amenui::el::El; use amenui::widgets::{Edit, Spec, number}; #[derive(Clone)] enum Msg { Width(Edit) } const W: Spec = Spec { min: 0.0 , max: 64.0 , step: 1.0 , decimals: 0 , unit: "px" }; let draft: Option<String> = None; let n: El<Msg> = number( "width" , "Width" , 12.0 , W, draft.as_deref(), Msg::Width).width( 320.0 ); let _ = n; Text fields keep a TextEdit in the state: use amenui::el::El; use amenui::widgets::{TextEdit, input}; #[derive(Clone)] enum Msg { Name(TextEdit) } let name = TextEdit::new( "Lin" ); let field: El<Msg> = input( "name" , &name, "Name" , 280.0 , 40 , Msg::Name); let _ = field; Ripples: a press reaches only its own control unless you say more; decide what loosens: use amenui::el::{El, Paint, Response, Scope, row, space}; use amenui::widgets::button; let area: El<()> = row().key( "area" ).ripplr_scope().gap( 16.0 ) .child(button( "go" , "Press" , ()).ripplr(Scope::Container(None))) .child(space( 60.0 , 40.0 ).fill(Paint::ACCENT).respond(Response::Loosen)) .child(space( 60.0 , 40.0 ).fill(Paint::hue( 1 )).respond(Response::Ignore)); let _ = area; Commands for what moves: keep them in the state, hand them over with on_commands : use amenui::morph::{Cmd, FlowSpec, MorphSpec}; let mut cmds: Vec<Cmd> = vec![]; cmds.push(Cmd::Morph { from: "a" .into(), to: "b" .into(), spec: MorphSpec::default() }); cmds.push(Cmd::Flow(FlowSpec::default())); // before a page change: shared `.flow(id)` parts move cmds.push(Cmd::Press { key: "go" .into() }); // press an element as a person would (not counted as input) cmds.push(Cmd::Commit { x: 400.0 , y: 300.0 , scope: None }); // keep the frame, play the new look's transition from here cmds.push(Cmd::Focus { key: "go" .into() }); // focus an element after this layout cmds.push(Cmd::Scrub(Some( 0.5 ))); // hold the morph in progress half way (None: let it go on) assert_eq!(cmds.len(), 6 ); Materials and the look: one global material, overrides per subtree: use amenui::el::{El, Paint, text}; use amenui::style::{Look, Material, LIGHT}; let look = Look { theme: LIGHT, material: Material::Dottr, legible_cap: 0.15 , ..Look::default() }; let card: El<()> = text( "Halftone" , 20.0 , Paint::INK).material(Material::Halftonr.id()); let _ = (look, card); Content that changes recomposes when it is keyed; turn it off where it must be immediate: use amenui::el::{El, Paint, text}; let count: El<()> = text( "12" , 28.0 , Paint::INK).key( "count" ); // recomposes 12 → 13 let clock: El<()> = text( "09:41" , 14.0 , Paint::DIM).key( "clock" ).recompose(false); let _ = (count, clock);

use amenui::el::{El, Fit, Paint, Plate, col, text}; // A stage drawn at its own size and zoomed to fit the window (only shrinks, to a quarter at least). let stage: El<()> = col().key( "frame" ).fill_width().fill_height().fit(Fit::default()) .child(col().key( "stage" ).width( 1440.0 ).height( 900.0 )); // At most three lines, ending in the face's own ellipsis; `Ui::clamped("blurb")` says whether it was cut. let blurb: El<()> = text( "A long paragraph to read." , 14.0 , Paint::TEXT).key( "blurb" ).clamp( 3 ); // Ink that stays: what the board's subtree draws is kept, each pixel gone 4 s after it was last drawn. let board: El<()> = col().key( "board" ).fill_width().fill_height().plate(Plate { fade_s: 4.0 }); let _ = (stage, blurb, board); absolute(left, top, right, bottom) pins against the parent's padding box, never the window. A face that comes later: declare it ( text::with_declared , Ui::declare_face ), set text in it as usual, and add its bytes when they come ( Ui::add_face ); fetch what Ui::faces_wanted() lists. Text stands in meanwhile. Ui::clear_focus() / Cmd::ClearFocus after a route change; El::preview(true) to show a sheet or menu in place. Plates are for music videos, the lab and drawing boards, not ordinary pages; Cmd::ClearPlate { key } empties one. Put text to read and controls beside a plate (its siblings), never inside it: Ui::problems reports OnPlate . A clamped text copies what it shows, without the ellipsis; the accessibility tree has the whole text. Look::off.ground turns the field's dots (the ground's own marks) off.

A 3D object is one more element: el::mesh(MeshId::TORUS) or el::scene3d(Scene3d { items, camera, light, spec, picture }) , sized like any element. Meshes are generated in code ( MeshId::CUBE , ICO[0..4] , TORUS …; Ui::add_mesh , mesh::load_gltf ); MeshInstances { mesh, transforms, paint, id } draws many copies in one call. The global material draws it (its outline and creases are edges in the nearness). Hear the pointer with .on_pick(|Pick| ..) ( Pick::Hover / Pick::Press carry MeshHit { object, instance } ); turn it with widgets::orbit(key, scene, &state.orbit, Msg::Orbit) and call Orbit::update / Orbit::step (see docs/recipes/mesh.md ). Morphs with many tiles run on the GPU by themselves ( Look::particles.gpu_above ). A scene that changes into another with shared actors is a commit plus a flow ( docs/recipes/chapter.md ). Ui::on_pointer tells the state where the pointer is. A style preset is data: preset::presets() , change a number ( Preset::set_number("transition.steps.0.a", 3.0) ) or read JSON ( Preset::from_json ), then preset.apply(&look) ; a commit ( El::commit ) that applies it plays its transition ( docs/recipes/preset.md ). A preset's post is the finishing pass (bloom, chromatic offset, scanlines, grain, vignette, curvature, then a dither and a palette — amenui::post , all off by default, DESIGN.md §1.21 ) and its marks make marks on 3D elements follow depth. El::shed(Shed) makes a moving element drop marks, El::flow_field(FlowField) carries marks along a noise field over a box (speed 0: still), and El::shift(dx, dy) moves a subtree after layout (pointer parallax without a layout). Gestures are state ( amenui::gesture : Spring , Animated , RubberBand , project ): widgets::bottom_sheet and widgets::floating report drags, Sheet::update / Floating::update take them with the time, step runs on the tick while moving() ; put them after the page in el::layers([...]) (docs/recipes/gesture.md). Under a live demo, El::caption_params prints the numbers that drive it and lets them be edited (DESIGN.md §5.2 ). widgets::nested_menu steers submenus by a safe-zone triangle ( El::on_move hears the pointer over an element; El::guide draws an outline in the annotation layer). While data loads, draw the real rows with .skeleton() as widgets::Loading::show says (docs/recipes/loading.md). Fields and drawings (DESIGN.md §1.26 ): el::canvas(Drawing) draws dots and strokes in its own space (each a shape with a true outline; its pointer handlers get points in that space; El::on_point hears move, press-drag and leave in one handler); amenui::field samples noise, bumps and metaballs on a Grid , traces iso-contours, advects a Swarm along curl or a stirred Flow , and grows GrayScott inside a mask. A text element's glyphs can be posed one by one ( El::pose(|GlyphAt| Pose) : move, turn, scale, tone, alpha; no layout). El::on_visible says when an element can be seen (step a demo only then), El::on_outline sends a subtree's true outline as a coverage grid (a mask). Every small mark draws from one frame budget ( budget::grant(n) ). El::decode(Decode) makes an element appear by decoding and disappear by the same backwards. The Lab's experiments ( examples/lab/ in the website repository, https://github.com/amenui-dev/website) show each: experiment::frame(key, name, hint, piece, formula, &params, msg, label) puts a piece on a 4:3 stage it fills, the formula on one line and the numbers behind [ params ] ; seen cells step every frame (with reduced motion they rest). Sampling ( morph::cover_at , cells , on_outline , decode) follows Instance::xf and poses, so a posed glyph loosens from where it is drawn; cover_at counts any fill (a ground-toned panel too), ink_at only ink that shows. The lens touches only pictures and 3D elements that may loosen and that no handler operates. The landing page and first scene, Body (the website's examples/body.rs , #body ), is written the same way: one posed text element (the skin, its glyph count conserved), drawings for its volume, reflection, dust and the instrument markings, springs for gather and the opening, a signed-distance form sampled to a spiral of surface points (DESIGN.md §6.2 ). Pose::hue picks a glyph's accent. The field map (DESIGN.md §1.29 , amenui::fieldmap ) is a coarse grid of energy and flow over the window that settles to exactly zero: an element with .stirr(Stirr::default()) stirs it behind itself as it moves (floating, bottom sheet and card stack do by default; Look::map / a preset's interaction.map set how strong), Cmd::Stir { at: StirAt::Point | Key | Path, .. } stirs it from the state, and it loosens and drifts what may loosen as fronts do (caps and responses unchanged; Ui::looseness reads it too). The scribblr material (DESIGN.md §1.30 , amenui::strand ) is plain at rest; loosened, an element's ink becomes one thread of constant width that knots where the map has energy and trails off along its flow, then writes itself back ( Ui::strands() lists the threads drawn; Look::hold_ms holds its pose for a beat). El::trace(Trace { points, progress, weight, dash, gap, pull, stir, paint }) draws a long path by progress under any material, solid or dashed by arc length, pushed by the map and stirring it at its head. Materials are named for what they do ( dottr , halftonr , charr , smudgr , carvr , glitchr , scribblr , plus plain and near ); an old name such as halftone is refused and the error names the new one. Each is one WGSL file ( src/materials/<name>.wgsl , its numbers in a header, its own numbers read as mp(SELF, i) ): amenui add material <name> copies one, and Look::material_source(name, wgsl, params) adds a changed copy under a name of its own before the first window or Offscreen is made. page.effect(Effect { material, response, scope }) puts a material, a response and a scope on any subtree in one line, and el::wrap_text(src) makes a page to read from plain text or Markdown. Small type: .tracking(em) spaces letters (laid out by parley); .whisper() is lowercase, 0.6 em, in the bundled Latin serif ( Font::Whisper , text::SERIF ). The annotation layer's scope-wide readouts (DESIGN.md §4.2 – §4.3 ): gaze::EDGE edge notes (true values only: scope size, pointer, material and theme, loosest element, non-zero map nodes), gaze::OSC a waveform of the map's energy along one row, gaze::LEVEL a bar of its mean; Ui::readout() returns what they drew and export_tree() 's root has field: { level, nonzero } . The tenth preset, Loose Thread ( loose-thread ), puts these together; post.binary (black and white only) and post.invert are finishing-pass switches. Text on a form (DESIGN.md §1.26 ): a pose has a depth and a facing ( Pose::z , Pose::facing ) and glyphs draw far to near; El::form(FormFx { back, edge, overlap, fog }) leaves out what faces away, fades the rim and thins glyphs nearer ones cover; form::Form { shape, spin, camera, cover } wraps text onto a sphere, a surface or a mesh ( .pose(move |g| form.pose_of(g)) ) and Form::hit(x, y, w, h) finds the pointer on it ( docs/recipes/form3d.md ). El::reveal_by(Reveal::Word) shows words whole. Ui::glyph_at(x, y) is the glyph drawn there ( Point::glyph in on_point ); El::turn(radians) turns an element, and it is pressed where it is drawn. Slow one-off work goes through Ui::prepare(key, |s| progress) and Ui::ready(key) ; the renderer warms up with Renderer::begin and Warmup::step (DESIGN.md §1.23 ). Text flows around true outlines with .around(Around::new(vec![Silhouette::circle(..)], gap)) ; a piece of a line beside an obstacle is justified so both its edges are flush, adding at most Around::justify_max ems per gap (default 0.25; inter-character next to CJK, inter-word at spaces, between Latin letters only with Around::justify_latin_letters ); Latin pieces then take up to Around::track_max (0.08 em) between letters and, if still short, hyphenate the next word ( Around::hyphenate , on by default); a piece that would need more stays start-aligned (DESIGN.md §1.2 , "around").

One way to do each thing: state in the state, changes in update , motion through the field and Cmd . Key everything you will find again (tests, --events targets, flows, morphs, recomposition). Keys must be unique on a page; Ui::problems() lists duplicates and says what to write. Every numeric parameter is a named field with a default and is shown as a number control. Text to read and controls stay legible: fronts nudge them and loosen them at most Look::legible_cap . Mark decoration respond(Response::Loosen) ; mark a showcase legible(false) . No third-party or character images in the repository. Verify with pictures and data: render a frame and read its tree. A Ui you drive by hand lays out at each input. To see what a host does with several moves a frame, turn on ui.coalesce(true) and call ui.settle() (or draw) before reading the tree.

cargo run --release --bin render -- --page recipe-form --size 1280x800 --at 1000 --out out.png --tree out.json cargo run --release --bin render -- --page recipe-counter --events inc.json --at 300 --out c.png --tree c.json cargo run --release --bin render -- --page recipe-form --audit --strict # what is wrong with the frame, most serious first cargo run --release --bin render -- --page component-button --audit --strict # a component's examples (examples/components/), one page In Claude Code this file is also the amenui skill ( .claude/skills/amenui/SKILL.md , made from it by tools/skill.sh ; cargo test fails when they differ). The repository's .claude/settings.json runs tools/audit-hook.sh after every Edit or Write: a change to a recipe ( examples/<name>.rs ), a component's examples ( examples/components/<name>.rs ) or its widget ( src/widgets/<name>.rs ) renders that one page with --audit --strict , and its P0 and P1 findings and the view's problems come back to you as the hook's output. Other files are left alone. inc.json : [{"at_ms": 100, "kind": "press", "target": "inc"}, {"at_ms": 130, "kind": "release", "target": "inc"}] (kinds: press, release, move — x , y or target ; key — key as a DOM name, shift , cmd , alt ; wheel — dx , dy ; text — text ). The clock is fixed at 60 Hz from 0, so the same arguments give the same bytes. The tree ( --tree , or Ui::export_tree() ) has each element's key, kind, role and label, rect, text, material, response, legibility, focus / hover / press, scroll offset and looseness. --material takes plain , dottr , halftonr … (or a number), --theme takes dark , light , paper … --audit measures the frame ( amenui::audit , DESIGN.md §1.31 ): text cut off, contrast by WCAG, glyphs over each other, text under 9 device px, a page that never settles; each finding names the element, the number and what to do.

cargo test # everything that needs no GPU (and a few that use one if present) cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings # no warnings allowed cargo run --release --bin render -- --help # one frame + tree cargo run --release --bin sheet -- sheets # contact sheets of the picture marks cargo run --release --bin amenui -- add dialog --to ../my-app # copy a component (and what it needs) into a project cargo run --release --bin amenui -- add material smudgr # copy a material's WGSL file (src/materials/smudgr.wgsl) cargo run --release --bin sheet -- --material scribblr --loose 1 , 0.5 , 0 --arrival --out s.png # a material's sample sheet, checked The native window ( window ), the GPU pixel acceptance ( check , lavapipe works), filmstrips ( film ) and the benchmarks ( bench ) are binaries of the website repository, https://github.com/amenui-dev/website.

src/el.rs the tree ( El , builders), src/ui.rs the runtime, src/scene.rs instances and the field, src/morph.rs morphs, flows, recomposition, src/style.rs themes, materials, Look , src/shader.wgsl the three passes, src/text.rs type, src/tree.rs the exported tree, src/drive.rs scripted input and render , src/error.rs errors. src/widgets/ one file per widget (header: purpose, props, states, messages, usage); registry.json . examples/ the recipes, docs/recipes/ their pages; the site (the gallery, the Lab, the scenes, the docs pages) is the separate repository https://github.com/amenui-dev/website. docs/DESIGN.md the contract (read §1.15 – §1.17 for ripples, recomposition and this surface).

i A self-drawn interface framework in Rust (wgpu, native and web). Views are plain trees of values; every glyph, shape and picture has a true outline that can loosen, morph and condense; looks are swappable materials. Built to be written and checked by models: a deterministic render tool gives a PNG and the laid-out tree as JSON. Start with AGENTS.md (the mental model, the ten things you write, the rules, how to verify). DESIGN.md is the contract; §1.15 – §1.17 cover ripple rules, recomposition and the AI-facing surface.

The Lab ( #lab ) is a grid of small live experiments, one file each in the website repository's examples/lab/ , written against the public API ( amenui::experiment::Experiment ); each has a page #lab-<name> with its formula and parameters (registry.json experiments ). Each piece fills a 4:3 stage; the numbers open under [ params ] ; seen cells run every frame (reduced motion: they rest). Lumen : light on text, tone by distance, outlines untouched ( El::pose ) Contours : iso-lines of noise plus a pointer bump ( field::Grid::contours ) Silk : marks advected by curl noise and a stirred flow ( field::Swarm , budget::grant ) Grown : Gray–Scott inside an element's true outline ( El::on_outline , field::GrayScott ) Mercury ↗ : metaballs with a spring-followed ball ( field::Balls ) Flow : text on a waving path ( Pose::angle ) Loupe : text on a sphere, drag to spin Orbit ↗ : Kepler orbits with pointer attraction Spring : the gesture spring, dragged and thrown Stack : the card stack in the lab's look Body : the landing page and first scene ( #body , the website's examples/body.rs ): a passage gathers into a turning, luminous body of its own glyphs and back; full-bleed, markings in the picture; two rest states, glyph count conserved Decode ↗ : El::decode , blocks over the true outline resolving coarse to fine ( #decode ) Field map ↗ : El::stirr trails and Cmd::Stir , energy and flow that settle to zero; decoration loosens and drifts behind what moves ( #stirr ) scribblr ↗ : the thread material, plain at rest, loose ink as one line that knots and trails off and writes itself back; El::trace long paths, solid or dashed ( #material-scribblr , #stirr ) Edge notes and readouts ↗ : El::tracking , El::whisper() in a small serif; gaze::EDGE , OSC , LEVEL read the runtime and the field map ( Ui::readout() ); the Loose Thread preset with post.binary and post.invert ( #style-loose-thread ) Text on a form ↗ : Pose::z and Pose::facing , El::form(FormFx) , form::Form and Form::hit ; Every documentation page as Markdown, at md/en/<page>.md and md/zh-Hans/<page>.md next to the web build ( cargo run --release --bin md -- dist/md ). Introduction : amenui is an interface framework that draws every pixel itself, written in Rust on wgpu; the same code runs in a native window and on the web. Installation : Pick the host your interface lives in. Command line : Components are distributed as source, the way shadcn/ui does it: you copy a component's file into your project and change it there. Your first view : A view is a function from state to an element tree; an update is a function from state and a message to a new state. Project structure : Forms : A form is state and messages, like everything else: the state holds every value, each widget sends a message for each edit, and update is the only place a va… The tree and messages : After every message the runtime calls view(&state) once, gets a new El tree, compares it with the last by key and lays out again only what changed. Layout : Layout is taffy's flexbox and grid, in logical pixels; elements do not shrink unless asked. Text : Text is set by parley and rasterised by swash; every atlas pixel holds coverage and the signed distance to the stroke, so every material draws a glyph by its… Materials and looseness : A material is how the second pass draws: plain, dottr, halftonr, charr, smudgr, carvr, glitchr, near, scribblr. Ripple rules : A press sends a front that by default reaches only the control pressed (Scope::Own); Scope::Container and Scope::Global reach further. Transforms : Two kinds: a morph (Cmd::Morph: one element breaks into cells that fly onto another's shape) and a flow (Cmd::Flow: what two pages share moves to its new pla… Presets : A style preset is data: theme, material and its numbers, annotation, interaction character, how scrolling looks, and a transition program. Annotation : The third pass is the annotation layer: frames, numbers, sizes, leaders and rulers drawn from the real layout, never loosened. 3D : el::scene3d(Scene3d) is one more element on the page: meshes are drawn off screen into shade, normals and depth, then become ink and nearness like glyphs, so… Particles : When a morph has many cells it is simulated on the GPU (a compute shader, or ping-ponging float targets), otherwise on the CPU, where a mesh side's cells sta… Languages : Each language has a message catalog (`assets/i18n/zh-Hans. Accessibility : The screen is drawn by the framework, so the runtime builds an accessibility mirror from the tree: every element's role (the WAI-ARIA role of the same name),… Performance : Draw only when something changed; draw only what changed (two boxes); scrolling moves, it does not lay out again; a long list builds only the rows that show;… Testing with render and the tree : render plays events on a fixed 60 Hz clock and draws the last frame and its tree; the same arguments give the same bytes. Theming and dark mode : A theme is a set of colours and the faces for display, body and monospace (style::THEMES). Right to left : A row lays out from the right when its direction is right to left: El::rtl(true) on the row (or any ancestor), or a locale that reads right to left. amenui is one Cargo package: a library, the amenui command line and two tools. Everything except render.rs and the shaders runs without a GPU, so the runtime can be driven and tested headless. DESIGN.md gives the reasons and the numbers; this page says where each part lives.

view(&state) → El tree → layout (taffy, parley) → instances (glyph, shape, picture, mesh) → G-buffer stage: coverage buffer + signed distance field, from true outlines → screen-space shading stage: the material → annotation layer → finishing pass (post) input → hit test → message → update(&mut state) → view again A press or the pointer lens puts energy into the wave field; commands in the state ( Cmd::Morph , Cmd::Flow and the rest in morph.rs ) ask the runtime for transforms. Widgets never animate themselves.
