The fonts in assets/ are all under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Their licenses are in assets/licenses/ . text::embedded() returns them compiled into the binary (about 14 MB, what a native application ships with; the native window uses it); text::load_bundled(dir) reads them from a folder instead, such as text::ASSETS in a checkout. The web build fetches the three main faces and compiles in only Geist Pixel and the serif. File Face Source Used as NotoSansSC-Regular.otf Noto Sans SC Google Noto The outline face for Latin, Han and kana DepartureMono-Regular.otf Departure Mono 1.500 (Helena Zhang) Its release package The Latin pixel face, 11 px FusionPixel-12px-Proportional-zh_hans.otf Fusion Pixel 12px, proportional, Simplified Chinese (TakWolf, upstream 2026.08.11) See below The CJK pixel face, 12 px GeistPixel-{Square,Grid,Circle,Triangle,Line}.otf Geist Pixel (Vercel and basement.studio) npm package geist 1.9.2 Optional Latin pixel faces ( text::GEIST_PIXEL ) SourceSerif4-8pt-subset.ttf Source Serif 4 (Frank Grießhammer, Adobe) Google Fonts repository Font::Whisper , small lowercase type and margin notes ( text::SERIF ) Pixel faces are drawn only at integer multiples of their size, at whole-pixel positions and without anti-aliasing, so their edges hold only ink and ground. Any face can also be printed as pixels through the material ( .print(pitch) ).

Fusion Pixel was merged back into one OTF from the WOFF2 files split by Unicode block in the npm package @vp-tw/cjk-web-fonts-fusion-pixel-font . The licenses of the upstream fonts it includes (Ark Pixel, Cubic 11, Galmuri) are kept in assets/licenses/fusion-pixel/ . Geist Pixel was converted from WOFF2 to an OTF container with fontTools, with no change to the glyphs or names. Its license field reads "SIL OPEN FONT LICENSE"; the text is in assets/licenses/geist-pixel/OFL.txt . It has Latin only. Source Serif 4 was instanced from the variable font SourceSerif4[opsz,wght].ttf with fontTools at the 8 pt optical size and weight 400, the cut drawn for small sizes, and subset to Basic Latin, Latin-1 Supplement and common punctuation (82 KB). The glyphs are unchanged. The license is in assets/licenses/source-serif/OFL.txt ; it has no reserved font name.

The bundled faces cover Latin, Han and kana (and Hangul in Fusion Pixel). For other scripts (Arabic, Hebrew, Thai, Devanagari, emoji…) a Ui takes more faces: Face::fallback(bytes) : tried after the face asked for and the first face, in the order given. This is the way on the web, where there are no system fonts. Face::system() , last in the list: the system's installed fonts, after every given face (feature system-fonts , on by default; fontconfig is loaded at run time on Linux). app::native::run adds it. The bundled faces still decide every character they have, so text in Latin and Chinese looks the same on every machine; tests and offscreen do not add the system's fonts, so their pixels do not depend on the machine. Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese line breaking needs the complex-scripts feature (dictionaries of a few MB). Text::missing_glyphs counts characters no face has.

Newest first. The acceptance checks for each part are in DESIGN.md §7 . Versions follow Semantic Versioning ↗ as Cargo reads it: before 1.0, a change to the second number (0.1 → 0.2) may break code, and a change to the third (0.1.0 → 0.1.1) does not. The crate and the amenui npm package ( web/ ) always carry the same version, because the page side must match the module that web_app! generates. The minimum Rust is the one CI builds with ( rust-version in Cargo.toml); raising it is a breaking change before 1.0 only in the second number.

A subtree marked El::audit_under(preset) is audited under that preset's rules, its accent share of its own box, and the rest of the page under the page's ( render --preset ) or the floors alone. Breaking: audit::audit takes the theme, audit::audit_under takes the preset (not its name and rules), Props and Node have audit_under , and Driven::audit and Driven::audit_under have no default body: a wrapper that forwarded only audit (so a preset run silently used the base audit) now has to forward audit_under too. A preset carries rules ( Preset::rules , preset::Rule : contrast for running text or all text to read, text size, margin, measure, accent share) that the audit holds its pages to as well ( audit::audit_under , render --preset , drive::in_preset ); the ten presets each have theirs. A rule can only tighten: a preset with a contrast under 4.5 or a text size under 9 px is refused when read ( PresetError::Looser ). Breaking: audit::Kind has Margin , Measure and Accent ; LookError has UnknownPreset and BadPreset , PresetError has Looser ; Preset has rules (older JSON reads with none). Under Glitch, text to read is kept clear of the chroma offset and most of the scanlines ( PostSpec::clear_text , off by default): on its ink and 2 px round it the offset is 0 and the scanlines 0.08. Pictures, shapes, the ground and legible(false) text keep the whole pass. The audit reads a frame bent by curvature where the bend drew it ( audit::unbend ; with no curvature, the frame as drawn), and reports text the bend carries past the window's edge as Clipped ( audit::bent_off ). Breaking: PostSpec and Post have clear_text , Scene has legible . The audit reports a cut as Clipped only where no scroll view can bring that edge's side into view: not the last row of a page that scrolls, cut by the window's bottom edge (the fold), nor a line in a strip that scrolls sideways cut by the strip's end or the window's. A box in the scroll view that does not scroll still clips what it cuts, and a scroll view clips across the way it scrolls. The audit tells large text by its size ( audit::LARGE_PX 24, LARGE_BOLD_PX 19 when bold): it needs 3:1, a P0 under it, and a preset's contrast rules do not apply to it. A 64 px headline at 3.28:1 passes. At rest a card stack's flat cards are on whole device pixels however large the box is drawn (a page's El::fit zoom too): each side's outline is one pixel at its grey, where the top and right ones had been two at half strength. Mesh3d.snap names a rectangle an orthographic view puts on whole device pixels ( Scene3d::proj_in ); the card stack's scene sets it to its top card. Breaking: Mesh3d has snap . A 3D element's edge on a pixel boundary reads as exactly there (the resolve's zero on a whole step, and distances within a step of a half pixel taken as that), so it covers the pixel inside fully and the one outside not at all. The pointer leaving an element whose messages are its own ( El::local_messages ) restages it as a move over it does; the leave had viewed and laid out the whole page. On the Lab's loupe this takes a 10 ms frame each time the pointer leaves the glass down to an ordinary one. Under dottr and charr a thin line at looseness 1 is a row of the least marks instead of falling between the cells: a loose cell with ink in it sampled below 0.25 ( INK_FLOOR ) is drawn as if sampled at 0.25 ( dottr a dot, charr the lightest character, centred on the line). Cells sampled at 0.25 or more are drawn as before; halftonr is unchanged. A card stack under dottr , charr and halftonr is drawn as under plain at rest: its cards loosen to 1 within 120 ms while a card's spring moves ( LOOSEN_S ) and back to 0 within 240 ms after the last one stops ( TIGHTEN_S ), and then ask for no frames. They had been held at looseness 1. Stack::moving is true until they are tight.

The reduced grid (stages at their own scale, a quality below 1) is fixed to the content of the largest scroll area, and the filter up weighs its texels itself: a stage a scroll carries is no longer shaded again in every moved frame. The reduced target is three texels larger each way. While the trace holds the rows, the frame moves as the viewport's ground does: an opaque shape with a material override under the whole viewport (a plain page over a dotted look, as the components pages are) is that ground. Their plain content had been shaded again over the whole viewport every frame as another lattice. While the trace holds the rows, a scroll area inside the moving one that does not scroll itself no longer makes every frame be drawn whole ("latch: not alone"): it is content the frame carries, shaded again where it was and where it is. On /components/ that was 81 frames in 180 of a fast back-and-forth scroll. With coalesced input (the web and desktop hosts), what a scroll brings into view no longer condenses as if it were new: the paint left for the frame is a scroll's when only scrolls asked for it, and when a scroll and something else (rows added, a new page) asked for it, what was in the layout before does not condense and new keys do. A fast scroll had condensed most of the screen every frame. A wheel gesture stays with what took its first step ( WHEEL_LATCH = 0.5 s between steps, the pointer still): a 3D view ( El::on_wheel , widgets::orbit ) scrolled under the pointer no longer takes over a page's scroll momentum, which stopped the page and laid it out again every frame. An on_wheel handler that returns None leaves the step to scrolling. A layout a handler's message asks for is put down to the handler's call in FramePath::layout_from (was Ui::send ). The runtime hashes its own maps and fingerprints with fasthash::FastHasher (a folded multiply), not SipHash. A scroll step's paint allocates about a third less and half the bytes: text's glyph lists are kept between paints, layout-cache look-ups no longer copy the text, the field map is not built to be compared each tick, and recording texts index the scene once. While a scroll goes on, Ui::a11y_diff sends only focus: the mirror's new places go once the scroll rests ( Ui::next_wake asks for that frame). Every scroll frame on the web had rebuilt the mirror and sent every element in the scroll area again, serialised. FramePath::layouts and layout_from : the layouts since the frame before and where the first was asked for (the Ui::relayout call's file and line), shown at the end of FramePath::line as layout 2 (src/ui.rs:2081) . Ui::layouts_since_drawn . A partial frame draws stage 1's boxes in one render pass for each of its two images (was a pair of passes for each box: the M1 Lab's median frame opened 8, each loading and storing both images whole on a tile-based GPU). Cost::passes counts them. FramePath::shade_why : the three reasons whose boxes cover most of a partial frame's shaded pixels, each as a share of the window, shown after the share in FramePath::line ( shade 54% (stage moved 43%, changed 12%, band 6%) ). A 3D element supersampled at a whole scale (the card stack, at 2) reads each pixel's texel from the pixel's own position, exactly: one driver lost the outline's top row and another its bottom. A cached subtree ( El::cached ) in a scroll area moves with the scroll: the frame moves its plate as it moves the last frame and inks only the band scrolled into view and what changed in it (every scroll frame of the Lab's Loupe was drawn whole, "plate emptied"). Any change to a cached subtree now inks its plate only within the frame's boxes. PlateSpan has a new field, replace . An instance whose clip alone changed (a clipping box's edge crossing a viewport's) is drawn again between the two edges, not in its whole box: the frame a cached sheet's edge scrolls past drew most of the window. A frame that moves the last one redraws, for what came into view or went, each instance's box within its clip (was one box round each run of them, which on the Lab spanned the window's width): stage 1 shades about half the pixels it did on a fast scroll. A scroll's trace pass probes the nearness as far apart as it reads (was every 4 px): the same frame, with fewer reads for each pixel it tests (it shades a little more of the viewport again, which costs less than the reads saved: on the Lab a fast-scroll frame took about a quarter less on the CPU rasteriser). The warm-up makes the trace pass (it was compiled on the first fast scroll, a stall of seconds), and after the warm-up, idle time makes every material pass, upsample and trace pass the page may need ( Renderer::preparing ; was one a drawn frame, so a page at rest made none before its first scroll). Each material pipeline (the finishing pass, the upsample, the trace pass, a material's own passes) is drawn with once, into one pixel, as it is made: the first frame that needs it no longer waits for a driver to finish it (the first switch to a dark scheme with bloom took twice as long as the later ones on the CPU rasteriser). Rows of another lattice (or none) in a viewport no longer draw the frame whole while the trace holds the rows: the frame moves as the page's material does, and what is in the other material is shaded again. A plain shape behind a whole scroll area (a page's fill(Paint::GROUND) ) moves with the scroll as the ground does: a slow scroll of the components pages shaded about 85 % of the window each frame, now the band and the edges.

.claude/skills/amenui/SKILL.md is AGENTS.md as the amenui skill (made by tools/skill.sh ; tests/skill.rs fails when they differ). .claude/settings.json runs tools/audit-hook.sh after Edit and Write: a change to a recipe, a component's examples or its widget renders that one page with render --audit --strict and hands its P0 and P1 findings and the view's problems back to the model. render --page component-<name> : a component's examples, one under another, as a page to render and audit.

The component examples and the widgets' Usage: lines show English only (Badge "New" and "Draft", Avatar "Grace Hopper", ...); Badge's "New" is Primary, not Accent, and Button's disabled example is a disabled Primary. near draws its bands inside the ink in the hairline grey (was the accent): at rest a material shows no accent.

El::on_pens(f) : a text sends its glyphs' pens as the shaper set them (logical px in the content box, the numbers GlyphAt::pen gives a pose) after a paint, when they changed; a state no longer collects them from inside a pose. Ui::glyphs_drawn(key) -> Vec<GlyphDrawn> : each glyph of a text as the last paint drew it, after its pose: its number, the box its raster covers (logical px, window coordinates) and its opacity. A message the runtime queues in a paint ( on_outline , on_pens ) asks for the next frame.

near at rest is the ink and its greys only: outside ink its three nearest bands are the ink at 0.5, 0.3 and 0.15 (was the second accent; none further out), and where loose the dim grey at 0.35 (was the third, the warning colour). Inside ink the bands stay hairline. Ui::on_kept(f) and Ui::kept_image(key) : a cached element over the plates' limit (four, twice the window's area) has no kept image and a cached_view of it draws nothing; f is told its key and false , then true when it has one again or goes, and the page is viewed again on that frame.

Mesh3d::resolution_scale goes up to 2 (was 1): above 1 the mesh pass is supersampled, so a silhouette and its drawn outline fall on a pixel's share of them. The card stack draws at 2: a turned card's hairline is a smooth line, its whole pixels still exactly the grey asked (was steps of two pixels, at 0.5).

A slow stage holding its image no longer paints the page on every frame it holds: a frame in which it would hold paints nothing for it, a step that comes while it would hold waits for its next draw (not viewed), and it draws alone, the rest of the page copied, on its own cadence and on the first frame without input. A stage that held draws whole then, not by its parts ( El::steps inside it), so the page comes to rest after it.

Stack::outlines : card n's outline grey (the last entry repeats; empty: the ink). The default stack is raised cards ( paints [RAISED] , was the three accents, ink and dim), outlined 1 px, the top one in the ink and the ones under it in the hairline grey. MeshInstances::outline (and MeshInstances::outlined ): the grey a group of copies' drawn outline ( Mesh3d::outline ) takes, by its tone; None is the ink as before. **A struct literal of MeshInstances needs outline: None ** ( MeshInstances::one sets it).

dot_chart : the picked range is ink (its dots up to the ink, the line under the axis ink) and the rest of the field dim; the accent is only on the dot under the pointer ( DotChart::under ) and on a control point and its tick while dragged ( DotChart::dragged ). avatar 's last argument is a shade, not a hue: 0 ink, 1 dim, 2 text ( widgets::SHADES ), initials in the ground. The examples: a main action is Variant::Primary ( counter , morph , mesh , chapter ), and nothing is in the accent that is not held or dragged or a named specimen ( counter 's shape, morph 's disc, chapter 's numbers and annotate 's panel are ink; annotate 's meter and loading 's pictures are greys, not hues; the caption specimen is raised in a hairline frame). badge 's usage line shows Variant::Primary .

widgets::MENU_SURFACE is the raised grey (it was the ground): menus, selects, context and nested menus, the sheet and the bottom sheet are raised in their hairline frame, and their selected and hot rows ( selected_on ) are the hairline grey with an ink label. A popover keeps the ground. A nested menu's chevron (a row with a submenu) is the text grey: dim reads 2.93:1 on the raised panel in the light scheme.

A stage that steps ( Ui::on_step ) or a subtree whose messages are its own is still drawn alone, the rest of the page copied, while a label or a slot's text recomposes glyph by glyph; before, the whole page was painted until the tiles landed. perf().counters.restages now counts only the frames that were drawn so.

El::steps() inside a stage marks a part of it that changes alone (a lens over a page that stays): a step ( Ui::on_step ) that names the stage views and draws only those parts, by their keys through Ui::stage_view , and the rest of the stage is the last frame's. A part stage_view does not give, or laid out otherwise, and the stage is viewed whole as before. The page naming the step no longer needs to name what in the stage moves.

El::bloom() marks what the look's bloom glows over: once any element is marked, the bloom glows only inside the box round what marked elements draw, and only from what is drawn there ( Post::bloom_region ). With none marked it covers the whole frame as before.

The default theme ( DARK , LIGHT ) takes the AA.9 table: new grounds, ink and accents (the accent is #f47a3c dark and #b23f0d light; #ff6b2b is retired), and four greys of its own ( Theme::greys : raised, hairline, dim, text). Paint::DIM , TEXT and FAINT (now HAIRLINE , and RAISED new) are drawn as those colours exactly, not as the ink mixed toward the ground; a tone between two greys is drawn between their colours. Their tones moved to whole 255ths (dim 0.66 → 168/255, text 0.86 → 219/255). Other themes take their greys mixed as before ( Greys::mixed ); **a theme built from DARK or LIGHT with its own ground and ink keeps their greys unless it sets greys: Greys::mixed(ground, ink) ** (or Greys::mixed_dim(ground, ink, 4.5) , which takes dim toward the ink until it reads 4.5:1 on the ground). Paint::EXTREME : white on a dark scheme, black on a light one ( Theme::extreme ). It is the ink image's fourth hue code (0.45, which the unused glyph-height code held). El::fill_hover and El::fill_held : a fill under the pointer and while held or dragged; El::border_hover : a border under the pointer or with focus. Variant::Primary : an ink plate with a ground label, the extreme under the pointer, for the one main action of a group. Variant::Accent stays for an explicitly coloured action. Badges take Primary too. The default controls rest in ink: a switch that is on (ink track, ground knob; off a hairline track and a dim knob), a slider (ink run and thumb, a hairline rest; the thumb is the accent while dragged), a radio's dot, a checkbox's outline and tick, a toggle that is on and a choice's current option (ink plates with ground labels). So are a pagination's current page (an ink plate), a current tab's rule, a progress bar's fill and the label of a selected list row or menu option; widgets::SELECTED , the plate of a selected or keyed row, is the raised grey (it was the accent at 0.12), the hairline grey on a raised surface ( widgets::selected_on ). Hot rows of the command, context and nested menus are that plate with an ink label, a skip link an ink plate. Outlines of interactive controls stay dim at rest and turn ink under the pointer or with focus, and while a select or menu is open or a number is typed into (they were the accent then); panel frames (menus, dialogs, sheets, popovers, toasts, tooltips) are hairline. A switch's knob is the accent while pressed. The hover and focus marks are ink ( Fx::marks_accent is 0 by default). The recipes' and samples' main actions are Primary ; the components' button page shows it.

near has ink bands ( 墨带 , 1 to 3, and 带宽 , px; 0 by default, the bands as before): only that many bands outside the ink, in the ink at 0.5, 0.3 and 0.15 (two: 0.5 and 0.25), each the width with as much ground before it, square round the ink's pixel corners, for pixel type on whole pixels and on the lattice. carvr never cuts deeper than its band ( 刻带 ), the knife's wander included. A glyph 32 px or more each way set in near or carvr takes all the ground its quad covers, padded by the spread once more, so what the material draws round the letter is drawn; text at reading sizes keeps the override just round its ink.

A cached subtree ( El::cached ) in which nothing it draws from changed is passed by when the page is painted: it is neither drawn nor hashed, and its plate is laid on as it was ( Counters::kept counts them). It was drawn and hashed instance by instance on every paint (about 9 ms for 11,000 glyphs natively).

fs_ink 's code test no longer mixes || and && without parentheses, which Chrome's WGSL compiler rejects (the ink, nearness and clearing passes were invalid there). A test now holds every WGSL source the renderer compiles to the expression rules Chrome enforces and naga does not.

The frame in which a fast scroll's trace starts or stops holding the rows to the lattice moves the last frame by what it shows, instead of shading the whole viewport (the readout's latch on/off ). A lattice material used only outside the scrolled viewport (a bar in dottr over a list in charr) no longer stops the last frame from moving (the readout's latch: mixed lattices ).

A 3D element that comes on the page or goes (scrolled into view, a section opened) draws the frame again only where it is or was, not the frame whole (the readout's meshes ); the 3D elements after it are not drawn again.

A picture given after its page is drawn ( Renderer::set_picture ) is drawn on the next frame where it is, with the cells that read it, not by a frame drawn whole: a page need not turn Renderer::partial off for it.

What a new page lays out only after a flow began (a label shown once what it follows is in view, a drawing's new marks) comes in as what was new when the flow began: over a growing picture once it has landed. It was drawn at once where it is, outside the part of the picture that shows. An element keyed the same on both pages that rode on the growing picture on the old page and is outside every flow on the new one (a layer over the page's frame: a pointer's box and its label) is carried by the picture to its new place. It was drawn at once there, outside the part of the picture that shows.

The stages' scale steps up only when the frames' cost there, by the level up's pixels, would be under 85 % of the display frame; a step down within 5 s of a step up holds the lower level, and a route's visit has at most two steps up ( perf::STAGE_UPS , StageScale::held ), in place of the waits of 5, 10 and 20 s and three returns a level.

A morph from what a stage draws ( El::stage ; posed glyphs stepped every frame) starts its tiles where the frame before it drew them, also when the morph is asked for by a command with a new view that poses them elsewhere or hides them; it took them as the new view put them.
Fx::marks_accent (1 by default, the accent as before): how much of the accent the hover and focus marks are drawn in; 0 draws them in the ink.

Scrolling under the automatic level is not softened on a frame that can move the last one ( dirty::Move ): that frame shades only the strip scrolled in, sharp. From a renderer's second frame, one a frame, the material passes for the page's materials (hidden elements', one waiting for a morph, included: Scene::mats ) are made ahead and kept by material; a morph's frames count the materials of its tiles. With one built-in global material and no override, the material pass (and its upsample) is a pipeline of its own for that material (the WGSL override constant MAT ): Renderer::specialise , Renderer::specialised , render::SPECIALISE_AFTER . Marks changed in place (drifting motes, a turning body's glyphs) are each their own box, not one box round them all; many boxes are gathered by where they are, and the final frame is shaded in up to 32 boxes grown from what changed ( dirty::MAX_SHADE_BOXES ; the G-buffer keeps 8). A fast scroll with its trace showing moves the last frame too, and shades again only the pixels the trace can reach ( fs_trace , Cost::trace ); under dottr and charr the frame moves by the lattice's steps ( dirty::Move::frame , trace , way , latch ). Not under glitchr or a material from source. El::local_messages : the messages a subtree's handlers send change only it and the El::steps elements, so it is restaged after them ( Ui::stage_view ) instead of viewing and laying out the page; for a stage dragged by hand. Inside El::cached , a pixel face asked for under its native size is set and drawn at the size asked, by its outline's coverage ( text::FINE , Text::fine ). A renderer made after the page was painted ( Offscreen::new in a render tool) draws it: it sends the whole glyph atlas on its first frame, and a cached subtree its plates do not hold is drawn again ( Ui::plates_lost ). A scene drawn twice with no paint between inks its plates once ( Scene::paint ). An element moved by its offsets in a restage stays where it was moved through a view of the page that lays nothing out; it had gone back to where the last layout put it. Perf::path ( perf::FramePath ): how the last frame was drawn, for a readout: whether it moved the last frame and the first reason it did not or was drawn whole, whether the material pass was specialised and why not, the share shaded at full resolution, and the soft, stage and reduced scales; FramePath::line , shown by the full overlay. dirty::parts_why , Parts::refused . A scroll with its trace showing over stages shaded at their own scale moves the last frame (it was drawn whole every frame); the stages in the viewport are shaded again where they are, slow or fast. dirty::meet , Move::bx . Renderer::spec_force : force the material pass made for the global material on (from the next frame, even over overrides, for measuring) or off. Off, a pass already made is not used either. The trace pass is made for the material too ( fs_trace with MAT ). A page of several built-in materials (up to render::GATED_MAX ) is drawn by a material pass for each, each drawing only its own pixels (the WGSL override ONLY ), once the same materials have held for specialise frames; an override in the global material no longer keeps the page from the pass made for it. FramePath::gated . A step of the stages' scale shades only the stages again, not the whole frame (and not the frame after either). Ui::stage_governor , StageScale::set_level , for checks.

pair::Faces resolves a role as the page's root does (its El::fonts ), and the faces kept follow it; a Lab page whose theme sets display to mono measured Noto Sans. Faces::face_of . Experiment::faces : a cell made alone ( experiment::ui , the contact sheet) is handed the faces. GlyphAt tells a pose each glyph's pen as laid out ( pen , base , advance ), so a pose can put a kerned glyph's pen exactly; GlyphAt is Default .

El::cached() : a subtree drawn once onto a plate and laid on from it while it draws the same, so a large page of small text costs no instances; drawn again when it changes and after a new window size. el::cached_view(over, from, ink) : part of a cached subtree, scaled into an element, read as coverage nearest (a magnifier's pixels). El::clip_round(radius) : a clip with round corners, or a circle. A stage's absolutely placed element that moves by its offsets alone is restaged with no layout, so a chip dragged about a stage costs no page view or layout. A pointer move asks for a frame only when something shows where the pointer is, the hover or the cursor changes, or a drag, touch or selection is under way; hovering a still page draws nothing. An experiment's formula and label are selectable.

A front pushes text to read and controls about the centre of the control they are in, and a surface that holds them is not that control: an element that follows the pointer ( on_point , on_move ) or one larger than a quarter of the window. A full-window stage with on_point or on_key made its whole page one piece, so every commit's front shoved everything on it sideways at once, when the front crossed the window's centre. A commit inside El::commit_scope is over once its front has reached the scope's farthest corner, not the window's, and its scope takes in what the material draws round the box (the nearness spread and a front's push). A card that switched to near kept the old outline round it for two seconds and then swapped it in one frame, and every frame until then was drawn whole. The commit's own front stays in the scope too, as the fronts of other presses there did. near draws no bands round text with strokes under 3 px. Only the shapes' nearness takes a label's surroundings into an element's own material, so round a label in a control its bands showed as stray dashes over the ascenders and a hook under a descender. Titles keep their bands. The hover and focus marks are drawn over the material, exact, in the accent, and on a segment or a tab they stay inside the control's border. Drawn by the material, near outlined each bar twice, and on a segment the bars sat on the control's own border, which looked broken. The performance readout keeps its width: every field keeps its width whatever its number ( idle is as wide as the rates), and its plate does not narrow while it stays open in a window of the same size. Its corner's inset no longer counts on both sides, so a wide inset (a stage's edge) leaves it the room beside it. Its edge used to jump about 70 px each time the page went idle and woke.

When frames are missed, the stages' device scale steps down (2 → 1.5 → 1 → 0.75) and back up after a wait that doubles each time; text, panels, the chrome and whatever is drawn over a stage stay at the device's scale ( perf::StageScale , Ui::reset_stage_scale , Perf::stage_label ). Look::quality below 1 pins it. A slow stage is held under input only once its scale is as low as it goes. Automatic quality goes by the intervals between frames drawn while something moves, not their CPU time, so a machine slow on the GPU steps down too ( perf::AutoQuality::feed(t, cost, moving) ). Under the automatic level, scroll areas are shaded at it while they scroll (no lower than the material's floor, render::soft_floor ); the ink's edges, overlays and the rest of the page stay sharp, and 100 ms after the last delta one frame is drawn sharp ( Ui::scroll_soft , render::SOFT_SCROLL ).

pair : the distance between two glyph outlines and the white between them, and where to set a pair for a gap or an area, from the page's faces handed to the state ( Ui::faces , Ui::on_faces ), not the text system.

A slow stage holds with input coalesced ( Ui::coalesce , as the web and desktop hosts run): the input of a frame waited for the frame's layout, and the tick had spent it before, so the stage drew every frame of a drag. El::steps marks an element beside a stage that changes with it (a formula, a label): Ui::on_step returns its key with the stage's and Ui::stage_view gives it, so an experiment's own page no longer lays out every frame. Text whose words changed but measures as before counts as laid out the same.

taffy is built with flexbox alone (no grid, block layout or calc), about 170 KB less in a web module. A Style with Display::Grid or Display::Block now lays out as flexbox; amenui itself used grid only for stack and layers . stack keeps its meaning: as wide as its widest child, as tall as its tallest, each child centred. It is a row whose children lie over one another by their margins (set from the widths they took), so a margin you give a child of a stack still counts, and a percentage margin there becomes a length. layers places each child absolutely at the top left of its box unless the child is placed already; the box does not grow with its children, as documented (a box with no height of its own grew with the grid before; give it fill_height or a height).

A ramp stroke ( Drawing::ramp ) fades as a whole: its far and middle stops follow the element's opacity as its start does. Coming back to an index, a window waiting for the picture to land no longer drew its rays at full size. A picture in a layer (after something that stirs, or a modal) is a picture for what is drawn over it, so a drawing's own colours ( Drawing::palette ) stay its own while its picture fades in, not the accent; a picture under 0.01 of its opacity no longer marks its area as a picture.

Ui::on_step(f) and Ui::stage_view(f) : a stage ( El::stage ) whose piece changes by itself is viewed and drawn again alone, in the boxes the last layout gave it, while the rest of the page keeps its last frame; the frame is the one a whole view of the page gives. A step that lays the stage out otherwise views the whole page (DESIGN.md §1.35 ). The website's Lab index with one cell running takes 2.9 ms a frame on the CPU, from 6.9 ms. perf().counters.restages counts those frames. The experiment cell's stage ( experiment::frame ) is an El::stage . Text to read over other ink finds that ink by a grid over the window, faster.

Ui::on_focus(f) : the state is told which element has the keyboard focus whenever it moves (Tab, a press, focus_key , clear_focus , a modal layer opening or closing), as on_hover tells it where the pointer is; f returns whether the view changed. A Lab cell can run while one of its controls has the focus.

El::stage() : the live piece of a page. When its draws take more than 0.6 of a frame it holds its last image on frames that answer input, so the controls beside it answer in that frame, and draws again on the first frame without input, after a release, and during a long drag every max(100 ms, 6 draws) up to 500 ms (DESIGN.md §1.35 ). A stage that draws in time is drawn every frame as before. Ui::slow_stage(ms) and Ui::stage_state(key) , for checks; stage holds the numbers. Props has a new public field, stage .

Pixel type set at its face's native size because a fitted box zoomed it under that size (the Lab's formula on a docs stage) has its lines as much further apart: the lines no longer overlap and the text's box holds them. ViewProblem::OwnColourOffPicture and ViewProblem::RampHue look at what is drawn of a mark, cut by its clip: a ray that runs out of a band holding its picture is no longer reported. Posed text ( El::pose ) whose box is outside its clip draws the glyphs its pose puts inside the clip.

Every Offscreen in a process shares one wgpu instance, adapter, device and queue, made on first use; each keeps its own renderer, target and read-back buffer. Tests that ran in parallel made and dropped Vulkan instances on several threads at once, which crashed lavapipe (a segmentation fault in a different GPU test each run on CI). A failure to start is kept and returned again to every later Offscreen .

Drawing only what changed matches instances in order rather than by place, so a drawing whose strokes change in number redraws its own box and not everything after it, and redraws up to 8 boxes a stage instead of their union ( dirty::parts , dirty::MAX_BOXES , Scene::cuts ; dirty::Inputs has a new public field, cuts ). A fitted box ( El::fit ) whose subtree changes only what it draws is one view and no layout a frame (it was three views and two layouts): the scales found last time stand until something layout reads changes. What text to read holds ( holds ) finds the ink drawn before it through a 64 px grid instead of testing every earlier instance, and the islands of loosened controls ( islands ) walk up each node's parents once instead of searching every earlier node. The scene is the same; on the website's Lab index (about 7,000 instances and 420 nodes, 1440 × 900 at 2×) a frame's paint goes from about 16 ms to about 4 ms natively.

widgets::number , caption and experiment::frame build their controls once, with their own messages, and map them to the application's; segmented , choice , slider and input build their body once per message type rather than once for every closure passed to them. Nothing changes in what they show or send. The website's full module is 11,819 bytes smaller gzipped (2,832,825 to 2,821,006).

Look::select ( style::Select { halo, alpha, ink } , 3 px, 0.34, on by default): the selection halo is opaque, the accent mixed into the ground as one colour (#5f2d18 on the dark theme), so halos that meet across glyphs and lines show no box and no darker band; selected glyphs are drawn in the ink. The halo comes and goes in one frame. Look has a new public field, select : code that builds one with every field named needs it.

widgets::number : never narrower than its steps and field; a width that leaves the label no room beside them puts the steps on a line under it, and a label wider than the control ends in an ellipsis, read whole. A caption's and the Lab's numbers no longer run into each other. experiment::frame : the formula wraps to the cell instead of being cut. El::clamp : a word wider than the line is cut too.

Drawing::palette([...]) : a drawing's own colours, which its marks name as Paint::hue(3 + k) , so it looks the same under any theme; exact over a picture (a ramp between two in OKLab), hue 0 and reported off one ( ViewProblem::OwnColourOffPicture , DESIGN.md §1.26 ). A frame's drawings have at most 32 between them. Drawing has a new public field, palette : code that builds one with every field named needs it. Outside a drawing, a Paint hue of 3 or more is hue 0. El::map maps an element's children in a plain loop rather than collecting them in place, which is built once for every pair of message types: with grain in a region, labels shown while clear, keyed elements, drawings that ride and their own colours, the website's full module is 4,605 bytes larger gzipped than before them (2,826,385 to 2,830,990).

El::show_clear(inset, rank) : a label shown only while it is clear, checked every frame against its view ( El::view_scale , or the window) and the labels of lower rank, coming back with 4 px more to spare and fading linearly over 150 ms; hidden, it takes no pointer and is still read (DESIGN.md §1.2 ). A view of more than 64 is reported ( ViewProblem::ShowClearMany ). Cmd::Flow : an element keyed the same on both pages of a picture that grows goes from its old place to its new one with the picture instead of fading out and in, its size on the picture's cubic (DESIGN.md §1.10 ). Own-size type at another size on the new page is reported ( ViewProblem::FlowOwnSize ) and cross-fades once the picture lands. A picture with the same flow id whose box changed now grows. Cmd::Flow : a drawing's marks that ride on a growing or shrinking picture go with the picture's transform, their pen kept, instead of at their own size by parts, so a drawing shrinks into the window with its picture; under a view scale everything that rides does, own-size labels apart. ViewProblem has two new variants, and Props a new field, show_clear .

El::grain() : once an element is marked, the look's grain is drawn only over what marked elements draw (their box, following a flowing picture), the same grain as over the whole frame; with none marked it covers the frame as before (DESIGN.md §1.21 ). Post has a new field, region , which the runtime sets.

El 's fields that do not depend on its message type are in El::props ( Props ), which an El reads and writes as its own fields ( el.style , el.key , e.children are as before). El::map , El::zoom and El::new move them as one, and each leaf is measured outside the generic code, so an application that embeds others' views builds less per message type: the website's full module is 13,937 bytes smaller gzipped (2,840,450 to 2,826,513). Code that builds or takes apart an El by naming all its fields names props instead. Web: a canvas resized by its stage is drawn again at its new size in the same refresh, so a route that changes the stage's size shows no empty refresh ( web/amenui.js ).

El::view_scale(s) : what a container holds is scaled by s except the pen: line, border and trace widths and a trace's dashes stay as at 1, own-size labels keep their size, and a dot is never less than one whole device pixel (DESIGN.md §1.2 ). El::zoom is unchanged. El has two new public fields, pen and view_scale : code that builds one with every field named needs them.

El::own_size(ax, ay) : an element that keeps its own size when it is zoomed ( El::zoom , El::fit ) or rides a growing picture ( Cmd::Flow ): its anchor point goes where the zoomed box would put it, on whole device pixels; in a row or column it takes its own room, and one that then overflows its parent is reported ( ViewProblem::OwnSizeOver , P1 in the audit). El::fit measures subtrees with one in two passes (DESIGN.md §1.2 ). Pixel faces are never drawn smaller at a higher device pixel ratio than at 1: at 2, 7 px of a 12 px face is two device px a face pixel, as at 1, not one (DESIGN.md §1.6.3 ). El has a new public field, own_size : code that builds one with every field named needs it.

Drawing::ramp(a, b, w, paint, mid, far) : a stroke whose colour and opacity go from paint at a to far at b , through an optional middle stop, still one instance. Over a picture the colours mix in OKLab; off one it keeps its first hue, and a ramp across hues there is reported ( ViewProblem::RampHue , P1 in the audit) (DESIGN.md §1.26 ). Mark::Line has two new fields, far and mid ( None for a plain line): code that builds one with every field named needs them.

Flow: what rides on a growing picture moves by whole parts (a word; strokes that touch, as a box of lines), so a box drawn as four lines stays one box at one size while the picture grows or shrinks (DESIGN.md §1.10 ). Ui::ambient_fps(30) on a 60 Hz display draws every second refresh: a paced frame is due within half a refresh of its time, and web/amenui.js wakes a refresh early for it (in Chrome it was 20 a second). Web: when the WebGPU device fails, the full build starts on WebGL2 before it reports device ; the canvas is given a WebGPU context only once a WebGPU device is there. Flow: cells that read a picture ( el::cells ) are not taken for the subtree's picture, so they are not drawn a second time as one that grows. What rides on a growing picture stays whole until it lands, and the new subtree's notes are there at once then: each note is drawn once every frame (DESIGN.md §1.10 ). Blade::lean_from and Blade::lean_full : the blade's colour (and its head's) goes to lean_paint from the one lean to the other on a smoothstep; both 0 (the default) keep the mix linear over max_lean , byte for byte ( Blade::mix , DESIGN.md §1.26 ). Code that builds a Blade with every field named needs the two new ones. The ink under text to read is held at looseness 0, not at legible_cap : a label reads on its ground's colour at rest (DESIGN.md §1.15 ). A filled control whose own fill is loosened keeps one island: its content's ink box grown by max(5, 0.36 × size) , rounded, within its outline at rest, with a hard edge. Text on others' ink keeps its glyph island, with the gaps inside a word held too. Scene has islands . Under scribblr such a control's fill becomes a thread round its outline, with the island whole at rest fill.

The webgl feature (on by default) carries the WebGL2 backend on the web. Without it a web build has only WebGPU, and a browser without WebGPU fails to start: Host::start returns app::web::StartError ( Adapter or Device ; it was a String ), the module's start_failure() export says which, and web/amenui.js calls opts.onFail(kind, message) . Drawing::blade(Blade) ( Mark::Blade ): a rooted stroke the field map bends from the flow at its root, worked out on the GPU every frame; its lean is its tip's tangent, its root leans 0.35 of that and it bends above its stiff part ( Blade::tangent , Blade::shape ), drawn in 10, 6 or 2 segments by its length; it keeps its length, tapers to half its width and can carry a head glyph on its tip, turned with it and going to lean_paint with the stroke; its own lean and the map's add, within ± max_lean (DESIGN.md §1.26 ). Mark has Blade , so exhaustive matches need the new arm. Cmd::Gust { gust, scope } ( fieldmap::Gust ): a band that crosses a scope with a wake behind it, worked out from the clock and laid over the map, never put into it: once it has passed, the map is as it was and nothing is asked for (DESIGN.md §1.29 ). Cmd has Gust . El::map_life(energy_life, flow_life) : what is put in the map within an element's box is back at rest after these lives, however much and however wide: nothing spreads there, and each node goes down the look's curve slowed to end at the life. A stir narrower than a cell is put in a cell wide. The warm-up goes on in idle time ( Renderer::warm_idle ; the web module's warm_idle , which web/amenui.js calls from requestIdleCallback ): a page that draws nothing after its first frame is still warm soon, and its pieces no longer land in the frames of the next input. A warm-up step no longer asks for a frame of its own. A page shell of its own calls warm_idle the same way, asking for the next idle callback whatever a call did (a pipeline compile that blocked, a call that threw or found the module busy) until warm() is empty. The field map's ink for creep is read again only for instances that changed since the last scene, and not for blades or what lies inside a box with lives of its own, where nothing creeps. Cmd::Flow grows a subtree with a picture on both pages: the picture is one, in a box and a visible part that go from the old to the new on whole pixels; the rest of the old subtree rides with it at its own size and fades, the rest of the new one and what is new outside the flows comes in once it has landed, and the old page's ground stays around it until then (DESIGN.md §1.10 ). The growing picture and its riders are drawn in the page pass over what dissolves, so the notes keep their colour and size and no other window is drawn over it; a frame along the window's edge fades under it; a picture that shrinks back takes the old page with it, the new page's ground around it from the first frame. A flier's clip goes from the old to the new one instead of covering both. Ui::ambient_fps(n) : frames for what moves by itself at most n a second; input and what it starts are not paced until a second after the last input.

Text and shapes drawn over a picture are their own colour there, blended with the picture by their coverage and opacity, in the page and in a layer (DESIGN.md §1.6.1 ). Before, their edges (or the whole text, in the page's own layer) were read as the picture's colours and showed red; a site no longer needs a layer of its own for ink over a picture. Text to read over a picture stays as it is while the picture loosens. el::cells(Cells, cols, rows) draws the picture under it as character marks at a pitch of its own (7 × 14 px by default) from a ramp the caller gives, each cell in its own colour mixed toward an ink: one instance and one draw, nothing laid out when it moves, nothing drawn while it is still (DESIGN.md §1.6.1 ). Content has Cells , so exhaustive matches need the new arm.

Breaking: FlowSpec has fade_ms and Look has overlay_keep and off , so struct literals of them need the new field or ..Default::default() ; Cmd has ClearFocus and ClearPlate , ViewProblem has FitShort , ClampAround , PlateOver and OnPlate , Off has ground , and FontError has Bad , so exhaustive matches need the new arms. Every element is now the box its absolutely placed children are pinned in (its padding box), not the window: a page that placed an absolute child against the window from inside a padded parent moves it. Lengths are laid out on a 1/64 px step, so a wrapping row in a box as wide as its content stays on one line. Text to read and controls hold the looseness under and around them to the legibility cap (DESIGN.md §1.15 ): a label on a loose shape reads as at rest. Sites no longer need a ground-coloured patch or band under labels. Each material meets the island in its own way: whole cells and an island that follows the glyphs in charr, dots that join it in dottr, separations that close up by whole dots in halftonr, no copies of the label in glitchr, a crisp fill in scribblr. An element that clips, clips inside its border. El::fit(Fit) zooms a subtree to fit its box in the same layout (pixel type is set smaller, the scale is kept; at min what overflows starts at the box's start, and only what is cut is reported); FitMode::Reflow lays it out at the box's width first, with its type at its own size, and zooms it down only if it still does not fit; El::clamp(lines) ends text in the face's own ellipsis (three full stops where the face's floats off the baseline), copies what it shows without it, and brings the rest in from the next frame when the clamp is taken away, keeping the ellipsis until the text after it has come, with Ui::clamped ; El::preview(true) draws sheets, menus and dialogs where they are written, without a layer (a skip link over what is beneath it and still where it is written in Tab order, a docked sheet inside the border); Ui::line_inks reads each line's box and ink; Ui::clear_focus and Cmd::ClearFocus take the focus off. Faces that come later ( §1.6.5 ): Ui::declare_face , text::with_declared , Ui::add_face , Ui::faces_wanted ; resources by name with Ui::add_asset , Ui::asset , Ui::assets_wanted . Text stands in until the face comes, then each line sweeps over in 240 ms; with a material each glyph comes apart a little as it changes (a heading up to 0.6). The web module carries only the three main faces; web/amenui.js takes opts.faces , opts.assets and opts.preload and fetches what is wanted. Plates ( §1.33 ): El::plate(Plate { fade_s }) keeps the ink a subtree draws, ageing it out over fade_s ; Cmd::ClearPlate { key } empties it. Ageing ink fades as its coverage, with no pattern; a new stroke makes new only the old ink under its own outline; an empty plate is not laid on; text to read inside a plate is reported. A decode held at a step draws once and then the page rests (it asked for frames for good before). Look::overlay_keep keeps the readout in its corner; the readout wraps to fit a window 390 px wide. With less motion a flow fades in place over FlowSpec::fade_ms (150 ms by default). With or without it, what is new on the page fades in over fade_ms , so a route change is never the new page drawn whole over the old one. Look::off turns each effect off (close, fronts and commits, flows, morphs, ripples, loosening, recompose, decode, material motion, bloom, the field's dots), each going straight to its end state and asking for no frames ( §1.34 ). A box whose last child was absolute no longer keeps the child's layout after it goes (it could panic in taffy).

Breaking: el::Point and el::Drag have t , when the event happened on the runtime's clock, so struct literals of them need it. experiment::Pointer::hear measures speed between the events' own times. Ui::coalesce (on in both hosts): pointer moves, wheels and ticks lay out and paint once a frame, before it is drawn ( Ui::settle , called by Renderer::draw ); every other input lays out what waits first. Eight moves in a frame cost one layout instead of eight. The words and lines of a text drawn by El::reveal_by are found once per text and width, not on every paint ( Counters::reveals ); each glyph's word is looked up in its own line. The renderer reuses the lists it compares frames with instead of copying the scene into new ones. Web: a panic in a call no longer leaves every later call failing with "already borrowed": the application goes on as the panic left it ( app::slot ). GPU errors are logged, not panics, and mesh vertices go in buffers of at most 256 KB ( render::MESH_CHUNK ).

Breaking: Cmd::Commit has a scope: Option<String> ( None is the old behaviour); MorphSpec is Clone , not Copy , and has from_last ; Look has overlay_at and overlay_inset , and Gaze has echo and echo_ms , so struct literals of them need the new fields or ..Default::default() . A drive file's commit without scope reads as before. Both hosts warm the renderer up a piece a frame within 6 ms ( Renderer::warm_frame , WARM_MS ): the first frame is the plain page. Ui::warm and Ui::on_warm say how far it is; the web export warm() gives [done, total] , and web/amenui.js sets aria-busy and calls opts.onWarm . A frame drawn while something moves owes one more, so a motion that ends between frames ends on the settled page; a host no longer needs to redraw by hand after one. An element that leaves with its page takes its field map and decode with it; one taken away alone decodes out with its own spec inside its clip. audit::off_palette counts colours no theme makes. Controls inside a subtree marked legible(false) keep their fill and label as at rest; a tab list's heads and rule are the control. El::pass lets the pointer through to what is under it; El::opacity fades a subtree as one (at 0 it takes no pointer); El::commit_scope keeps a commit inside one element's box. Ui::morph_from_last and MorphSpec::from_last fly an element's glyphs, each whole, from where they were drawn last frame to the new element's, across a route change, in every material. The readout goes in Look::overlay_at 's corner and moves on clockwise rather than cover text to read. The INK leader is dashed and routed round text to read; Gaze::echo keeps fading earlier INK boxes. With reduced motion, what comes and goes fades over 150 ms. Looks: the thread's clearances move its control points, so the curve stays smooth; a thin accent rule under charr is one unbroken row; the Crack's pieces start to leave at 0.28; a press's flash in plain keeps a filled control's label at 4.5:1.

Breaking: the six printing materials are named for what they do: dot → dottr , halftone → halftonr , ascii → charr , print → smudgr , lino → carvr , glitch → glitchr (the Material variants and their strings); plain , near and scribblr keep theirs. PicFx is Markr ( El::markr ), the finishing pass's Dither is Dithr ( post.dithr , DithrKind ), Cmd::Front / Cmd::FrontAt are Cmd::Ripplr / Cmd::RipplrAt , and El::ripple , El::ripple_scope and El::wipe are El::ripplr , El::ripplr_scope and El::wipr . No aliases: an old material name is refused and the error names the new one, and LookError gives the closest name for any other. Look recipes start with look:v2: ; a look:v1: recipe is refused with the renames listed. Material has a variant for added materials, so cast with Material::id() , not as . Materials as source ( §1.6.4 ): each material is src/materials/<name>.wgsl with its name and numbers in a header; amenui add material <name> copies one into a project, and Look::material_source(name, wgsl, params) adds one back under a name of its own (ids 9–15, Material::Custom ). Look::numbers(m) reads the numbers a material is drawn with. El::effect(Effect { material, response, scope }) puts a material, a response and a scope on a subtree in one line, and el::wrap_text turns plain text or Markdown into a page to read. The thread ( §1.30 ): one large lopsided knot and smaller ones ( knot_fall ), a few chords escaping ( escape ), long flat tails with a few gentle bends ( tail_turns ) at half the line's tone ( tail_tone ), all in strand::ThreadShape ; it no longer lingers between a half-drawn title and a thread when it draws back ( strand::shown ), and it passes behind pictures without changing colour. Sample sheets that check themselves ( amenui::sample , sheet --material <name> --loose … --arrival ). The audit finds text a material wears away at rest ( Eroded , P1 under 85 % of plain's ink); a clipped finding names the side, the distance and what cuts it. Annotation tags and INK readouts keep off text to read and off each other. near keeps a label in the ground's colour on a solid button whole. Text on a form fades its rim from edge 0.6 (range 0–0.8), and in form3d the pointer's light falls off smoothly. The warm-up ( §1.23 ): the material arrives on the page at rest, then over 120 ms ( ui::RAMP ) the page loosens to its caps and condenses, so the arrival no longer jumps. Every public item of strand , fieldmap , field , hit , audit , form and materials has a doc comment.

Glyph poses have a depth and a facing ( Pose::z , Pose::facing ; the defaults draw as before), and a text element's glyphs are drawn far to near. El::form(FormFx { back, edge, overlap, fog }) keeps text on a form legible: what faces away is left out, what is edge on fades, a glyph mostly covered by nearer ones is not drawn (measured on the true ink), the far side is dimmer ( §1.26 ). amenui::form : Form wraps a block of text onto a sphere, a surface function or a mesh seen by a mesh::Camera ( Form::pose_of ), and Form::hit finds the pointer on the surface. The recipe form3d . El::reveal_by(Reveal::Word | Line) : clips, poses and the window show words and lines whole. Hits follow what is drawn: Ui::glyph_at , Point::glyph and Point::z ; El::turn turns an element and its subtree, and it is pressed where it is drawn; MeshHit has point , normal , t and uv , and Mesh::ray casts a ray at a mesh. A button or link inside an element that drags (a scene with on_point ) takes its own press. The warm-up ( §1.23 ): Renderer::begin draws plain at once, Warmup::step / Renderer::warm_step make the rest a piece at a time, and the page condenses into its look when it is ready; Offscreen::try_warming . Ui::prepare , Ui::ready and Ui::readiness run an application's own work in the frames' spare time; the annotation layer reads READY . The audit ( §1.31 ): amenui::audit , drive::audit , render --audit (with --strict , a P0 or P1 fails): text cut off, contrast, glyphs over each other, text too small, a page that never settles. The annotation layer's INK kind draws the same measured ink box. What the audit found: Paint::DIM is 0.66 (it was 0.5, 3.2:1 on light); the light theme's accent is darker (5.6:1) and the selection tint 12 %; near keeps text's ink whole; the loading recipe no longer asks for a frame every tick.

amenui::app : the framework runs applications itself. app::native::run opens a winit window (feature window , on by default) with the system clipboard, the input method, touch, frames on demand, and --shot / --exit-after for checks under Xvfb. app::web::Host and the web_app! macro generate a wasm module's exports from an application's state and message types. The App trait is how a shell routes, reads the route, takes clipboard requests, and sets the look, the language and reduced motion; every method has a default. Native screen readers: app::access builds an AccessKit tree from the accessibility mirror for the window (UI Automation, NSAccessibility, AT-SPI) and turns Focus, Click, Increment and Decrement into the runtime's focus, activation and arrow keys. The mirror says more: El::expanded , El::description , El::live ( Role::Status is polite by default), El::invalid , El::required . The accordion, select and popover report expanded instead of checked . Fonts beyond the bundled ones: Face::fallback for faces tried after the bundled ones, and Face::system() for the system's installed fonts (feature system-fonts , on by default; the native window adds it). Text::missing_glyphs . The complex-scripts feature for Thai, Lao, Khmer and Burmese line breaking. Any language: Locale::Other(Tag) for any BCP 47 tag, falling back to English, with CLDR plural rules, right-to-left direction by language or script, and its own locale.name and locale.date . Arabic ships ( Locale::AR , assets/i18n/ar.txt ). Locale::ALL lists the three shipped locales; i18n::installed() lists the application's. Locale::name returns a String . Focus: El::tab_order (positive first, 0 in document order, negative out of Tab), El::skip_to and El::focus_shown , and the skip_link component. App::set_appearance ( Appearance { dark, high_contrast } ), App::files_hovering and App::files_dropped ( Dropped with a path natively, name and bytes on the web), from both shells. The native window draws with the bundled faces compiled in ( text::embedded ), so a shipped binary finds its fonts anywhere. WindowError::Font is gone. amenui add writes from the sources compiled into it ( sources::file , add::write replaces add::copy ), so an installed command works without the repository. Crate metadata for crates.io (description, keywords, categories, rust-version ); the package leaves out CI (8.7 MiB compressed, under the 10 MiB limit). The native window recovers from a lost GPU device: new device and renderer, setup again, the Ui untouched. native::run 's setup is now Fn . web/amenui.js , the amenui npm package: the page side of the web entry ( mount , stage , css ). offscreen::read_back : one frame drawn into a texture of a given format and read back. error::WindowError . CI: clippy for native and web, rustdoc, the tests on lavapipe, and the website's tests against each framework commit.

The site (the gallery shell and its pages, the skeleton demo, Body and the Lab, the site documentation, the web shell, the native window, and the sample, acceptance and timing tools) moved to amenui-dev/website ↗ , with its history. i18n::install : an application installs its own message catalogs, looked up before the framework's. The framework's catalogs keep only the components' own strings ( widget.* ). amenui::pictures : sample pictures computed in code (formerly in demo.rs ). amenui::sources : AGENTS.md , llms.txt , registry.json , CHANGELOG.md and every component's source, compiled into the library. text::ASSETS : where the fonts are on disk. drive::render_with takes an application's own pages; drive::open opens recipes only, and so does the render tool. The library is no longer a cdylib . The web entry point ( wasm-bindgen ), winit and arboard moved to the website repository with the native window.

Body is English only, whatever the interface language. Its language marking reads LANGUAGE EN / ZH , and pressing it changes the language of the rest of the gallery. The field map ( src/fieldmap.rs ): a coarse grid over the window whose nodes hold energy and a flow direction. It steps at a fixed 1/60 s, spreads, decays by lifetime, meanders ( meander ) and creeps along ink ( creep ), returns to exactly zero within a bounded time, and needs no frames at rest. Trails: an element with El::stirr stirs the map along the path it moved. Cmd::Stir stirs a point, an element or a stretch of a path. The floating box, the bottom sheet and the card stack trail by default; the preset sets how strongly (Normcore has none). Reading the map: in the G-buffer stage it is one more source of looseness (still bounded by the legibility cap and each element's response), and instances that can be pushed drift along its flow (pictures and 3D elements loosen in place). The dot material's ground dots and glitch 's ground read it; Ui::looseness uses the same value. An element that trails and has a ground fill is drawn on a layer above, so loose decoration it passes over does not show through it. The #stirr page, with twelve numbers as number controls; one more line in the F2 readout; check item 19 (the former item 19, effects, is now item 17), bench … map and craft <dir> stirr . The scribblr thread material ( src/strand.rs ). At rest it is byte-identical to plain . Loosened, the fill fades and the ink becomes one continuous thin line: it first follows the glyphs' true outlines, bridged into one stroke (clean outlined letters); looser, it drops vertices step by step and merges into long polylines across several glyphs that wander off. The one to three places with the most energy knot into large stars, one long tail enters from the scope's edge and another leaves through the opposite edge, and it writes itself back in reverse. Text to read and controls never turn into thread, fade or move. Eight numbers are in the material parameters ( reach 40, knot_r 48, tail 480, angular 0.9), and Look::hold_ms holds the thread's pose for a beat. Long paths with El::trace : a polyline drawn by progress, solid or dashed ( dash , gap , by arc length from the start), bent by the flow, stirring the map at its head. "Draw a line" on #stirr . The thread starts from the outline as the G-buffer stage drew it, plus the offset by which the map pushed the instance. Vertices are ranked by one Ramer–Douglas–Peucker pass, slide onto their chord and are then removed, so the line follows its chords and nothing jumps on the way back. Knots are long chords through a center. Tails are cut at the scope's edge and stop before text to read. strand::figure draws a tangle from a fixed seed as page content. The #material-scribblr page; check item 20, bench … strand , craft <dir> scribblr and tests/strand.rs . Letter spacing with El::tracking . Quiet type with El::whisper() : lowercase, 0.6 em tracking, in a serif (Source Serif 4 at its 8 pt optical size, Latin only, 82 KB, OFL). Three new readouts in the annotation layer: edge notes EDGE (a hairline, ticks and a pointer mark at the scope's right edge, with the scope size, the pointer position, the material and theme, the loosest element and the number of non-zero map nodes set vertically), a waveform OSC (the energy of one row of nodes as a one-device-pixel polyline) and a level bar LEVEL (the mean energy). The annotation layer honours instance transforms, used only to turn the edge notes by 90°. The exported tree gains field: { level, nonzero } . The tenth preset, Loose Thread: white thread on black (or paper white), one accent, scribblr , only edge notes and corner marks on hover; the map meanders, creeps along ink and lives two seconds (a title the pointer sweeps loosens past 0.8 and comes back within three seconds); the thread holds every other beat; a 700 ms transition loosens into thread and then draws the outline. Its style page is English only: a lowercase serif title, one picture, one sentence, three controls as one line of small type in the footer, and a drawn tangle at rest. The finishing pass gains black and white only ( binary : a black-and-white palette, no dither, line widths rounded; text, thread and annotations are thresholded by coverage rather than brightness, and pictures get a two-level ordered dither) and invert ( invert : 1 − colour at the end). Annotation corner marks sit 6 px outside the element's rect, off its own text. Fixed theme ids and style-page descriptions that had drifted after themes and styles were removed. check items 7.2 and 7.3 (edge notes, waveform, level bar, edge notes at 1080p) and 20.6 and 20.7 (black and white only, invert), three tests in tests/gaze.rs , the Loose Thread page in tests/i18n.rs , craft <dir> loose-thread and craft <dir> thread-ref .

Sampling follows transforms: morph::cover_at maps points back through each instance's own transform, and cells and ink_bounds use the turned bounding box, so a posed or turned glyph loosens from where it is drawn, and masks and decode work there too. Hover and focus corner marks land on their target in the frame the pointer arrives (they used to chase it every frame and trail behind), with only a 70 ms close-in and fade. The lens touches only pictures and 3D elements that may loosen and that the pointer is not operating, added per instance in the G-buffer stage as fronts are. Looseness belongs to the instance's own ink (its ink wins over another's distance band) and no longer spills onto neighbouring decoration. Dragging, throwing and settling the floating box joined check 's partial-redraw comparison (every material, two at 2× scale). Decode counts coverage of the outline, not colour, so a dialog filled with the ground colour is covered too at the finest level. DESIGN.md no longer mentions the removed chrome, liquid and collage materials. The Lab: each stage takes over 70% of its cell and the piece fills it, the formula is one line and the numbers fold into [ params ] . Cells that can be seen keep running and stop when scrolled away (they rest with reduced motion). Every cell was redone to fill its stage, with the blue under the pointer; decode's exploded view became planes seen at an angle, each with a leader and a label. Removed the film (the prologue and chapters, the slate, the timeline, before-and-after, each chapter's caption), the xray material and its preset (Transparent Electronics), and the tests, checks, docs and strings that existed only for them. The exploded scene no longer uses xray. Body ( #body ) is the new full-bleed landing page. A page of readable text appears, then gathers into a slowly turning, luminous body made of its own glyphs (the skin, glyph count conserved) and more than ten thousand volume marks, with a key light, rim light, fog, bloom, a reflection and halo on the ground, three layers of dust, parallax and a breathing lens. Small markings in the picture (form, seed, gather / release, language, Lab, components); an opening at the pointer shows the original text. Bloom samples at a per-pixel noise angle, so text no longer shows ghost copies. Pose::hue gives one glyph an accent colour.

Per-instance transforms ( Instance::xf : turn, scale and shear about the instance's own center) and glyph poses ( El::pose ), so text can follow a path, wrap a sphere and be lit while its outlines stay true. Drawings ( el::canvas(Drawing) : dots and strokes are shapes with true outlines) and El::on_point (move, press-drag and leave in one handler, in the canvas's coordinates). Fields ( amenui::field ): noise, bumps, metaballs, curl, grids, marching-squares contours, vector flows, advected swarms and masked Gray–Scott. El::on_visible (run only while seen) and El::on_outline (an element's true outline handed to the state as a mask). The frame budget ( amenui::budget ): morph tiles, shed marks, flow fields, swarms and drawing marks all draw from one budget, which shrinks when a frame runs over and recovers when there is room; the readout shows it. The Lab ( #lab ): ten experiments (lit text, contours, silk, grown shapes, mercury, text on a path, text on a sphere, orbits, a spring, the card stack), one example file each, each with its own page. The decode transition ( El::decode ): an element resolves from coarse to fine over its true outline and disappears by the same backwards; its documentation page has an exploded 3D view and a timeline. Removed the chrome, liquid and collage materials, the Neo-Y2K and Mixed media presets, and film chapters 11 and 12 (with the finale).

Gesture physics ( amenui::gesture ): an analytically stepped spring with velocity hand-off on release, a rubber band, throw projection and velocity tracking. A bottom sheet (detents, dismissal by projection, rubber banding, a scrim, hand-off from scrolling) and a floating box (the corner picked by projection). The formula caption: a line under a demo that prints its real parameters, each editable. el::layers : children stacked in one box. English text around obstacles: Liang hyphenation (en-US) and up to 0.08 em of letter spacing; pieces that are not justified fall below 15%. A dot chart: a dot's size and brightness are the area under the curve, a sweeping line, draggable control points. The zine chapter's toner halved and kept off the text ( Shed.clear ), with a one-line caption. A fanning card stack: angle0 × falloff^n, delay_ms × n, three looks that follow the material. Skeletons: El::skeleton() draws the real tree as a skeleton (bars are measured line widths), the two Loading numbers, zero layout shift, and a comparison of four ways to load. Nested menus: a safe-zone triangle, two delays, the keyboard, and a triangle that can be drawn ( El::on_move , El::guide ).

The film's prologue: one small interface, as it is on the left and in a material on the right, with a draggable divider and a row of material names. No slogans: a chapter's title is one element that recomposes glyph by glyph across cuts; chapters 9, 10 and 11 redone. Guidance in the bottom bar: previous and next chapter, autoplay progress, hints shown only until the first input, bracket hints, invisible edges. Text around obstacles follows the true distance, leaves no slivers and does not hop while dragged; body text never condenses glyph by glyph; nothing is cut off at 330 px wide. The F2 readout: one line or every number, with a sparkline, and no frames at rest. look:v1: recipes (in a URL or a PNG text chunk); eight new mark sets grouped by family; five Geist Pixel faces; the <amenui-view> custom element.

Slow scrolling moves a picture by whole pixels; fast scrolling leaves each material's own trace ( §1.8.3 , check item 18). The film's third actor is a flat sign; chapter 13 is a real 3D mechanism (gears, a cam, a follower). Message catalogs, t! , plurals, a fallback chain and right-to-left rows ( §1.20 ). Eighteen new components, amenui add , and a documentation site laid out after shadcn/ui.
Bounded recomposition, particles emitted from mesh surfaces, local clocks, and the twelve-chapter film.
Drawing only when something changed, the frame-time readout, text input, incremental layout and long lists, touch, and the accessibility mirror.
The element tree, taffy, parley, scrolling, clicks, focus and the number control.
Two-stage drawing, waves that follow outlines, and one codebase for native and web.

The landing page ( #body ). A passage of text is first a page you can read; then it gathers itself into a slowly turning, luminous body made of its own glyphs, and goes back to being readable text. The code is examples/body.rs , written only against the public API; the page is the scene alone, full-bleed, with no chrome.

The page, every glyph exactly where the layout put it (the text is not posed at all), and the body, turning slowly while the camera breathes. A spring carries gather between them; a click, Space or Enter, or the gather / release marking toggles.

The passage's glyphs are the body's bright skin and their count is conserved: glyph i of n travels between its place on the page and point i of a spiral on the surface, turned to the spiral's tangent, squeezed by its slope, larger in front. The volume is a second population of some eleven thousand small marks from the frame budget, on the far shell and inside, born while it gathers and gone when it releases. The form is a signed-distance field: rock is a sphere with large relief and a few flat facets, cloud a smooth union of lobes; the seed places them. One key light from the upper left: the lit side white-hot, the middle in the form's hue, the far side its deep shade, a rim on the silhouette, depth fog, the finishing pass's bloom and a vignette. Rock is bone-white, ember and deep violet; cloud pale cyan, cyan and indigo. Beneath it, a pool of reflected marks and a faint spill of light; dust drifts at three depths with parallax; the whole picture follows the pointer a little. Drag to turn it (it coasts back to its idle turn). Near the pointer the glyphs snap back to their places on the page, so the words can be read through a clean opening. The controls are small markings in the picture with leader lines to the silhouette: form, seed, gather / release, the language, and the way to the Lab and the components.
Perform an action.

Components are distributed as source. Copy it and what it depends on into your project, then change it as you need: cargo run --release --bin amenui -- add button --to ../my-app Files copied: src/widgets/button.rs , src/widgets/mod.rs
use amenui::widgets::{button, button_as}; fn view() -> El<Msg> { button_as( "b1" , "Save" , Variant::Default, Msg::Nothing) }
fn view() -> El<Msg> { button_as( "b2" , "Cancel" , Variant::Quiet, Msg::Nothing) }
fn view() -> El<Msg> { button_as( "b3" , "Publish" , Variant::Accent, Msg::Nothing) }

Every number is a number control under the cell (type, arrow keys, drag sideways); none is a slider. name default range what it is L0 0.16 0.05–1 tone at rest r 54 px 8–160 the light's radius ω 0.35 rad/s 0–2 speed of the idle path

The text is one block of small monospaced type. El::pose asks each glyph's pose from its centre, and the pose returns only a tone: the glyph's colour is multiplied by L(d) , while its outline and position are untouched. That is why the dim text is still readable letters, not dissolved ones. The light follows the pointer on a spring. When nobody is there, it wanders over the text in a slow figure of eight at speed ω . Where the pointer holds the light, the brightest part of the beam takes the accent. L0 is the tone everything falls back to; at 1 the light has no effect. The code is examples/lab/lumen.rs .

f(x, y) = n(x/s, y/s, t) + a · e^(−|p − m|²/r²)

Every number is a number control under the cell (type, arrow keys, drag sideways); none is a slider. name default range what it is s 52 px 12–120 noise feature size a 0.70 0–2 bump height r 30 px 6–90 bump radius n 9 2–16 number of levels

The field is the sum of two parts: field::Noise , which drifts slowly with time, and field::Bump , a Gaussian under the pointer whose height fades in and out as the pointer arrives and leaves. field::Grid::sample samples it at every node; Grid::contours runs marching squares at each of the n levels and joins the segments into polylines, and Drawing::contours turns them into strokes. Where the bump bends a line, the line takes the accent, so the pointer's effect stays visible against the drifting noise. A small s gives tight, busy lines; a large one gives a few broad ones. The code is examples/lab/contours.rs .

Many marks carried by the curl of drifting noise (a flow without sources, so they never bunch), plus a flow grid the pointer's velocity is stirred into and that fades back. Each mark is drawn as the stroke it travelled. The count is a request to the frame budget.

The distance field: each chip is a rounded box with a signed distance, and the outline is their smooth union. Drag a chip near another and the two outlines neck together, with the gap printed between them; let go inside join and they are one group, one outline with the labels side by side, moved as one. Pull a member away fast and it tears off. A press without a drag turns a chip on.

Keys on a focused chip: arrows move it 8 px, Enter joins it to the nearest chip within join , Backspace takes it out of its group, Space turns it on.

The union is sampled on a 2 px grid over the chips' bounds ( field::Grid::sample ) and traced by marching squares at 0, 6 and 12 px ( Grid::contours ). The chips are elements: their fills, their labels (selectable text) and their group, which is an element of its own in the tree. Nothing moves but what the hand moves and the spring that takes a chip to its place, so the piece draws no frame at rest. The code is examples/lab/weld.rs .
