El::pose gives each glyph a vertical offset dy and an angle : the glyph's instance carries its own transform ( Instance::xf ), so it is drawn turned with its true outline, not as a rotated picture. The angle is the arctangent of the curve's slope at the glyph's centre. Four lines spread down the stage, each riding the wave a little behind the one above. Near the pointer, the nearest line's baseline is pulled toward it with a Gaussian of width σ , and the pulled glyphs take the accent. An A of 0 flattens the wave and leaves only the pull. The code is examples/lab/flow.rs .

A magnifier over a real page. This piece's own source is set in columns at 2.75 px, too small to read: a grey texture. Under the glass the same text is set again at reading size from its outlines, hard-edged. On the rim, in the accent, the zoom and the line and column under the glass's centre. Move to read. [ coverage ] shows how the renderer sees the page, each pixel's coverage as a grey, with the pixel grid at ×8 and above; [ distance ] draws bands of the distance field from the glyphs' ink every 2 px. A press pins the glass and the text in it selects and copies; a second press frees it. Drag the rim to resize; [ and ] change the zoom.
shown: the page within radius / zoom px of the glass's centre size: zoom × 2.75 px (11, 22 or 33 px: whole multiples of the face) rim: ×zoom · LINE l · COL c, (l, c) the character under the centre

name default range what it is zoom 8 × 4, 8, 12 how many times larger the glass sets the text radius the lesser of 132 px and 30 % of the stage's width 64–240 px on a stage under 480 px wide, else 80–240 the glass's radius columns 8 4–10 columns of the page [ ink ] , [ coverage ] and [ distance ] choose what the glass shows; [ grid ] shows and hides the pixel grid in coverage .

The page is laid out and drawn once and kept ( El::cached ); coverage shows part of what was kept, enlarged ( el::cached_view ). The glass holds a fixed set of line slots, as many as its height and width need at this zoom and radius: each holds one row of the page, padded with spaces to the column's width, and the glyphs outside the circle are left out by their poses ( El::pose ). A moving glass moves its slots and changes a slot's text only when the row under it changes, so nothing is laid out again; the glass and its rim are made again by themselves, and the kept page is not drawn again ( El::local_messages ). Pinned, the glass holds exactly the text it shows, so a selection copies it with no padding. The distance bands come from the glyphs' outlines ( pair::Faces ): their ink on a 4 px grid, its distance transform, and the transform's contours. The code is examples/lab/loupe.rs .

The distance field between two letters: one word whose letters are bodies on springs, and each spring's rest length is measured between the letters' outlines, not their boxes. Under each pair is the smallest distance between the two outlines; above it, the white area between them. The tightest pair is in the accent. Drag a letter along the baseline: its neighbours keep the rule and are pushed along, touching but never overlapping, and no letter leaves the stage; let go and they spring back.

metric: x_i = the shaper's pen (the face's advances, kerning included) gap: x_i = x_(i−1) + min dx : d(A, B + dx) ≥ target, d(A, B) = min |p − q|, p ∈ A, q ∈ B area: x_i = x_(i−1) + dx : white(A, B + dx) = W (W the pairs' mean in metric)

name default range what it is target 8 px 0–40 in gap , how far apart every pair is at its closest; the slider stops at the largest value that keeps the word 16 px inside each edge of the stage, and the panel prints it size 176 px 44–220 the most the word is drawn at; the drawn size is the largest whole px under it at which the word, in metric , is at most 80 % of the stage stiffness 600 100–900 the springs damping 44 10–60 the springs [ metric ] , [ gap ] and [ area ] choose the rule, and the letters move to it on their springs. [ dims ] shows and hides the measures. The field under the word changes it: up to 10 characters, as many as fit the stage at 44 px.

The word is set in the site's sans, Noto Sans SC, where the three rules give three different settings: metric is where the shaper puts each letter, kerning included, as the layout tells the word's pose ( GlyphAt::pen ); gap and area then respace those pens by the outlines. A pixel monospace would not show this, since every letter reaches the same columns of its cell and every pair's gap comes out equal. Each letter's ink comes from the page's faces ( Ui::on_faces , pair::Faces ); the distance between two outlines and the white between them are pair::gap and pair::area , measured every frame a letter moves, and the spacing a rule asks for is found once by pair::spaced and pair::spaced_area . The word is one text, so it selects and copies as a word: each glyph is moved from where the layout set it to its letter's place ( El::pose ). The code is examples/lab/kern.rs .
A mass on a spring, the same gesture::Spring the sheets use, solved exactly. Drag it along its track; let go and it springs back with the speed it was thrown at, its last two seconds traced beneath.
Every number is a number control under the cell (type, arrow keys, drag sideways); none is a slider. name default range what it is k 180 10–1200 stiffness c 6 0–80 damping m 1 kg 0.2–5 mass

gesture::Animated::hold makes the mass follow the finger while it is pressed, and a velocity tracker measures how fast it was moving. On release, to(x₀, v, now) hands that speed to the spring, so a throw keeps its momentum instead of stopping dead. The spring is solved exactly at each frame, not stepped, so it is the same at any frame rate. The formula line shows the damping ratio ζ as it changes: below 1 the mass overshoots and rings, at 1 it returns as fast as it can without overshooting, above 1 it creeps back. The trace under the track is the last two seconds of position. The code is examples/lab/spring.rs .
The card stack ( widgets::card_stack ) in the lab's look: hover or press a card and the ones beneath fan out.
angle(n) = angle0 × falloff^n, delay(n) = delay × n

Every number is a number control under the cell (type, arrow keys, drag sideways); none is a slider. name default range what it is angle0 42° 0–90 first card's turn falloff 0.70 0.1–1 each next one's share delay 28 ms 0–200 stagger

Each card has its own spring with velocity hand-off (DESIGN.md §1.24 ): when the pointer moves to another card before the fan has settled, the springs keep the speed they had and turn toward the new target instead of starting again from rest. Card n starts delay × n after the first, so the fan opens from the top card down and closes the same way. The cards are drawn in the lab's look, near the ground with a hairline outline; the card under the pointer takes the accent. Turning falloff to 1 gives every card the same angle, and a delay of 0 moves them all at once. The code is examples/lab/stack.rs .

W-01 in Works, at noon (12:00). A straw field seen from standing height, side on, flat to a level horizon under a pale sky with one thin high cloud. On the horizon a mast carries an orange windsock and a note: the wind, and how long until the next gust. The sock hangs at rest and lifts while a gust passes the mast, level in a strong one. The field is 1,570 stalks in 15 rows at 1440 × 900 (392 on a phone); the far rows are ticks, the near ones are taller than the title, and the stalks in the nearer half carry a head that is a glyph from ' " ; : ! i l , . Each stalk has a length of its own and leans a little downwind at rest. No stalk stands within 24 px of the title, its number or the small line, and no head within 8 px of the links at the foot, the status line or the note at the mast. On a phone the 24 px hold for the title and its number only: the small line's two lines keep heads 8 px away, and a stalk whose head would come nearer than that is planted without it. Wind comes as gusts with stillness between them. A gust is a band that crosses the field from left to right, the near rows behind the far ones, so the band runs diagonally; inside it the stalks lean and show their pale side, and behind it they sway back through upright once. Every fourth gust is strong. The pointer walks through the field: the stalks near where it has been lie down away from it and take 6 seconds to stand up again, the far end of the path first.

Part amenui The sky, the cloud and the ground one picture computed in code at start-up (960 × 600, the horizon at 64 % of its height, 62 % on a phone), shown with El::picture at pitch 1. The ground has long streaks: value noise of four octaves, ± 18 of 255, its period (30 + 300 d) px wide and (3 + 22 d) px high at depth d The stalks one Drawing of Mark::Blade s: each rooted on its row, 5 + 24 · t^1.4 px apart at depth t with one in six left out, its row's length × (0.80 + 0.35 h) long and leaning 0.06 ± 0.06 rad at rest ( lean , which the map's lean adds to), width 0.75 at the far row to 1.5 at the near one, max_lean 72°. Upright it is #7b6a2c , mixed 55 % toward the ground in the far rows; leaning it turns toward #fff6c8 at full strength at every depth, the pale side: not at all up to 8° of lean, wholly from 20°, a smoothstep between ( lean_from , lean_full ), so a stalk at its own lean or swaying back is its upright colour. A head is the blade's Head , a glyph of Departure Mono on its tip in #5d4f1e The gusts Cmd::Gust : a band 330 px wide at 240 px a second, its far side 500 px ahead of its near side along the depth's 0.53th power (on a phone 40 % and 45 % of the window's width at most: 156 and 175 px at 390), strength 0.79 (57°), 1.0 for a strong one (72°), with its wake behind it The path Cmd::Stir at the pointer, each side's flow away from it, over 10 + 60 · t px at depth t, each with three times the look's flow; El::map_life(8, 8) on the field, so 3 seconds after the pointer the stalks on its path still lean about 20° and show their pale side, by 6 seconds they are under 8° and upright in colour, and at 8 they are at rest. A pointer that moves more than 320 px in one event starts the path again where it lands, with nothing stirred between The windsock its own small drawing, 22 px long, 8 px wide at the mast and 4 at its tip; 55° below the horizontal at rest, lifted to 55° · (1 − f) by the gust's value f at the mast's foot, on the frames the gust draws anyway The windsock's note two labels and a leader; the countdown changes in place without a layout ( recompose(false) ) The blades are bent on the GPU from the field map at their roots: while only the wind moves, nothing is laid out, painted or built on the CPU. A gust is never put into the map; it is worked out from the map's clock and laid over it, so once it has passed, the map is exactly as it was and no frame is asked for. What the pointer stirs goes into the map with a layout, at most 30 times a second. The map reads the scene's ink for creep only where an instance changed, and never for the blades or anything inside the field's own life, where nothing creeps.

What moves by itself is paced at 30 frames a second ( Ui::ambient_fps ), input is not. Between gusts the only frames are the countdown's, one a second. After 60 seconds without input the gust under way ends and the piece rests until the next input. With reduced motion it is still: one gust band held with its centre 72 % across the far row, from the mast down to the foot, and the sock lifted as at the band's peak, 55° · (1 − 0.79), about 11.5° below the horizontal. Measured at 1440 × 900 and 2× in headless Chrome on SwiftShader, a software renderer (not a GPU), so a real machine does better: A frame Mean 95th percentile Worst The field at rest and in gusts 3.3 ms 7.7 ms 15.3 ms The pointer walking 4.6 ms 9.4 ms 13.6 ms Counting only the frames a gust draws, the mean is 2.35 ms and the 95th percentile 5.1 ms. The first frame, which lays out and paints the page, takes 89.5 ms. A pointer that jumps more than 320 px in one event stirs nothing between, so a jump costs no more than a step. Natively a frame during a gust takes 1.1 ms of CPU, a pointer event 2.4 ms (a layout every other event), and a jump of 800 px 2.1 ms. The piece opens with its first gust already 72 % across, so its first minute at rest draws about 1,100 frames: about 160 in the first 5.5 seconds as that gust finishes, then 30 a second during each crossing of about 10 seconds and one a second between. A frame holds 6,348 instances at 1440 × 900 and 1,482 at 390 × 844, every blade and head counted; when frames are slow the drawing is thinned evenly. The code is src/gallery/touch.rs in the website repository. The field map is described in Ripples .

W-03 in Works, at dusk (18:40). Five ridges stand one behind another under a low sun, and a survey is laid over them: a dashed level line at the sun's height, spot heights on three real summits, and boxes around whatever moves. Every 40 seconds a flight of seven birds crosses from right to left in 16 seconds, each bird boxed and trailing three fading echoes. A small pale cloud wears a fainter box labelled BIRD 0.03 : the one wrong call. The pointer gets surveyed too. A scan window 300 × 190 px follows it, and inside the window the same hills are drawn as characters, the way the system sees them. The pointer's own box is labelled HUMAN? , and the score rises while the pointer moves the way a hand does.

Part amenui The hills, sky and sun one picture computed in code at start-up (960 × 600, value noise per ridge, mixed toward the sky with distance), shown with El::picture at pitch 1 The survey, birds and boxes one Drawing per frame: dashes, leaders and four-stroke rectangles on the pixel grid, with labels as small text elements placed absolutely The scan window 14 rows of cells, each row one line of Departure Mono with its characters set a cell apart by tracking; El::pose gives every glyph its own cell's colour, mixed 0.62 toward the survey ink The pointer's box a second Drawing and a label with recompose(false) , so the number changes in place without a layout Each cell takes a character from the ramp . : - = + * # by the luminance of the picture under it. There are no blank cells: the lightest two eighths are both . . The characters are worked out again only when the window moves, the pointer's box moves, or the ground changes, and between those times the rows keep their layout ( recompose(false) ). The cells under the pointer's box and its label are left empty. The title and the number are drawn at full strength in every state; only the small line, the strip and the status line fade. A test holds every character's darkest pixel to at least 3 : 1 against the median of its cell. Everything drawn over the picture sits in a layer of its own. Its ink replaces the picture's, so the survey is never mixed into the colours of the hills.

Between flights the piece asks for no frame at all, and the flight itself is paced at 30 frames a second. The scan window follows the pointer on a 120 ms spring, and only while the pointer moves. After 60 seconds without input, the flight under way ends and the piece rests until the next input. With reduced motion it is still: the birds stay halfway across, boxed, without echoes. Measured at 1440 × 900 and 2× in headless Chrome on SwiftShader, a software renderer (not a GPU), so a real machine does better: A frame during a flight Mean 95th percentile Worst The scan window still 2.17 ms 2.9 ms 3.3 ms The pointer moving 2.31 ms 4.1 ms 8.9 ms Layout takes 0.6 to 0.9 ms of a frame during a flight (measured natively). At rest the piece draws 82 frames a minute, all of them during flights and none between. A frame holds 760 instances at 1440 × 900 and 412 at 390 × 844. To a screen reader the scan window's characters are one picture, named by its label. The code is src/gallery/works.rs in the website repository. The annotation layer that the site's other pages use for frames and callouts is described in Annotation .

W-04 in Works, at night (23:10). Flat dark water under a starry sky. Across the sky runs one line of type on a slow curve: the build's log, nightly ok ok ok build 0412 ok passing … . An aurora hangs from the line, 540 rays rising from it, tall in the folds and short in the gaps. On the horizon a small orange light carries a callout, KP 5 STEP 3/7 . The curve drifts and the rays' lengths travel slowly along it. Moving the pointer near a fold leans it toward the pointer. A press runs the next step of the build: a pulse travels both ways along the line from the nearest point, and the rays it reaches brighten and lengthen for half a second. After step 7 the whole curtain flares, the callout says PASSING , the build number rises by one, and a new curtain comes in. Under the horizon the curtain's broken reflection shifts once with every press.

Each ramps from #baffd8 at its root through #2fae8c at 30 % of its length to transparent at its tip, mixed in OKLab over the picture under it. The drift is paced at 30 frames a second ( Ui::ambient_fps ) while the piece is awake; a pulse, a flare and the fold's spring ask for frames of their own only while they run. After 60 seconds without input the piece rests. With reduced motion the curtain is still: a press counts the step and shifts the reflection, with no pulse and no flare, and the fold takes its lean at once.
